signals.title: [Bug]: PUT /v1/mcp/server silently nulls authorization_url, token_url, oauth2_flow when delegate_auth_to_upstream=true
signals.text: ### What happened? When an MCP server is configured with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`, any subsequent update via `PUT /v1/mcp/server` silently discards `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow` — even when those exact fields are explicitly present with non-null values in the request body. The response (and the persisted record, confirmed via a follow-up `GET /v1/mcp/server`) always comes back with these three fields set to `null`. This breaks the Admin UI's own "Authorize & Fetch Token" convenience button (used to fetch a test token for a server's Tools tab), since that feature depends on `authorization_url`/`token_url` being present. It fails with: \`\`\` {"detail":"MCP server authorization url is not configured. OAuth endpoint discovery against the configured server url did not resolve it; the url may be misconfigured. Check the proxy logs for 'MCP OAuth' warnings from server load, verify the server url, or set Authorization URL and Token URL manually, or set Issuer to discover them from the identity provider (RFC 8414)."} \`\`\` Setting `issuer` instead (for RFC 8414 discovery) does not help either — discovery does not appear to run on-demand, and `authorization_url`/`token_url` remain `null` regardless. Importantly, this only affects the UI test button. The actual delegated/passthrough OAuth flow works correctly for real traffic: a client that authenticates against the upstream IdP directly and passes its own bearer token via `x-mcp-<server_name>-authorization`, alongside a valid LiteLLM virtual key in `Authorization`, successfully reaches the upstream MCP server and receives a real tool list. So the runtime behavior of `delegate_auth_to_upstream` is sound — only the persisted config for `authorization_url`/`token_url`/`oauth2_flow` is being wiped on save. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create/register an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`. 2. Send a `PUT /v1/mcp/server` with the full server object, explicitly including `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow: "authorization_code"` (and `issuer` cleared to `""`): \`\`\`bash curl -X PUT 'https://your-litellm-proxy.example.com/v1/mcp/server' \ -H 'authorization: Bearer <admin-key>' \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "server_id": "<server_id>", "server_name": "example_mcp_server", "url": "https://your-mcp-server.example.com/mcp", "transport": "http", "auth_type": "oauth2", "oauth2_flow": "authorization_code", "issuer": "", "authorization_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/auth", "token_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/token", "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true, "oauth_passthrough": false, "dcr_bridge": false }' \`\`\` 3. Inspect the response, or immediately follow up with `GET /v1/mcp/server` and find the same `server_id`. ### Expected behavior `authorization_url` and `token_url` should be persisted exactly as submitted, and `oauth2_flow` should remain `"authorization_code"`. ### Actual behavior The response (and subsequent GET) shows: \`\`\`json { "issuer": "", "authorization_url": null, "token_url": null, "oauth2_flow": null, "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true } \`\`\` All three fields are nulled despite being explicitly sent as non-null in the request. ### Relevant log output N/A on our end — we don't have access to the proxy's server-side logs in this deployment, only client-observable request/response pairs (above). ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Auth-stage failure spend logs (budget_exceeded) drop x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata even though the header is present
signals.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` is documented to attach caller metadata to spend logs, and it works for successful calls and for post-auth failures (invalid model name, unsupported params, blocked model — all keep the metadata). But when a request is rejected during **auth** — most importantly `budget_exceeded` — the failure spend-log row is written with `"spend_logs_metadata": null`, even though the header is present on the rejected request. Mechanism (from reading the proxy source): the header is only consumed by `LiteLLMProxyRequestSetup.add_litellm_metadata_from_request_headers` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), which runs inside `add_litellm_data_to_request` **after** `user_api_key_auth` succeeds. Auth-stage exceptions (`BudgetExceededError`, invalid key, etc.) go through the auth failure logging path, which builds the failure `SpendLogsPayload` without ever consulting the request headers — so the caller's metadata is dropped for exactly those rows. Impact: deployments that put a gateway in front of the proxy tag every request with `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` (e.g. `{"my_request_id": "..."}`) to join the client-facing request id to spend-log rows. Budget rejections are the most common customer-visible failure in prepaid setups, and they are precisely the rows that lose the join key. The customer holds a request id from the response, but the corresponding spend-log row cannot be found by it. Reproduced on `v1.91.1` and `v1.97.0` (`litellm-database` images). Fully self-contained repro below (no provider key needed). ## Steps to Reproduce `config.yaml` (mock model, absurd per-token cost so one call exceeds any small budget): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: mock litellm_params: model: openai/mock api_key: mock mock_response: "ok" input_cost_per_token: 1.0 output_cost_per_token: 1.0 ``` Start the proxy: ```bash docker network create litellm-repro docker run -d --name litellm-repro-pg --network litellm-repro \ -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm -e POSTGRES_USER=litellm -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=litellm \ postgres:17-alpine docker run -d --name litellm-repro --network litellm-repro -p 127.0.0.1:14001:4000 \ -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:litellm@litellm-repro-pg:5432/litellm \ -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-repro-master -e LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-repro-salt \ -e STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True \ -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro" \ docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:v1.97.0 --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000 ``` Run the two-call sequence (identical header on both calls): ```bash BASE=http://127.0.0.1:14001 KEY=$(curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/key/generate" \ -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"key_alias":"budget-repro","models":["mock"],"max_budget":0.01}' | jq -r .key) # call 1: succeeds, accrues spend (~30 USD at 1.0/token) far above max_budget curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "call1=%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$BASE/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"my_request_id":"req_success_1"}' \ -d '{"model":"mock","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' sleep 20 # wait for the spend batch writer # call 2: rejected at auth with 429 budget_exceeded curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "call2=%{http_code}\n" -X POST "$BASE/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"my_request_id":"req_rejected_2"}' \ -d '{"model":"mock","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' sleep 15 # wait for the failure row curl -sS "$BASE/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-18%2000:00:00&end_date=2026-08-19%2000:00:00&page=1&page_size=10" \ -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master' | \ jq '.data[] | {request_id, status, spend, spend_logs_metadata: .metadata.spend_logs_metadata}' ``` Observed output (v1.97.0): ```json { "request_id": "6796b7ea-088d-4ade-8e82-cb7df540642d", "status": "failure", "spend": 0.0, "spend_logs_metadata": null } { "request_id": "chatcmpl-49bfbc9b-93f2-40d8-b836-bfc913386980", "status": "success", "spend": 30.0, "spend_logs_metadata": { "my_request_id": "req_success_1" } } ``` ## Expected behavior The `failure` row for the budget-rejected request should carry `"spend_logs_metadata": {"my_request_id": "req_rejected_2"}` — the header is on the request, and post-auth failure rows already preserve it. The auth failure logging path should parse `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` (same `safe_json_loads` treatment as `_get_spend_logs_metadata_from_request_headers`) before building the failure `SpendLogsPayload`. Related but distinct: #35068 covers post-call failures losing `call_type`/router metadata from the `litellm_metadata` bucket; this issue is about auth-stage failures never reaching the header-parsing step at all. ## LiteLLM version Reproduced on `docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:v1.91.1` and `:v1.97.0`.
signals.author: samzong

signals.title: [Bug]: provider_budget_config reports budget_reset_at ~57 years in the future without Redis
signals.text: ### What happened? With `provider_budget_config` and **no Redis configured**, `GET /provider/budgets` reports a `budget_reset_at` roughly 57 years in the future, so a monthly budget effectively never resets. Config: ```yaml router_settings: provider_budget_config: openrouter: budget_limit: 5 time_period: 30d ``` Response: ```json {"providers":{"openrouter":{"budget_limit":5.0,"time_period":"30d", "spend":4.8888e-06,"budget_reset_at":"2083-05-04T16:04:00.635943+00:00"}}} ``` Same result with `time_period: 1mo` (`2083-05-05T15:39:32`), so it is not specific to the period format. Today's date when this was captured: 2026-08-18. ### Root cause `async_get_ttl` means different things in the two cache backends, and `_get_current_provider_budget_reset_at` assumes the Redis meaning: - `RedisCache.async_get_ttl()` returns **remaining seconds** (Redis `TTL`). - `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl()` returns `self.ttl_dict.get(key)` — and `ttl_dict` stores an **absolute expiry timestamp**: `self.ttl_dict[key] = time.time() + float(kwargs["ttl"])` (`litellm/caching/in_memory_cache.py`). `litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py`: ```python if self.dual_cache.redis_cache: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.redis_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) else: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) if ttl_seconds is None: return None return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds)).isoformat() ``` Without Redis, `ttl_seconds` is an absolute unix timestamp (~1.79e9), so the result is `now + ~56.7 years` — which matches the observed 2083. The budget limit itself works; only the reported reset time (and therefore the reset window for in-memory deployments) is wrong. ### Suggested fix Either make `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` return remaining seconds like the Redis backend does, or convert at the call site: ```python ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds - time.time() # in-memory stores absolute expiry ``` The first option is preferable — `async_get_ttl` returning different units per backend is a trap for any other caller. ### Relevant log output ``` LiteLLM.LoggingError: [Non-Blocking] Exception occurred while success logging File ".../litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py", line 412, in async_log_success_event raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required") ValueError: custom_llm_provider is required ``` Separate but related observation while testing the same feature: every request through a `pass_through_endpoints` route raises the above in `budget_limiter.async_log_success_event`, so pass-through traffic is not counted toward provider budgets at all. Happy to file that separately if useful. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: Add Skills page to Internal Users page visibility settings
signals.text: ### Problem In the LiteLLM Admin UI, under **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**, admins can choose which pages an internal user can see (e.g., Models, Teams, Keys, Spend, etc.). However, the **Skills** page is missing from this list, so there is no way to hide it from internal users without disabling the entire Admin UI (`DISABLE_ADMIN_UI=true`) or removing the Anthropic provider configuration. ### Context - The **Skills** page is visible in the Admin UI, but there is no per-role/per-user visibility toggle in **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**. - For teams that do not want end users to access the Skills page, the only documented way to hide it is to disable the whole Admin UI. ### Request Add a **Skills** visibility toggle in **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**, so admins can show or hide the Skills page per user/role, just like the other UI sections. ### Possible implementation Expose a `ui_page_visible.skills` flag (or equivalent) in the UI visibility configuration and respect it when rendering the sidebar/routes. ### Alternatives considered - `DISABLE_ADMIN_UI=true`: disables the entire UI, not acceptable. ### Environment - LiteLLM version: latest stable - Deployment: self-hosted proxy with Admin UI

signals.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses omits required reasoning_tokens for Gemini responses without thoughts, breaking Codex clients
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? LiteLLM v1.97.0 emits an invalid OpenAI Responses API `response.completed` event when a Gemini response contains text tokens but no thinking tokens. For `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, a simple request with `reasoning.effort: "low"` can legitimately return no Gemini `thoughtsTokenCount`. LiteLLM still creates `usage.output_tokens_details` from the text-token count, but omits `reasoning_tokens`: ```json "output_tokens_details": { "text_tokens": 1 } ``` OpenAI's Responses schema requires `reasoning_tokens` inside `output_tokens_details`. Codex consequently terminates the stream with: ```text stream disconnected before completion: failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field `reasoning_tokens` ``` Expected: ```json "output_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 1 } ``` If the provider reports a real reasoning-token count, LiteLLM should preserve it. If the provider reports no thinking-token count, the Responses API serializer should emit `reasoning_tokens: 0`. This appears related to #31759 and #32837. PR #32837 intentionally omits `reasoning_tokens` when the provider value is absent, but that produces a response incompatible with the OpenAI Responses schema whenever other output-token details are present. References: - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31759 - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/32837 - https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_usage.py - https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs ### User Flow Before a hypothetical fix: a developer runs Codex through a LiteLLM Responses API endpoint backed by Gemini 3.7 Flash, and the completed response cannot be parsed. 1. The developer sends `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses` with model `gemini-3.7-flash`, streaming enabled, reasoning effort `low`, and a simple text prompt. 2. The live Gemini provider completes the request without using thinking tokens. 3. The developer receives a `response.completed` SSE event whose `usage.output_tokens_details` contains `text_tokens` but no `reasoning_tokens`. 4. Codex displays `failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field reasoning_tokens` and retries or aborts instead of completing the task. After a hypothetical fix: the same request completes successfully and remains schema-compatible when Gemini uses no thinking tokens. 1. The developer sends the same `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses` request with the same model and inputs. 2. The live Gemini provider completes the request without using thinking tokens. 3. The developer receives a `response.completed` SSE event whose `usage.output_tokens_details` contains both `text_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens: 0`. 4. Codex parses the completed response and finishes the task without retrying or aborting. ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: - LiteLLM Proxy v1.97.0 - model alias: `gemini-3.7-flash` - provider model: `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash` - no model-level `reasoning_effort` or thinking override - live Vertex AI provider call - authorization value redacted Command: ```bash curl --no-buffer https://<litellm-host>/v1/responses \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "model": "gemini-3.7-flash", "input": "Return exactly: ok", "max_output_tokens": 64, "reasoning": {"effort": "low"}, "stream": true }' ``` Relevant fields from the final SSE event: ```text data: { "type": "response.completed", "response": { "status": "completed", "model": "gemini-3.7-flash", "usage": { "input_tokens": 4, "input_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 4 }, "output_tokens": 1, "output_tokens_details": { "text_tokens": 1 }, "total_tokens": 5 } } } ``` Codex output: ```text stream disconnected before completion: failed to parse ResponseCompleted: missing field `reasoning_tokens` ``` Provider comparison from the same live proxy using Gemini `generateContent` with `thinkingLevel: LOW`: - `gemini-3.6-flash` returned `thoughtsTokenCount: 59`. - `gemini-3.7-flash` returned no `thoughtsTokenCount`, which is valid for a request where the model used no thinking tokens. The bug is the Responses API serialization of the absent provider count, not the absence itself. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: LangSmith tracing 400s with "trace_id does not match first part of dotted_order"
signals.text:
## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (#7140 is the closest but covers child-run `dotted_order` with a `parent_run_id`. This is a root-run `trace_id != run_id` mismatch, no parent involved.) ## What happened? With LangSmith tracing enabled in the proxy config, requests that carry a session/trace header have every run batch rejected by LangSmith with a 400. No trace for those requests lands in LangSmith. Plain requests without such a header land fine. Langfuse (enabled side by side) works throughout. Likely cause: `_ensure_required_ids` in `litellm/integrations/langsmith.py` mints a fresh `run_id` when the request has no `id`, but only defaults `trace_id` to `run_id` when `trace_id` is *also* missing. When a request carries one of the headers LiteLLM maps to `metadata["trace_id"]`, the proxy honors it while generating a new `run_id`. For a root run LangSmith requires `trace_id == run_id`, so the payload is rejected. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/ef84494d52c6708e4e9f4a54ce551a265995ad8f/litellm/integrations/langsmith.py#L170-L181 `metadata["trace_id"]` is derived from headers in `get_chain_id_from_headers` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), which accepts `x-litellm-trace-id`, `x-litellm-session-id`, and any `x--session-id` header whose value looks like a session id. That last rule is what makes this hit real users without them ever setting a `trace_id` - for example, Claude Code through ngrok sends a constant `x-claude-code-session-id` for the whole session, so every run in the session carries the same `trace_id` while each gets a fresh `run_id`. ## User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer who turns on LangSmith tracing in the proxy gets no traces in LangSmith for requests that carry a session id header. 1. They set the LangSmith API key and project in the proxy environment, enable LangSmith tracing in the proxy config, and start the proxy. 2. They send `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with a model name and a message, their client (e.g. Claude Code) attaching a session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200 with the completion content. 4. They open their LangSmith project. No trace appears for that request. 5. The proxy log shows LangSmith's API rejecting the run with a 400. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request produces a trace in LangSmith. 1. Same proxy config and LangSmith keys. 2. Same `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with the same model, message, and session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200. 4. A trace for that request appears in the LangSmith project, and the proxy log shows no 400. ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml # litellm-config.yaml (excerpt) litellm_settings: success_callback: ["langfuse", "langsmith"] ``` Env vars set on the proxy: `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`, `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL` (values redacted; `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL=https://apac.api.smith.langchain.com`). Version or commit: `v1.97.0` (image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`). The `_ensure_required_ids` logic is byte-identical in `v1.96.2`. Commands and their full output: All three LLM endpoints are affected. Each was sent with its own `x-litellm-trace-id` so the runs can be told apart, and each returned 200 to the caller before LangSmith rejected the run on the next batch flush.
POST /v1/chat/completions - command and 400 ```bash podman compose up -d curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 does not match first part of dotted_order a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 for run_id:a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 trace_id:3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 dotted_order:20260818T100130082650Za0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/messages - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a does not match first part of dotted_order 4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 for run_id:4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 trace_id:7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a dotted_order:20260818T102348430265Z4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/responses - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","input":"hi"}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 does not match first part of dotted_order 6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a for run_id:6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a trace_id:bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 dotted_order:20260818T102443557144Z6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a parent_run_id:"} ```
The same request without the `x-litellm-trace-id` header lands cleanly on every one of those endpoints. Shown here for `/v1/chat/completions`, verified against the LangSmith API:
Headerless control - the run lands, id == trace_id ```bash # headerless request curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # resolve the project to its session id curl -s "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/sessions?name=$LANGSMITH_PROJECT&limit=1" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" | jq -r '.[0].id' # # the headerless run is present: id == trace_id, success, no error curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"]}' \ | jq -r '.runs[] | [.id, .trace_id, .status, .error, .dotted_order]' # ["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","success",null,"20260818T100034808837Z7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"] # the run_id from the /v1/chat/completions 400 above never lands - no run exists for it curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0"]}' | jq -r '.runs | length' # 0 ```
Only requests carrying one of the session/trace headers trip the 400. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? `v1.97.0` ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _(optional, leave blank)_

signals.title: [Bug]: anthropic_messages drops plaintext reasoning across tool-call replay
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I searched existing issues and did not find this plaintext chat-completions round-trip failure. ### What happened? `anthropic_messages()` does not preserve plaintext reasoning state across its Anthropic ↔ chat-completions adapter when an assistant tool-call turn is replayed: 1. On the request path, an Anthropic `thinking` block is left only in the internal `thinking_blocks` field rather than restored as top-level `reasoning_content` on the chat assistant message. 2. On the response path, an explicitly present `reasoning_content: ""` is dropped because the adapter treats the field by truthiness, even when the same assistant turn contains tool calls. These are presence-sensitive protocol fields. Fireworks documents that interleaved thinking/tool use must replay the prior `reasoning_content`, and DeepSeek documents the same requirement for thinking-mode tool calls: - https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/reasoning - https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/ This is distinct from #26916, which concerns Anthropic thinking being serialized as visible OpenAI Responses `output_text`. This report concerns plaintext reasoning state crossing the Anthropic/chat-completions adapter in both directions. ### Minimal reproduction No provider credentials or network call are required. ```python from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.transformation import ( LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter, ) from litellm.types.utils import ModelResponse, Usage adapter = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter() request = { "model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [ { "role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "thinking", "thinking": " preserve me ", "signature": ""}, { "type": "tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "lookup", "input": {"q": "x"}, }, ], } ], } translated, _ = adapter.translate_anthropic_to_openai(request) assistant = translated["messages"][0] print(assistant) assert assistant["reasoning_content"] == " preserve me " response = ModelResponse( id="chatcmpl-test", model="accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro", choices=[ { "index": 0, "finish_reason": "tool_calls", "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "lookup", "arguments": '{"q":"x"}', }, } ], }, } ], usage=Usage(prompt_tokens=1, completion_tokens=1, total_tokens=2), ) blocks = adapter._translate_openai_content_to_anthropic(response.choices) print(blocks) assert blocks[0] == {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": None} ``` ### Observed output The first assertion fails because the translated assistant contains `thinking_blocks` but no `reasoning_content`: ```python { "role": "assistant", "content": None, "thinking_blocks": [ { "type": "thinking", "thinking": " preserve me ", "signature": "", "cache_control": {}, } ], "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup", "arguments": '{"q": "x"}'}, } ], } ``` If execution continues, the response translation contains no thinking block: ```python [ {"type": "text", "text": ""}, { "type": "tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "lookup", "input": {"q": "x"}, "provider_specific_fields": None, }, ] ``` ### Expected behavior - A plaintext Anthropic `thinking` block should become `reasoning_content` on the chat-completions assistant message with its exact value, including whitespace. - An explicitly present empty `reasoning_content` on an assistant tool-call response should remain representable in the Anthropic response shape so the next request can replay it. - A fully empty non-tool assistant response should remain omitted; the empty carrier is significant here because it accompanies tool calls. - Provider transforms may remove internal `thinking_blocks` before wire, but must retain `reasoning_content`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (`litellm` Python package), `anthropic_messages()` chat-completions adapter. ### LiteLLM version `1.95.0`

signals.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages streaming emits two content_block_stop for one tool_use block → tools executed twice
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? On `POST /v1/messages` with `stream: true`, when the model returns a tool call, the SSE stream contains **one `content_block_start` but two `content_block_stop` events for the same index**. This only happens for deployments whose `custom_llm_provider` is `openai` (i.e. the request is served by translating Anthropic Messages ⇄ OpenAI Chat Completions). Text-only responses on the same model/deployment are correctly 1:1. Deployments configured with `custom_llm_provider: anthropic` on the same proxy do not show it. Strict Anthropic clients treat every `content_block_stop` as "this block is complete", so Claude Code / `claude-agent-sdk` materializes the same `tool_use` block twice and **executes the tool twice**. The resulting conversation contains two `tool_result` blocks referencing the same `tool_use_id`, which is itself an Anthropic protocol violation on the following turn: ``` assistant msg=msg_80c9223d tool_use id=call_bews4NByNlDTUsgsZ9Qqe3ku name=Read input={"file_path":"..."} user tool_result for=call_bews4NByNlDTUsgsZ9Qqe3ku assistant msg=msg_80c9223d tool_use id=call_bews4NByNlDTUsgsZ9Qqe3ku name=Read input={"file_path":"..."} <-- same msg id, same tool_use id, same input user tool_result for=call_bews4NByNlDTUsgsZ9Qqe3ku ``` The upstream OpenAI-compatible backend is well-formed: for the same prompt, `POST /v1/chat/completions` on the same model streams exactly one `tool_call` id, one function name and one `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. The duplication is introduced on the `/v1/messages` path only. **Expected:** exactly one `content_block_stop` per `content_block_start`, as the Anthropic Messages streaming contract requires — so the client executes the tool once and produces one `tool_result` per `tool_use_id`. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running a Claude Code–based batch job through the gateway sees every tool call run twice, and tool side effects happen twice** 1. The developer starts their agent batch job, which points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the gateway and selects model `gpt-5.6-luna`; the agent sends `POST $PROXY_URL/v1/messages` with `"stream": true`, a system prompt, and 8 tools (file reads plus in-process MCP tools that save generated artifacts and run web searches). 2. The response stream comes back `200` and contains one `content_block_start` announcing `{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_9WCq9gl4Jp7N4Zd1pw5xe93V","name":"get_weather"}`, the `input_json_delta` fragments, and then **two** `content_block_stop` events with `"index": 0`, followed by `message_delta` with `"stop_reason":"tool_use"`. 3. The agent runs the tool, sends `POST $PROXY_URL/v1/messages` again with the tool result, and the transcript on disk now shows the same `tool_use` id twice and two `tool_result` blocks pointing at that one id. 4. Side effects double: the same web search is issued twice, the same artifact is written twice, and a text-replacement tool fails the second time with "original text not found" because the first call already applied it. On a batch of rows, this doubles token spend on tool turns and pollutes every generated artifact's history. 5. Switching the exact same job to a model whose deployment is Anthropic-native makes the doubling disappear, so the developer has to blacklist this model for any tool-using agent. **After a (hypothetical) fix: the same job runs each tool exactly once** 1. The developer starts the same agent batch job pointing at the gateway with model `gpt-5.6-luna`; the agent sends `POST $PROXY_URL/v1/messages` with `"stream": true`, the same system prompt and the same 8 tools. 2. The response stream comes back `200` with one `content_block_start` for `{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_…","name":"get_weather"}`, the `input_json_delta` fragments, and **one** `content_block_stop` with `"index": 0`, followed by `message_delta` with `"stop_reason":"tool_use"`. 3. The agent runs the tool once, sends `POST $PROXY_URL/v1/messages` with the tool result, and the transcript shows one `tool_use` id and one matching `tool_result`. 4. No doubled side effects: one web search, one artifact write, no spurious "original text not found" errors, and tool-turn token spend is halved back to the expected level. 5. The model behaves like the Anthropic-native deployments, so it can be used for tool-using agents without a special case. ### Proof the bug occurs **Config / setup the proxy ran with** The affected deployment is the only non-Anthropic-native one on this proxy (all other 11 deployments use `custom_llm_provider: anthropic` and are unaffected): ```yaml model_list: # affected: OpenAI-compatible upstream, served through the /v1/messages <-> chat/completions translation - model_name: gpt-5.6-luna litellm_params: model: gpt-5.6-luna custom_llm_provider: openai use_chat_completions_api: true api_base: http://<internal-openai-compatible-upstream>/v1 # exposes /v1/chat/completions only api_key: os.environ/UPSTREAM_KEY # unaffected control on the same proxy - model_name: gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: gpt-5.6-sol custom_llm_provider: anthropic api_base: http://<internal-anthropic-compatible-gateway> api_key: os.environ/GATEWAY_KEY ``` Env: `LITELLM_USE_CHAT_COMPLETIONS_URL_FOR_ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES` is **unset** ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Feature]: Add current Fireworks AI Serverless model cost entries
signals.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related issues: - [#35344](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35344) requests standard Kimi K3 support but contains no detailed pricing, metadata, or reproducible cost-map information. This issue includes Kimi K3 with the complete Fireworks pricing and metadata. - [#31459](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31459) already covers `glm-5p2-fast` and has PR [#31460](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/31460). `glm-5p2-fast` is therefore excluded from this request. - [#35410](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35410) is a broad Morph support request and does not cover this cost-map change. ## The Feature LiteLLM's cost map does not recognise the following exact Fireworks AI Serverless model IDs: - `accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3` - `accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-fast` - `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` - `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` - `accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b` - `accounts/fireworks/models/muse-glimmer-30b` - `accounts/fireworks/models/nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b` - `accounts/fireworks/models/nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4` Please add provider-accurate pricing and metadata for these exact IDs to both: - `model_prices_and_context_window.json` - `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` All entries should use: - `litellm_provider: "fireworks_ai"` - `mode: "chat"` - `supports_function_calling: true` Vision support should be enabled only for Kimi K3 and Muse Glimmer 30B, and disabled for the other entries. ### Pricing Prices are USD per 1M tokens in the order uncached input / cached input / output. | Model ID | Context / max output | Standard | Priority / Fast | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3` | 1,048,576 / 131,072 | $3 / $0.30 / $15 | Priority: $3.75 / $0.375 / $18.75 | | `accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k3-fast` | 1,048,576 / 131,072 | N/A | Fast: $4.50 / $0.45 / $22.50 | | `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | 1,048,576 / 131,072 | $0.14 / $0.028 / $0.28 | Priority: $0.21 / $0.042 / $0.42 | | `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | 1,048,576 / 131,072 | $1.32 / $0.044 / $3.96 | Priority: $1.65 / $0.055 / $4.95 | | `accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b` | 262,144 / 32,768 | $2 / $0.25 / $6 | N/A | | `accounts/fireworks/models/muse-glimmer-30b` | 131,072 / 16,384 | $0.35 / $0.04 / $1.50 | Priority: $0.525 / $0.06 / $2.25 | | `accounts/fireworks/models/nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b` | 262,144 / 32,768 | $0.05 / $0.01 / $0.20 | N/A | | `accounts/fireworks/models/nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4` | 262,144 / 32,768 | $0.60 / $0.12 / $2.40 | N/A | Convert the per-million-token prices to LiteLLM per-token fields by dividing by 1,000,000. Fast IDs are serving paths, not separate model families. The `kimi-k3-fast` entry should use the Kimi K3 model metadata and the Fireworks fast-serving price. Please include direct Fireworks model-page URLs in the `source` field: - [Kimi K3](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/kimi-k3) - [DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/deepseek-v4-flash-0731) - [DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/deepseek-v4-pro-0813) - [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b) - [Muse Glimmer 30B](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/muse-glimmer-30b) - [Nemotron Lightning](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b) - [Nemotron 3 Ultra](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4) Pricing authority is the [Fireworks Serverless pricing page](https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing). The DeepSeek Flash model page currently shows different Priority pricing than the pricing page. Please confirm the correct value before merging. Nemotron Ultra also shows a slightly different cached-input value on its model page; the pricing page value above should be treated as authoritative unless confirmed otherwise. ## User Flow ### Before this feature (today) A user sends a request through the proxy using one of the exact Fireworks model IDs above, but LiteLLM cannot calculate provider-accurate spend because the ID is absent from the cost map. 1. The user sends `POST <actual-proxy-url>/v1/chat/completions` with an exact Fireworks model ID, for example `accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b`. 2. The proxy forwards the request to Fireworks and receives a successful response containing usage information. 3. Cost reporting cannot calculate the correct provider cost for the exact model ID, resulting in missing, zero, or incorrect cost data. 4. The user's workaround is to maintain temporary pricing information outside LiteLLM. ### After this feature (ideal user flow) The same user sends the same request through the same proxy and receives accurate Fireworks cost reporting. 1. The user sends `POST <actual-proxy-url>/v1/chat/completions` with the same exact Fireworks model ID. 2. The proxy forwards the request to Fireworks and receives the same successful response containing usage information. 3. Cost reporting recognises the exact model ID and calculates spend using the published Fireworks input, cached-input, output, and Priority rates. 4. The user can rely on LiteLLM cost reporting without maintaining temporary external pricing configuration. Fireworks API documentation: https://docs.fireworks.ai/api-reference/post-chatcompletions ## How far you got ### Proxy setup Not relevant, missing config from json. ### LiteLLM version or commit ```text 1.97.0 (not present in models.litellm.ai either) ``` ### Request through the proxy ```bash curl -X POST "<actual-proxy-url>/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b", "max_tokens": 32, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}] }' ``` Paste the complete response here, including the missing, zero, or incorrect cost result. ### Direct Fireworks request ```bash curl https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $FIREWORKS_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-2p4t-a95b", "max_tokens": 32, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}] }' ``` Paste the complete successful response here, with the API key redacted. ### What stopped me The exact Fireworks model ID is absent from LiteLLM's cost map, so the proxy cannot calculate provider-accurate cost reporting for the request. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: [Feature]: Derive a stable session id for chatgpt/ models when the client sends none, so multi-turn conversations hit the upstream prompt cache
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (Closest found: #29978, which maps Codex session metadata into observability fields, and the Vertex Anthropic session-affinity work in #31898; neither derives a session id when the client sends none) ### The Feature When a request to a chatgpt/ model arrives with no session identifier, derive a deterministic one from the conversation's stable prefix (for example a hash of the system prompt plus the first user message) instead of generating a random one per request. The same conversation then maps to the same upstream cache shard on every turn, so the backend serves the resent history from its prompt cache. Clients that already send a session id keep full control; the derivation only fills the gap for clients that cannot be changed The upstream capability already exists and already works through LiteLLM when the caller passes `litellm_session_id` explicitly; the transcript below shows ~91% of input tokens served from cache on a repeat call with it, and 0% without it. The missing piece is only the default when nothing is passed: today that default is a fresh random id per request, which guarantees a cache miss on every turn of a multi-turn conversation ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a Claude Code user routing requests to a chatgpt/ model through the proxy burns subscription quota reprocessing the full conversation every turn, because each request lands on a fresh prompt-cache shard 1. They configure a model_name mapping to chatgpt/gpt-5.4 and point Claude Code at the proxy 2. Each agent turn sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the full conversation history; Claude Code sends no session identifier 3. Every response reports cached input tokens at or near zero, even though each turn resends an identical prefix that is tens or hundreds of thousands of tokens 4. Weekly subscription quota drains several times faster than the same conversation in the native client; the workaround they live with is an out-of-tree proxy hook that injects a deterministic session id hashed from the conversation prefix, which restores roughly 90 percent cached input but has to be re-verified on every LiteLLM upgrade After this feature (ideal user flow): the same conversation hits the upstream prompt cache with no client or hook changes 1. They configure the same model_name mapping and point Claude Code at the proxy 2. Each agent turn sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with no session identifier 3. The proxy derives the same conversation-stable session id turn after turn, and responses report most of the input as cached 4. Quota consumption tracks new tokens instead of full-history reprocessing ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: codex litellm_params: model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 ``` Proxy: `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000`, ChatGPT device-code auth cached under `~/.config/litellm/chatgpt/` Version or commit: stock `litellm_internal_staging` at 973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e Two request bodies were generated, each with a different deterministic ~6.4K-token filler document (different between runs so the second run starts from a cold cache and cannot ride anything the first warmed). Run A sends the identical body twice with no session field; Run B sends its identical body twice with `"litellm_session_id": "stable-demo-1"` added ```bash curl -sS -D a1.headers -o a1.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_a.json curl -sS -D a2.headers -o a2.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_a.json curl -sS -D b1.headers -o b1.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_b.json curl -sS -D b2.headers -o b2.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_b.json ``` All four calls returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Usage extracted from each response's `response.completed` event (the provider returns the body as SSE), verbatim: ``` a1.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 26, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6471} a2.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 24, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6469} b1.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 26, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6471} b2.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 24, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6469} ``` What stopped me there: with no session field, the byte-identical repeat call (a2) reports `cached_tokens: 0`; there is nothing a client like Claude Code can set without modification, and nothing in proxy config changes the default. Passing `litellm_session_id` explicitly makes the repeat call (b2) report 5888 of 6445 input tokens cached (~91%), which shows the upstream path is already functional and only the no-id default is missing ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details https://linkedin.com/in/dkrisman

signals.title: [Bug]: generic_cost_per_token double-counts overlapping cached image tokens
signals.text: ### What happened? `generic_cost_per_token()` can overcharge multimodal requests when `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` are overlapping subsets of `prompt_tokens`. Some OpenAI-compatible providers report usage with these semantics: - `prompt_tokens`: total input tokens across all modalities - `cached_tokens`: the subset of total input read from cache - `image_tokens`: the subset of total input attributable to images `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` are therefore not guaranteed to be disjoint. ### Minimal synthetic reproduction Assume a model with no explicit `input_cost_per_image_token`, so image tokens use the ordinary input rate: ```python usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=10, total_tokens=110, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetailsWrapper( text_tokens=None, cached_tokens=90, image_tokens=80, ), ) model_info = { "input_cost_per_token": 1e-6, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 1e-7, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-6, } ``` With overlapping dimensions, the expected price is: ```text uncached input = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens = 10 prompt cost = 10 * 1e-6 + 90 * 1e-7 = 19e-6 output cost = 10 * 2e-6 = 20e-6 total = 39e-6 ``` Current `main` computes: ```text text_tokens = max(100 - 90 - 80, 0) = 0 prompt cost = 90 * 1e-7 + 80 * 1e-6 = 89e-6 output cost = 20e-6 total = 109e-6 ``` The 70 overlapping image/cache tokens are charged once at the cache rate and again at the full input rate. ### Root cause The generic calculator detects overlapping token details, then calculates text as the remainder: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py#L841-L861 It later prices both cached tokens and image tokens independently: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py#L654-L671 This assumes cache and modality details are mutually exclusive buckets. ### Related upstream work - #18750 and merged PR #18768 already handle the same semantic issue for Gemini by reading `cacheTokensDetails` and subtracting cached tokens per modality. - Merged PR #19772 fixes the case where `text_tokens` includes cached tokens, but its generic remainder calculation does not resolve cache/image intersection when only aggregate cache tokens are available. ### Expected behavior Each input token should be billed exactly once. - If a provider supplies cached-token counts per modality, normalize text/image/audio into uncached modality buckets before generic pricing. - If only aggregate `cached_tokens` and aggregate modality totals are available, the generic calculator should not assume they are disjoint. - For models where image tokens are included in `prompt_tokens` and use the same input rate, pricing should use `(prompt_tokens - cached_tokens) * input_rate + cached_tokens * cache_rate`. - Models with a distinct image rate need an explicit provider/model semantic or a per-modality cache breakdown; aggregate overlapping fields are insufficient to derive exact buckets. OpenAI documents that images count as input tokens and can participate in prompt caching: - https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision - https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching ### Impact Incorrect `response_cost` / `raw_spend` propagates to spend logs, budgets, alerts, chargeback, and billing reconciliation for affected OpenAI-compatible multimodal providers. ### Version Reproduced against upstream `main` at commit `bc6e7df05b018eefe6c7293790ca3f4de38709ac`. ### Data note All token counts and prices in this report are synthetic. No production request, customer, endpoint, credential, or billing data is included.

signals.title: [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment
signals.text: # [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related: #37117 (same root cause in `savings.py`, but scoped there to *multiple deployments per `model_name` + `cost-based-routing`*). Filing separately because the trigger is much broader — a **single deployment with default routing** is enough — and because there is an additional key-shadowing behaviour that constrains the fix. Also related: #35693 (same `shared_backend_model_info()` stripping, surfaced as an unsuppressible cache-cost warning). ## What happened? The Cost Optimization dashboard reports **"$0.00" next to a perfectly correct non-zero "N tokens compressed"**. In our case: `2,642,007 tokens compressed`, `compression_savings_spend = $0.00`, while real `spend` for the same rollup row was `$11.71`. The trigger is not multi-deployment routing. It is simply: > the deployment carries operator-supplied custom pricing **and** the model is not in LiteLLM's built-in cost map — i.e. **any self-hosted / custom model**. Chain of events for a single deployment: 1. `Router._create_deployment()` registers the deployment's pricing under **two** keys: - the deployment UUID -> full pricing retained - `{provider}/{model}` -> passed through `shared_backend_model_info()`, which **strips every pricing field** 2. The **public `model_name`** — the value the spend log records, and therefore the only thing `compute_savings_spend()` receives — is **never registered with pricing at all**. 3. `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` calls `litellm.get_model_info(model=<public name>, custom_llm_provider=...)`, which raises `"This model isn't mapped yet"` for a custom model. 4. That raise is caught and the helper "falls open" to `(0.0, 0.0)`. 5. `compression = saved_tokens * 0.0 == 0.0`. Billing (`spend`) is unaffected, because response-cost calculation reads the deployment object directly instead of going through `litellm.model_cost`. Only the savings columns break, which is why the token count and the dollar figure disagree. ## Relevant log output ``` get_model_info('muse-glimmer-30b','openai') -> Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=muse-glimmer-30b, custom_llm_provider=openai _input_and_cache_read_cost('muse-glimmer-30b','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) ``` DB rollup row (`LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend`) showing the contradiction: ``` date=2026-08-18 model=muse-glimmer-30b custom_llm_provider=openai prompt_tokens = 31,274,060 spend = 11.7122 <-- billing works compression_saved_tokens = 2,642,007 <-- correct compression_savings_spend = 0.0 <-- should be ~$0.9247 api_requests = 2,287 ``` The per-request guardrail metadata is recorded correctly, so nothing is wrong upstream of pricing: ```json {"guardrail_name": "headroom-compression", "guardrail_provider": "headroom", "guardrail_status": "success", "guardrail_response": {"tokens_before": 49323, "tokens_after": 49206, "tokens_saved": 117}} ``` ## Steps to Reproduce Minimal config — **one** deployment, no `router_settings`, no `cost-based-routing`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: muse-glimmer-30b litellm_params: model: muse-glimmer-30b custom_llm_provider: openai api_base: https://your-self-hosted-endpoint/v1 api_key: os.environ/MY_TOKEN input_cost_per_token: 3.5e-07 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-06 guardrails: - guardrail_name: headroom-compression litellm_params: guardrail: headroom mode: pre_call api_base: http://headroom-proxy:8787 default_on: true ``` Send traffic through it, then read `/user/daily/activity` (or the Cost Optimization tile): `total_compression_saved_tokens` climbs, `total_compression_savings_spend` stays `0.0`. Reproduced directly in the running container, replaying what `Router` does for that single deployment: ```python import litellm from litellm.router import shared_backend_model_info from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import _input_and_cache_read_cost PRICE = {"input_cost_per_token": 3.5e-07, "output_cost_per_token": 1.5e-06, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 3.5e-07} full = dict(PRICE, id="dep-solo") litellm.register_model(model_cost={"dep-solo": full}) litellm.register_model(model_cost={"openai/solo-model": shared_backend_model_info(full)}) print(litellm.model_cost["dep-solo"]["input_cost_per_token"]) # 3.5e-07 print(litellm.model_cost["openai/solo-model"]["input_cost_per_token"]) # None print(litellm.model_cost.get("solo-model")) # None print(_input_and_cache_read_cost("solo-model", "openai")) # (0.0, 0.0) ``` Output: ``` model_cost['dep-solo'].input = 3.5e-07 model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input = None model_cost['solo-model'] = None LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) ``` ### Second finding: the provider-prefixed key shadows the public name Important for whichever fix is chosen. `get_model_info()` prefers the combined `{provider}/{model}` key, and `Router` has already created that key *without* pricing. So registering pricing under the bare public name is **not** sufficient: ``` after pricing bare 'solo-model': model_cost['solo-model'].input = 3.5e-07 model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input = None LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) <-- STILL ZERO after also pricing 'openai/solo-model': LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (3.5e-07, 3.5e-07) <-- fixed ``` ## What did you expect to happen? `compression_savings_spend` / `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should price saved tokens at the deployment's configured input rate whenever that rate is known — which it demonstrably is, since ordinary `spend` is calculated correctly from the same deployment. Expected for the row above: `2,642,007 x 3.5e-07 = $0.9247`. At minimum, savings should never silently render `$0.00` beside a non-zero token count; that reads as "compression achieved nothing" rather than "pricing lookup failed". ## Suggested fix Preferred: make the savings path deployment-aware rather than name-aware, so key shadowing is irrelevant. **Option C** (in addition to Options A/B in #37117): have `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` consult `Router.get_deployment_model_info(model_id, model)` before falling back to `get_model_info()`. `savings.py` already imports `Router` for the autorouter baseline and `_effective_model_info()` already performs deployment-aware resolution, so most of the plumbing exists. Two smaller points regardless of approach: 1. Any cost-map-repair fix must also write the `{provider}/{model}` key, or stop `shared_backend_model_info()` from stripping pricing when a single deployment owns that key (cf. #35693). 2. Consider distinguishing "priced at zero" from "price unknown". The current fall-open to `(0.0, 0.0)` turns a lookup failure into a confident `$0.00`; a debug log exists but nothing surfaces to the operator. `compression_savings_spend` is written with `increment`, so historical rows will remain `$0.00` after a fix and need a separate backfill. ## Workaround A `CustomLogger` registered via `litellm_settings.callbacks` that mirrors each deployment's pricing (read back from `litellm.model_cost[<deployment id>]`) onto both the public `model_name` and the `{provider}/{model}` key, re-synced on an interval to catch DB/UI-added deployments. It invents no prices: deployments without custom pricing are skipped, so nothing is over-reported. Verified end-to-end against the live proxy after deploying it: ``` delta saved_tokens = 734 delta saved_usd = 0.000256900 expected (734 x 3.5e-07) = 0.000256900 MATCH /user/daily/activity -> total_compression_savings_spend = 0.00113715 (was 0.0) ``` Also confirmed to survive a pod restart (860 saved tokens -> $0.000301, exact match). ## Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.2 (also verified present in v1.97.0) ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Feature]: Support GPT-5.6 (Sol / Terra / Luna) via Amazon Bedrock Runtime
signals.text: ### Overview AWS [announced on 2026-08-17](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/amazon-bedrock-cross-region-openai-v2/) that the GPT-5.6 family — Sol, Terra, and Luna — is now available through the **Bedrock Runtime** data plane, distinct from the existing Bedrock Mantle path. LiteLLM currently only has entries for these models under `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}`. There is no equivalent under a `bedrock/` prefix to reach them via Runtime. ### Why this matters Bedrock Runtime introduces two routing modes not available through Mantle: - **Geo (US CRIS)** — routes within a predefined US geography - **Global** — routes across any commercial AWS Region where the model is available, at lower per-token cost and with the highest throughput during demand spikes This addresses a practical capacity limitation with the current Mantle setup: as of 2026-07 GPT-5.6 is only available in us-east-1 / us-east-2, whereas global inference via Runtime removes that constraint. ### Problem Attempting to call these models via the Runtime path today fails. There are no model cost/metadata entries for them under a `bedrock` (non-Mantle) provider, and manually registering a model using the `openai.gpt-5.6-*` IDs produces: ``` BedrockException - {"message":"{\"error\":{\"code\":\"unsupported_parameter\",\"message\":\"Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model.\",\"param\":\"max_tokens\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}"} ``` ### Expected behavior LiteLLM should support invoking `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, and `openai.gpt-5.6-luna` via Amazon Bedrock Runtime, including support for the cross-region global inference endpoints, with correct parameter mapping for these models.

signals.title: [Bug]: prometheus_initialize_budget_metrics emits no key budget metrics for keys with team_id = NULL
signals.text: ### What happened? With `litellm_settings.prometheus_initialize_budget_metrics: true`, the background job runs and its user, team and org branches work, but `litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric` is never emitted for any virtual key whose `team_id` is `NULL` — which is every key created without an explicit team. The gauge therefore exists only for keys that have made a request since the last proxy restart. For a deployment whose keys are mostly idle, a metric that is supposed to be pre-populated is empty, and any alert resting on it is silently inert. Nothing logs an error and the job reports no failure. Related but distinct: #29937 reports budget metrics being *emitted with the wrong value*. This is about them not being emitted at all. ### Root cause `PrometheusLogger._initialize_api_key_budget_metrics` fetches keys through `_list_key_helper` with `exclude_team_id=UI_SESSION_TOKEN_TEAM_ID`, to filter out UI dashboard session tokens: ```python # litellm/integrations/prometheus.py key_list_response: Final = await _list_key_helper( ... exclude_team_id=UI_SESSION_TOKEN_TEAM_ID, # "litellm-dashboard" return_full_object=True, ... ) ``` which becomes: ```python # litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py if exclude_team_id and isinstance(exclude_team_id, str): user_condition["team_id"] = {"not": exclude_team_id} ``` `{"not": ...}` on a nullable column is a SQL inequality, and `NULL <> 'litellm-dashboard'` evaluates to `NULL`, not `TRUE`. Rows with `team_id IS NULL` are excluded along with the dashboard tokens, so `_set_key_list_budget_metrics` receives a list containing none of them. The user, team and org branches of the same job do not pass `exclude_team_id`, which is why they populate correctly and only the key branch is affected. `_initialize_api_key_budget_metrics` is the only caller in the codebase that passes a non-`None` `exclude_team_id`, so the blast radius is this one code path. `GET /key/list` leaves it unset and returns `NULL`-team keys normally, which is why the UI is unaffected and this is easy to miss. ### Steps to Reproduce On a proxy with a database and `prometheus_initialize_budget_metrics: true`: 1. Create a key with a budget and **no** team: ```bash curl -X POST $PROXY/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"key_alias":"no-team","max_budget":5.0}' ``` 2. Wait for more than one `PROMETHEUS_BUDGET_METRICS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` tick (default 5 minutes). Make no request with the key. 3. `GET /metrics` — no `litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric` series for it. 4. Create a team and a key inside it: ```bash curl -X POST $PROXY/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_alias":"t"}' curl -X POST $PROXY/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"key_alias":"with-team","team_id":"<team_id>","max_budget":7.0}' ``` 5. Wait for the next tick, again making no request with it. 6. `GET /metrics` — the team-scoped key **does** get a series. ### Evidence Proxy restarted at `01:58:59Z`, readings at `02:10Z`, so two ticks of the 5-minute job had passed. Five virtual keys existed, each with `max_budget=5.0` and no team. Same job, other branches, populated correctly: ``` litellm_total_users 1.0 litellm_active_users 1.0 litellm_teams_count 0.0 ``` Key branch, one series, and it is not one of the five: ``` litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric{api_key_alias="",hashed_api_key="litellm_proxy_master_key"} +Inf ``` **Isolating it against traffic.** A throwaway key with `max_budget=5.0` and no team produced no series when minted. One local chat completion with it produced the series immediately: ``` BEFORE 1 series (master key only) mint key, max_budget=5.0 no new series one chat completion HTTP 200 +25s litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric{ api_key_alias="budget-metric-probe", ...} 5.0 ``` **Isolating it against the team filter.** A key created inside a team, with `max_budget=7.0` and **no request ever made with it**, was picked up by the initialiser after one tick, while the `NULL`-team keys still were not: ``` BEFORE 2 series create team, mint key in it, make no request +6 min AFTER 3 series, now including litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric{api_key_alias="null-team-probe-key",...} 7.0 ``` **Against the database.** Running the predicate the filter implies against the live `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` table: ``` total keys | 9 team_id IS NULL | 7 team_id <> 'litellm-dashboard' | 0 NOT (team_id = 'litellm-dashboard') | 0 ``` All seven real keys have `team_id IS NULL`, and the inequality returns none of them. ### Suggested fix The filter needs to keep rows where `team_id IS NULL`. Sketch, **untested**: ```python if exclude_team_id and isinstance(exclude_team_id, str): user_condition["OR"] = [ {"team_id": {"not": exclude_team_id}}, {"team_id": None}, ] ``` `user_condition` is appended into an existing `or_conditions` list, so whether a nested `OR` composes cleanly there is worth checking. Since `_initialize_api_key_budget_metrics` is the only caller passing `exclude_team_id`, an alternative is to filter dashboard tokens out in the Prometheus code after fetching and leave `_list_key_helper` untouched. ### Relevant log output ```shell No error is logged. The job completes and reports success; the series is simply absent. ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ --- Environment detail: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, digest `sha256:468c25f35f3e5ec4e414974f00deab93337b1b4d9953cabcfd3722e59415f834`, built 2026-08-16. `litellm-enterprise` 0.1.54. PostgreSQL 16, single proxy process, no Redis, `store_model_in_db: false`. Possibly related and not investigated: a key's `litellm_remaining_api_key_budget_metric` series persists in the process registry after the key is deleted through `/key/delete`, and is still exported on subsequent scrapes until the proxy restarts. Mentioned only in case it shares a cause.

signals.title: [Bug]: Responses bridge returns one choice per output message item — internal reasoning/plan text becomes choices[0] on n=1 chat requests (gpt-5.4+)
signals.text: ### What happened? When a `/chat/completions` request is transparently bridged to the Responses API, `_convert_response_output_to_choices()` (in `litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py`) emits **one `choices[]` entry per Responses output `message` item**, with incrementing index. GPT-5.4+ with reasoning active frequently emits a short plan/preamble `message` item before the final answer `message` item, so an `n=1` chat request comes back with **two choices**: - `choices[0]` = the model's internal plan/preamble text, `finish_reason: "stop"` - `choices[1]` = the actual user-facing answer Virtually every Chat Completions client (OpenAI SDKs, LangChain/LangGraph, ...) reads `choices[0]` only, so **the user is shown the model's internal reasoning and the real answer is silently discarded**. The caller never asked for `n>1`, and nothing in the response signals that choices[0] is not the answer. This is easy to hit unknowingly: gpt-5.4+ rejects function tools on `/v1/chat/completions` whenever reasoning is active, and `responses_api_bridge_check()` (litellm/main.py) reroutes those requests through the Responses API automatically. So a caller who sets `reasoning_effort: "low"` on a chat request with tools gets opted into the bridge — and into this bug — without changing anything else. **Observed in production** (2026-08-17, LiteLLM proxy in front of `openai/gpt-5.4`, `reasoning_effort: "low"`, 15 function tools, non-streaming): a customer-facing agent replied to an end user with: > "Need ask for specific date because resolver failed, but can mention 2-bed offered. Must start exact greeting Hello! I'm ELI... despite additionalInstruction conflict due explicit. ..." while the real answer sat unread in `choices[1]`. We also hit the sibling shape `[message item, function_call item]` → `[text choice, tool_calls choice]`, where reading choices[0] makes an agent framework treat the turn as final and **skip the tool call entirely**. That shape is already covered by PR #33931 — but #33931 explicitly does *not* merge multiple plain `message` items (its multi-message handling still emits one choice per message), so this issue remains after it merges. ### Expected behavior For a request with `n` absent or `n=1`, the bridge should return **exactly one choice**, like the native Chat Completions endpoint does: - the final `message` item's text is `choices[0].message.content` - earlier `message` items (preamble/plan) belong in `message.reasoning_content` (alongside text from `reasoning` items), not in a separate choice - if the turn contains tool calls, they live on that same single choice with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` (PR #33931's merge) `choices[]` cardinality should be driven by the caller's `n`, never by the provider's output item count. ### Repro Any gpt-5.4+ chat completion that (a) gets bridged to the Responses API and (b) returns `[reasoning?, message, message]` output items. Minimal unit-level repro against the transform: ```python from openai.types.responses import ResponseOutputMessage, ResponseOutputText from litellm.completion_extras.litellm_responses_transformation.transformation import ( LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler, ) items = [ ResponseOutputMessage( id="msg_1", role="assistant", status="completed", type="message", content=[ResponseOutputText(type="output_text", text="Internal plan: ask for the date first.", annotations=[])], ), ResponseOutputMessage( id="msg_2", role="assistant", status="completed", type="message", content=[ResponseOutputText(type="output_text", text="Hello! What move-in date works for you?", annotations=[])], ), ] choices = LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler._convert_response_output_to_choices(items) assert len(choices) == 1, f"expected 1 choice for an n=1 request, got {len(choices)}" # fails: len(choices) == 2, choices[0] is the internal plan ``` ### Related - PR #33931 — merges message + tool_calls into one choice; does **not** cover the multiple-plain-messages case. - PR #33242 / issue #33221 — the auto-bridge trigger (function tools + reasoning on gpt-5.4+). ### Relevant log output ``` POST /v1/chat/completions, model=gpt-5.4, reasoning_effort=low, 15 function tools, n not set -> response: 2 choices, finish_reasons ["stop","stop"] choices[0].message.content = "Need ask for specific date because resolver failed, ..." # internal plan choices[1].message.content = "Hello! I'm ELI, the virtual leasing agent for ..." # real answer, discarded by clients ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? Reproduced on main (2026-08-18) via code inspection of `_convert_response_output_to_choices`; observed in prod behind `main-stable`.

signals.title: [Bug] router_settings.max_fallbacks silently dropped by /config/update — UpdateRouterConfig schema excludes it
signals.text: ## What happened Setting `router_settings.max_fallbacks` via `POST /config/update` returns "Config updated successfully" but the value is **silently dropped** — never persisted, never applied. No warning. ## Why 1. `UpdateRouterConfig` (litellm/types/router.py) has no `max_fallbacks` field → pydantic drops it. 2. `Router.update_settings()` whitelist also excludes it. 3. Runtime enforcement (`async_function_with_fallbacks`) reads `self.max_fallbacks`, set only at Router construction. So the only ways to change it: bootstrap config.yaml + restart, or `ROUTER_MAX_FALLBACKS` env. ## Impact Any proxy whose fallback chains exceed 5 hops silently loses every hop beyond 5. The /config/update success message makes this invisible — chains LOOK configured in /router/settings fallbacks list, but traversal is capped at 5. ## Expected Either (a) add `max_fallbacks` to `UpdateRouterConfig` + `update_settings()` whitelist, or (b) reject unknown router_settings keys with 400 instead of silently dropping. ## Repro ```bash curl -X POST /config/update -d '{"router_settings": {"max_fallbacks": 10}}' # → success message curl /router/settings | jq '.[] | select(.field_name=="max_fallbacks")' # → still 5 ``` Verified on v1.81.3 and current main (types/router.py checked via gh api 2026-08-18).

signals.title: [Bug]: langfuse_otel raises JSONDecodeError for Responses API function calls with empty or invalid arguments
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? ## Issue description ### Description The langfuse_otel callback raises a JSONDecodeError while processing tool calls returned through the OpenAI Responses API. LiteLLM still returns HTTP 200 to the client, but the Langfuse observation output may be incomplete and the exception generates significant log noise. ### Environment - LiteLLM: 1.97.0 - Python: 3.13 - Deployment: Docker - Image: docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:main-stable - Callback: langfuse_otel - Endpoint: POST /v1/responses ### User Flow ### Error LiteLLM:ERROR: opentelemetry.py:2506 - OpenTelemetry logging error in set_attributes Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../litellm/integrations/opentelemetry.py", line 2163, in set_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger.set_langfuse_otel_attributes( span, kwargs, response_obj ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 53, in set_langfuse_otel_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger._set_langfuse_specific_attributes( span=span, kwargs=kwargs, response_obj=response_obj, ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 244, in _set_langfuse_specific_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger._set_observation_output( span=span, response_obj=response_obj, ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 196, in _set_observation_output arguments_obj = json.loads(arguments_str) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/json/__init__.py", line 352, in loads return _default_decoder.decode(s) json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) The associated request still succeeds: POST /v1/responses HTTP/1.1 200 ### Observed frequency During a 24-hour inspection: OpenTelemetry JSON errors: 674 /v1/responses requests: 3931 /v1/responses HTTP 200: 3913 ### Root cause In LangfuseOtelLogger._set_observation_output(), the Responses API path assumes that every string in function_call.arguments contains valid JSON: elif item_type == "function_call": arguments_str = getattr(item, "arguments", "{}") arguments_obj = ( json.loads(arguments_str) if isinstance(arguments_str, str) else arguments_str ) An empty string, whitespace, partially generated JSON, or non-JSON argument causes json.loads() to raise. The Chat Completions path in the same function already handles this condition with try/except, but the Responses API path does not. ### Expected behavior Invalid tool arguments should not cause the telemetry callback to raise an exception. LiteLLM should safely record a fallback value and continue exporting the span. ### Suggested fix Apply the same guard already used by the Chat Completions path: elif item_type == "function_call": arguments_str = getattr(item, "arguments", "{}") try: arguments_obj = ( json.loads(arguments_str) if isinstance(arguments_str, str) else arguments_str ) except json.JSONDecodeError: arguments_obj = {} langfuse_tool_call = { "id": getattr(item, "id", ""), "name": getattr(item, "name", ""), "call_id": getattr(item, "call_id", ""), "type": "function_call", "arguments": arguments_obj, } output_items_data.append(langfuse_tool_call) Alternatively, the raw argument string could be retained instead of {} to avoid losing diagnostic information: except json.JSONDecodeError: arguments_obj = arguments_str ### Suggested regression tests Add tests covering Responses API function_call output with: - Valid JSON arguments. - Empty-string arguments. - Whitespace-only arguments. - Incomplete or non-JSON arguments. - Arguments already represented as a dictionary. The test should confirm that _set_observation_output() does not raise and that the Langfuse observation output is still recorded. ### Proof the bug occurs e: line 1 column 1 (char 0). Arguments: redacted-by-litellm litellm | 17:18:56 - LiteLLM:ERROR: opentelemetry.py:2506 - OpenTelemetry logging error in set_attributes Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) litellm | Traceback (most recent call last): litellm | File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/opentelemetry.py", line 2163, in set_attributes litellm | LangfuseOtelLogger.set_langfuse_otel_attributes(span, kwargs, response_obj) litellm | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ litellm | File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 53, in set_langfuse_otel_attributes litellm | LangfuseOtelLogger._set_langfuse_specific_attributes(span=span, kwargs=kwargs, response_obj=response_obj) litellm | response_obj=response_obj) litellm | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ litellm | File litellm | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ litellm | File "/usr/lib/python3.13/json/decoder.py", line 363, in raw_decode litellm | raise JSONDecodeError("Expecting value", s, err.value) from None litellm | json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about?
