signal.title: refactor(ui): migrate the key edit form off Ant Design onto react-hook-form
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Key editing was the last antd Form in the key flow - antd's store made the saved payload implicit, not stated - A control could silently stop feeding the payload undetected How it solves it: - Ports the form to react-hook-form and the shadcn primitives - Projects the payload explicitly, so every saved key is written out - Keeps the existing suite as the contract, unedited apart from query mechanics - A payload net written against the antd version passes unchanged ## User Flow This is a refactor, so the two flows are step-for-step identical and the saved key is byte-identical. What changes is the rendered control set Before: a proxy admin edits a virtual key and the form is drawn with Ant Design controls 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Settings 2. The editor shows the antd controls: an antd multi-select for Models, antd selects for Key Type and Reset Budget, antd inputs for the limits 3. They change Key Alias, add a model, set Reset Budget, then click Save Changes 4. The key is saved and the row reflects the new alias and models After: the same admin edits the same key and the form is drawn with the dashboard's own controls 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Settings 2. The editor shows the shadcn controls: a chips combobox for Models, dashboard selects for Key Type and Reset Budget, dashboard inputs for the limits 3. They change Key Alias, add a model, set Reset Budget, then click Save Changes 4. The key is saved and the row reflects the new alias and models, exactly as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once in two terminals from the repo root: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` ```bash cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev ``` Then create the key both sides edit, so the starting record is the same: ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"parity-probe","models":["gpt-4o"],"max_budget":10,"tpm_limit":100,"rpm_limit":10,"metadata":{"tags":["blue"]}}' ``` The capture is the same on both sides: open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, click the `parity-probe` key, open Settings, open DevTools Network and filter on `key/update`, make exactly these edits, click Save Changes, then copy the request payload of the `POST /key/update` that fires. The edits, in order: set Key Alias to `parity-probe-edited`, add `gpt-4o-mini` to Models, set Reset Budget to `monthly`, set TPM Limit to `250`, tick Never Expire ### Before (MERGE_BASE_SHA) #### /key/update request payload, antd form 1. `git checkout MERGE_BASE_SHA` and restart the dev server 2. Run the capture above 3. Paste the request payload here #### the saved record 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=<the generated key>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Paste the response here ### After (TIP_SHA) #### /key/update request payload, react-hook-form 1. `git checkout TIP_SHA` and restart the dev server 2. Run the capture above against a freshly generated `parity-probe` key 3. Paste the request payload here, it should match the Before payload key for key #### the saved record 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=<the generated key>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Paste the response here Screenshots of the editor on both sides go under the matching case, so the control change is visible next to the identical payload ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Seven tests had queries rewritten; antd selectors cannot match shadcn - Those seven are proven by mutation, not by passing both ways - MCP and Agent selectors are stubbed here, they remain antd - `TagsInput` still lives under the guardrails route folder - Several selector labels resolve to nothing, pre-existing, not fixed here - `TagsInput` and `MultiSelect` gained an optional `disabled` prop ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: test(ui): pin the MCP server edit save payload before the form migration
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nothing asserts the MCP server edit save payload - No `toStrictEqual` anywhere, so key changes stay invisible - Upcoming form migration would change it silently How it solves it: - 19 cases pin the exact object sent to the server - Values captured from live behaviour, not read off the source - Six-mutant battery proves the net actually bites ## User Flow There is no user-visible change here, by design. This PR adds tests only, and the point of it is that the flow below stays byte-identical before and after. Both lists are therefore the same list Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change After: unchanged 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so there is no live-proxy before and after to show. Stating that plainly rather than staging a run that would look identical on both sides The evidence that matters for a characterization net is whether it fails when the thing it pins changes. That is the mutation battery below, run at `9df4cafcfb`, six mutants applied one at a time to the payload builder in `mcp_server_edit.tsx`, each reverted before the next Every anchor was asserted unique before substitution, and every run was checked to have executed all 19 tests, so a mutant that silently failed to apply or broke the file would report as a harness fault instead of a kill. Two earlier mutants did exactly that and were caught by those guards | mutant | payload change | tests red | | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | leaks `created_by` into the body | 19 / 19 | | M2 | drops `logo_url` from `mcp_info` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M3 | emits `allowed_tools` with the gate removed | 17 | | M4 | turns a flat key into a lodash path | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M5 | sends `null` where today it sends `undefined` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M6 | sends `null` where today it sends `[]` | 18 / 18 strict cases | Kill rate 6/6. M3 spares the two allowlist cases because `allowed_tools` is present either way in one and the gate is the subject of the other. M1 is the only mutant the leak-guard case catches, which is what it exists for M5 is the one worth reading twice. It is caught only because the file uses `toStrictEqual`; `toEqual` treats a key holding `undefined` as absent, and that is precisely the distinction that separates a gated-off field from a mounted-but-empty one in this form today ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Records current behaviour, including anything currently wrong - `alias` and `mcp_access_groups` assignments are dead, shadowed by `...restValues` - Both left untouched here, noted for the payload extraction next - Integration tier, so roughly two seconds per case ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Custom classifiers (classifier_type "custom", from the earlier backend PR) are config-file-only - The dashboard cannot create or edit a custom-classifier auto-router at all - The models table mislabels custom routers "Heuristic" How it solves it: - New top-level `classifier_plugins` config key: names mapped to dotted paths - Names resolve through a registry at save, load, and deployment init - Dashboard picker gains a Custom classifier option with a plugin dropdown - Decision card and models table now name the plugin cause correctly ## User Flow Before: a platform admin who wants a team-aware auto-router cannot build one in the dashboard 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-playground → Models and Endpoints → Add Model → Auto Router 2. The Classification method picker offers only Heuristic and LLM Classifier 3. They try POST /model/new with `"classifier_plugin": "tier-by-team"` and get back 400 `complexity_router_config is invalid at classifier_plugin: Input should be an instance of ClassifierPlugin` 4. Their only path is editing config.yaml on the proxy host and restarting After: the same admin declares plugins once in config and builds routers in the dashboard 1. The operator adds a top-level `classifier_plugins:` block naming `tier-by-team` and restarts the proxy once 2. The admin opens Add Model → Auto Router; the picker now shows Custom classifier 3. Selecting it reveals a dropdown listing `spend-aware` and `tier-by-team`, a plugin timeout field, and the classifier fallback picker 4. Saving sends the name; the same POST from step 3 above now returns the created model 5. A saved router with an unknown name is rejected at save with `'no-such-plugin' is not a registered classifier plugin; declare it under classifier_plugins in the proxy config` 6. In the logs page each routed request shows cause "Custom classifier plugin" with the tier, and the models table labels the router "Custom classifier" ## Pre-Submission Checklist (optional but appreciated): - [x] I have included relevant documentation updates (stored in /docs/my-website) - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have added a screenshot or proof of the fix working locally - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] My PR passes all tests ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Backend: top-level `classifier_plugins` config key (name to dotted path), resolved at startup through the existing `resolve_classifier_plugin` load-time checks into `litellm.classifier_plugin_registry` (module global beside `guardrail_name_config_map`, since the consumer is router code that must not import proxy_server). A `mode="before"` validator on `ComplexityRouterConfig.classifier_plugin` resolves string values through the registry, so one seam covers the save-time write gate, router deployment init, and direct construction: registered names resolve, unknown names fail with a clean error naming the fix. DB-stored auto-routers therefore carry plain names and no proxy read path changes at all. `resolve_classifier_plugin` checks the registry before dotted-path import, so config files may use either form. `GET /auto_router/classifier_plugins` lists the names (admin viewer auth, names only; dotted paths stay operator-private). Dashboard: the classification method picker gains Custom classifier with a plugin dropdown fed by a `useClassifierPlugins` hook over the new endpoint, a plugin timeout field, and the fallback picker shown for both non-heuristic modes (the backend has always applied `classifier_fallback` to custom). Create and edit serialize and validate identically, including an edit-time guard cloning the create-time one so edit cannot save what create blocks. The empty-registry state disables the radio with a hint but never locks out a router already in custom mode, and a failed registry fetch never blanks a stored plugin name. The models table gains a three-way classifier label, and the routing decision card names the `classifier_plugin` cause, suppresses the meaningless score display for it, and stops claiming the LLM classifier failed on plugin fallbacks. Considered and rejected: letting the dashboard submit dotted paths directly. A register-by-path form would make the proxy import any module a dashboard admin names, which is arbitrary code execution handed to a role that cannot touch the filesystem today. The registry keeps code declaration on the operator side, matching how custom guardrail and callback code is declared. ## Feature Demo ```yaml classifier_plugins: tier-by-team: custom_classifiers.tier_by_team spend-aware: custom_classifiers.spend_aware ``` Dashboard flow for screenshots (dev server on :3000 against the rig proxy on :4474, or any proxy with the block above): 1. Go to http://localhost:3000/ui?page=models-and-endpoints, open the Add Model tab, pick Auto Router 2. Under Classification method choose Custom classifier; the dropdown lists spend-aware and tier-by-team 3. Pick tier-by-team, leave timeout at 3000, choose the fallback, fill tiers, save 4. The Auto Routers table row shows Classifier: Custom classifier 5. Send traffic, open http://localhost:3000/ui?page=logs, click a request: the routing decision card reads Custom classifier plugin with the tier ## Proof it works: live proxy Same rig pattern as the backend PR (all provider credentials on this box are still dead, so tier models point at a local recording upstream returning distinct model names; auth, save validation, registry resolution, deployment init, routing, and spend logging are the real path end to end). ### Before (merged backend only): dashboard-shaped writes are impossible ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" $PROXY/auto_router/classifier_plugins -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" 404 $ curl -s $PROXY/model/new ... -d '{..."classifier_type": "custom", "classifier_plugin": "tier-by-team"...}' {"error":{"message":"complexity_router_config is invalid at classifier_plugin: Input should be an instance of ClassifierPlugin. ..."}} ``` ### After: names list, save, resolve, route, attribute ``` $ curl -s $PROXY/auto_router/classifier_plugins -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" {"classifier_plugins":["spend-aware","tier-by-team"]} $ curl -s $PROXY/model/new ... -d '{..."classifier_plugin": "no-such-plugin"...}' {"error":{"message":"complexity_router_config is invalid at classifier_plugin: Value error, 'no-such-plugin' is not a registered classifier plugin; declare it under classifier_plugins in the proxy config. The router would drop this deployment at load time, so the write is rejected instead."}} $ curl -s $PROXY/model/new ... -d '{..."classifier_plugin": "tier-by-team"...}' created: smart-router $ curl -s $PROXY/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEARCH_TEAM_KEY" -d '{"model": "smart-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' served by claude-sonnet-5 $ curl -s $PROXY/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TEAM_KEY" -d '<same body>' served by claude-haiku-4-5 ``` Spend log attribution for those two requests: ``` classifier_plugin|REASONING|claude-sonnet classifier_plugin|SIMPLE|claude-haiku ``` ### After: restart with a name missing from the registry fails loudly Removing tier-by-team from `classifier_plugins` and restarting logs `'tier-by-team' is not a registered classifier plugin; declare it under classifier_plugins in the proxy config`, the DB-stored router is dropped, and requests to it 400 instead of silently misrouting. Restoring the entry recovers it without touching the model ## Linear ticket ## Tests - Python (725 pass in the touched files): registry name resolution, unknown-name rejection, and instance passthrough on ComplexityRouterConfig; end-to-end aclassify through a registry name; write-gate accept and reject cases; registry-first resolve_classifier_plugin; the list endpoint - Vitest (full dashboard suite: 7877 pass): new ClassificationMethodConfig suite (radio, dropdown from mocked hook, disabled-when-empty, timeout field), build and edit serialization gates including an untouched-open-and-save preservation test for classifier_plugin, submit-payload assertion, three-way row label, decision card cause and score suppression - `make check` passes (ruff, budgets, basedpyright, prettier, eslint, npm run build, API type sync) ## Caveats / follow-ups - Registration stays config-file-only by design (see Changes); the docs-site page goes to the litellm-docs repository - The routing-test endpoint keeps classifier_plugin closed off; custom-mode routing tests are a follow-up - Provider legs of the proof ran against a local recording upstream because every provider credential on this box is out of credits; the curls rerun unchanged against real providers <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 72671282dfb60d2f2757b9570e4ac26c07e98d79. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router tab, and expand Detailed Configuration 2. The Complexity Tier Configuration section shows exactly four tiers with no way to add or remove one 3. Their only options are renaming a tier or hand-writing tier_definitions in raw config and restarting the proxy After: the same form edits the tier set directly 1. They open the same tab and click Edit tiers after the Reasoning tier 2. They click Add tier, name it SECURITY_REVIEW, write the definition the classifier should route on, and pick its model(s) 3. They optionally remove Medium, pick a Fallback Tier, and see the classifier method locked to LLM with escalation and session pinning disabled 4. Submitting creates the router; the same edits work in the Edit Auto Router modal and round-trip a stored custom config without losing keys ## Relevant issues Builds on #37226 (merged), which added the backend tier_definitions/fallback_tier fields this form writes ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix UI change; screenshots to be posted from the steps below. signal.title: fix(cost): stop double-billing cached tokens that overlap a modality
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Providers report cached and image tokens as overlapping counts - Billing treats them as separate slices of the prompt - Cached image tokens are therefore charged twice - Synthetic case in the issue bills 109e-6 instead of 39e-6 How it solves it: - Cap each modality at what the cache did not cover - Billed components sum back to prompt_tokens again - Uncached tokens keep their own modality rate ## User Flow Before: a team sending image prompts with prompt caching turned on sees spend far above what the provider invoices, so their dashboard cannot be trusted for chargeback 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with an image prompt, to a provider that reports `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` as overlapping subsets of `prompt_tokens` 2. The provider serves most of that prompt from cache and reports it in `usage` 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at roughly 2.8x the price the provider actually charged 4. Sending the same prompt again makes the gap worse, because a warmer cache means more overlap After: the same request is logged at the price the provider charges, so cached image prompts get cheaper instead of more expensive 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same image prompt 2. The provider serves most of it from cache and reports the same `usage` 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the cached portion at the cache-read rate and the rest once at the ordinary rate 4. Sending it again lowers the logged spend, matching what caching is supposed to do ## Relevant issues Fixes #37281 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproducing the issue's synthetic case at cd7cdb3e3a, using a model with no explicit image rate so image tokens fall back to the ordinary input rate: ```python usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=10, total_tokens=110, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetailsWrapper( text_tokens=None, cached_tokens=90, image_tokens=80, ), ) generic_cost_per_token(model=model, usage=usage, custom_llm_provider="openai") ``` Before: ``` prompt=89.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=109.0e-6 ``` After: ``` prompt=19.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=39.0e-6 ``` The 70 tokens counted as both cached and image were previously billed at the cache rate and again at the input rate. Now the 90 cached tokens bill at 1e-7 and the 10 uncached tokens bill once at 1e-6 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Overlap is assumed maximal, since providers do not report it - Only applies when a cached or cache-creation count is present

signal.title: fix(mcp): serve token-forwarding servers when oauth discovery fails
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Token forwarding MCP servers 503 when upstream OAuth discovery fails - Clients get HTTP 200 with an empty tool list, no error - Internal APIs publish no OAuth metadata, so they never work How it solves it: - Discovery failure now blocks only gateway run OAuth flows - Forwarded token servers open sessions with no discovered endpoints - Discovery still runs, so the OAuth front door keeps its endpoints ## User Flow Before: a developer reaching a corporate MCP server through the gateway, sending their own upstream token, gets an empty tool list and no reason for it 1. Their admin registers the corporate server on the gateway in token forwarding mode, so the caller's own bearer is what that server sees 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/mcp/ with `x-litellm-api-key` for admission and `Authorization: Bearer <their own upstream token>`, asking for the tool list 3. The response is HTTP 200 with `"tools": []`, and the corporate server's own request log shows it was never contacted 4. Narrowing the same request to that one server with `x-mcp-servers` returns HTTP 503 `OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server '<name>'` 5. Every retry repeats it, because the gateway's network cannot reach the identity provider's discovery documents, and an internal API publishes none at all 6. Opening https://litellm-domain/<server>/authorize returns that same 503, so nothing says which setting is missing After: the same request returns the server's tools, and the tool call reaches that server carrying the developer's own token 1. Same registration 2. Same POST with the same two headers 3. The tool list now names the corporate server's tools 4. A tool call returns real data, and the corporate server's request log shows the developer's own bearer on the request 5. A wrong or missing token still fails: the corporate server rejects it and the developer sees the upstream 401 6. https://litellm-domain/<server>/authorize now answers HTTP 400 naming the missing authorization url and how to set it ## Relevant issues - MCP servers that forward the caller's own bearer no longer 503 when upstream OAuth discovery comes back empty - Discovery still runs for those servers, so the gateway's own authorize, token, and register endpoints keep resolving their endpoints - Interactive `oauth2` and token exchange servers are untouched and still fail closed `true_passthrough` and `oauth_delegate` mint nothing; the credential they send upstream is the caller's own bearer, and the adapter maps both onto a `PassthroughConfig` that carries no endpoint at all. The completeness gate still treated them like interactive `oauth2`, so a server stayed unresolved until discovery produced both an `authorization_url` and a `token_url`, and `ensure_oauth_metadata_discovered` raised 503 from the first statement of every client build, before the upstream was ever contacted. The single server route surfaced that 503 while the fan out swallowed it into HTTP 200 with an empty list, which is why this reads as "the tool list is just empty" with nothing in between The endpoints are not useless for these modes, which is why the exemption is not written into the unresolved check itself. The gateway's own `/authorize`, `/token` and `/register` read them, and `_resolve_ephemeral_dcr_client` mints for `true_passthrough` whatever `dcr_bridge` says. Marking these servers resolved would disarm the discovery slot and silently drop a front door that works today, so the split is by consequence instead: discovery keeps running and a failure is fatal only where the gateway runs the flow itself. Every front door site already had its own `is None` check and returns a 400 that names the missing setting, which is a better error than the 503 it replaces `MCPServer.is_client_forwarded_token` now owns the mode pair. Five call sites spelled `is_true_passthrough or is_oauth_delegate` inline, one of them already calling the result `is_client_forwarded_mode` ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both legs. One proxy on `:4611` against real Postgres, plus two real streamable HTTP MCP upstreams that each require `Authorization: Bearer upstream-ok`. Port 9101 publishes no OAuth metadata at all, every `/.well-known/` path 404s, which is what an internal API or an egress blocked endpoint looks like from the gateway. Port 9102 publishes proper RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 documents, and is there to prove discovery still enriches a forwarding server when it can reach one ```yaml mcp_servers: pbi_pass: { url: http://127.0.0.1:9101/mcp, transport: http, auth_type: true_passthrough } pbi_delegate: { url: http://127.0.0.1:9101/mcp, transport: http, auth_type: oauth_delegate } pbi_bridge: { url: http://127.0.0.1:9101/mcp, transport: http, auth_type: true_passthrough, dcr_bridge: true } pbi_oauth2: { url: http://127.0.0.1:9101/mcp, transport: http, auth_type: oauth2, oauth2_flow: authorization_code, client_id: rig-client, client_secret: rig-secret } pbi_meta: { url: http://127.0.0.1:9102/mcp, transport: http, auth_type: true_passthrough } ``` Both legs run the same script, `evidence.sh`, whose six numbered steps are the six numbered blocks below. Every request carries `x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-1234` for admission and `Authorization: Bearer upstream-ok` as the forwarded upstream token ### Before (55777d0e80) ``` 1. tools/list, scoped to one server with x-mcp-servers pbi_pass HTTP 503 {"detail": "OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_pass'"} pbi_delegate HTTP 503 {"detail": "OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_delegate'"} pbi_bridge HTTP 503 {"detail": "OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_bridge'"} pbi_oauth2 HTTP 503 {"detail": "OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_oauth2'"} pbi_meta HTTP 200 {"pbi_meta": {"status": "ok", "tool_count": 1}} tools=['pbi_meta-list_dashboards'] 2. tools/call on the passthrough server, carrying the caller's own upstream token {"detail":"OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_pass'"} [HTTP 503] 3. same tool call with a WRONG upstream token, which must not return data {"detail":"OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_pass'"} [HTTP 503] 4. OAuth endpoints the gateway resolved for each server pbi_pass auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_delegate auth_type=oauth_delegate dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_bridge auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=True authorization_url=None pbi_oauth2 auth_type=oauth2 dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_meta auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=http://127.0.0.1:9102/oauth/authorize 5. gateway OAuth front door for a passthrough server whose upstream publishes nothing {"detail":"OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_pass'"} [HTTP 503] 6. what the upstream on :9101 actually received during this leg ``` Step 6 printed nothing because the upstream received zero requests during the whole leg: the gateway never got as far as contacting it ### After (951265c18d) ``` 1. tools/list, scoped to one server with x-mcp-servers pbi_pass HTTP 200 {"pbi_pass": {"status": "ok", "tool_count": 1}} tools=['pbi_pass-list_reports'] pbi_delegate HTTP 200 {"pbi_delegate": {"status": "ok", "tool_count": 1}} tools=['pbi_delegate-list_reports'] pbi_bridge HTTP 200 {"pbi_bridge": {"status": "ok", "tool_count": 1}} tools=['pbi_bridge-list_reports'] pbi_oauth2 HTTP 503 {"detail": "OAuth metadata discovery returned incomplete metadata for MCP server 'pbi_oauth2'"} pbi_meta HTTP 200 {"pbi_meta": {"status": "ok", "tool_count": 1}} tools=['pbi_meta-list_dashboards'] 2. tools/call on the passthrough server, carrying the caller's own upstream token {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"reports for finance: [Sales, Ops]"}],"structuredContent":{"result":"reports for finance: [Sales, Ops]"},"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] 3. same tool call with a WRONG upstream token, which must not return data {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: upstream authentication required (HTTP 401)"}],"isError":true}} [HTTP 200] 4. OAuth endpoints the gateway resolved for each server pbi_pass auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_delegate auth_type=oauth_delegate dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_bridge auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=True authorization_url=None pbi_oauth2 auth_type=oauth2 dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=None pbi_meta auth_type=true_passthrough dcr_bridge=None authorization_url=http://127.0.0.1:9102/oauth/authorize 5. gateway OAuth front door for a passthrough server whose upstream publishes nothing {"detail":"MCP server authorization url is not configured. OAuth endpoint discovery against the configured server url did not resolve it; the url may be misconfigured. Check the proxy logs for 'MCP OAuth' warnings from server load, verify the server url, or set Authorization URL and Token URL manual 6. what the upstream on :9101 actually received during this leg 13 {"path": "/mcp", "method": "POST", "authorization": "Bearer upstream-ok"} 1 {"path": "/mcp", "method": "POST", "authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"} ``` A regression test drives the listing leg itself, `_get_tools_from_server`, since that is where the 503 became an empty list: a forwarding server now returns its tools from there while a gateway-run flow still raises rather than being listed as empty `pbi_oauth2` still 503s in step 1, which is the gate staying closed for a flow the gateway runs itself. `pbi_meta` keeps its discovered `authorization_url` in step 4, which is the enrichment that would have been lost had the exemption gone into the unresolved check. Step 3 shows a wrong token still failing against the upstream, so nothing fails open ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Unresolved endpoints now surface as 400 at `/authorize`, replacing the 503 - A listing spanning two forwarding servers still withholds their shared `Authorization` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 951265c18de9a9b5b3529ad8aab1e047baf83c40. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: feat(rust): route /chat/completions through the Rust core for anthropic and bedrock
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `rust: true` covers no `/chat/completions` deployment today - The Rust core has no chat completions route at all - The opt-in never even reached the chat completions handlers How it solves it: - New `chat_completions` route module in `litellm-core` - Anthropic Messages and Bedrock Converse provider transforms - Requests outside the covered subset fall back to Python ## User Flow Before: an operator who sets `rust: true` on a chat completions deployment gets nothing, with no way to tell 1. They add `rust: true` to a `claude-sonnet-4-5` deployment and restart the proxy 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model 3. The answer comes back correctly, and the response headers carry no `x-litellm-rust` 4. They repeat it against a `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` deployment and see the same, so the flag reads as broken rather than as unsupported After: the same flag serves the request through the Rust core, and says so on the response 1. They add `rust: true` to the same two deployments and restart the proxy 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the Anthropic model 3. The answer comes back with `x-litellm-rust: true` in the response headers, and the same content and token counts as the deployment without the flag 4. The Bedrock deployment behaves identically 5. They send a request carrying tools, an image, or `"stream": true`, get a correct answer with no `x-litellm-rust` header, and can tell from the header alone which requests the Rust path is serving ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5698 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. The same config serves both legs, with each provider deployed twice so the only difference between an A and a B request is the flag: ```yaml title="config.yaml" model_list: - model_name: claude-rust litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rust: true - model_name: claude-python litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: bedrock-rust litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 aws_region_name: us-west-2 rust: true - model_name: bedrock-python litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 aws_region_name: us-west-2 general_settings: master_key: sk-lit5698 ``` Both legs run against the real Anthropic API and real AWS Bedrock, on the same machine, minutes apart. `LITELLM_RUST` is exported empty on both so only the per-model flag is in play. The system prompt is chosen so the answer itself shows whether it reached the provider. ### Before (5277dab4f2) #### anthropic, `rust: true` vs no flag 1. Start the proxy at the merge base and send the flagged deployment: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-rust","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Ignore the question. Reply with exactly one word: PONG"},{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France?"}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 28 completion_tokens: 6 total: 34 ``` 2. The unflagged deployment answers identically, so the flag changed nothing: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' prompt_tokens : 28 completion_tokens: 6 total: 34 ``` #### bedrock converse, `rust: true` vs no flag 1. Send the flagged Bedrock deployment: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 29 completion_tokens: 6 total: 35 ``` 2. The unflagged one is again indistinguishable: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' prompt_tokens : 29 completion_tokens: 6 total: 35 ``` #### requests outside the covered subset 1. Tools, a multimodal image, and `"stream": true` all answer correctly and all carry no `x-litellm-rust` header, exactly like every other request on this leg ### After (5017c83484) #### anthropic, `rust: true` vs no flag 1. Send the flagged deployment: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-rust","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Ignore the question. Reply with exactly one word: PONG"},{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France?"}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: true content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 28 completion_tokens: 6 total: 34 ``` 2. The unflagged deployment stays on Python and returns the same content and the same token counts: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-python","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Ignore the question. Reply with exactly one word: PONG"},{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France?"}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 28 completion_tokens: 6 total: 34 ``` The equal `prompt_tokens` on the two legs is the parity check: a dropped system prompt would show up as a smaller count on the Rust side, and `PONG` shows the system prompt was obeyed on both. #### bedrock converse, `rust: true` vs no flag 1. Send the flagged Bedrock deployment: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-rust","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Ignore the question. Reply with exactly one word: PONG"},{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France?"}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: true content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 29 completion_tokens: 6 total: 35 ``` 2. The unflagged one matches it exactly: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'PONG' finish_reason : stop prompt_tokens : 29 completion_tokens: 6 total: 35 ``` 3. A multi-turn conversation on the Rust path keeps its history: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-rust","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"My name is Ada."},{"role":"assistant","content":"Nice to meet you, Ada."},{"role":"user","content":"What is my name? One word."}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: true content : 'Ada' prompt_tokens : 33 completion_tokens: 4 total: 37 ``` #### requests outside the covered subset 1. Tools on a flagged Anthropic deployment fall back and still return a tool call: ```bash curl -i -s http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-rust","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris?"}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : None finish_reason : tool_calls prompt_tokens : 553 completion_tokens: 53 total: 606 ``` 2. An image on a flagged Bedrock deployment falls back and still describes the image: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-rust: (absent) content : 'The image shows a very small, dark shape ...' finish_reason : length ``` 3. `"stream": true` on a flagged deployment falls back and still streams: ```bash curl -s -N http://localhost:4598/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5698' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-rust","max_tokens":32,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"count to three"}]}' ``` ``` data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"1, 2, 3"}}]} data: {"id":"chatcmpl-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]} ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats - Non-streaming only; streaming falls back to Python - Text conversations only; tools and images fall back - Bedrock covers the `converse` route, not `invoke` - Rust pre-call logging records the request before translation - Rust `post_call` carries the core's normalized response, not the provider's wire body - `rust` is a deployment setting, refused in a proxy request body - Follow-ups: tools LIT-5715, streaming LIT-5716 - Docs: BerriAI/litellm-docs#923, merge that after this ## Review notes Scope of the Rust path, and why it is drawn there. Acceptance is an allowlist rather than a denylist, so a parameter or message shape the core has never seen declines by construction instead of being translated wrong. `chat_completions_decline_reason` answers that question with no credential resolution and no I/O, which is what lets the caller emit its pre-call logging exactly once on whichever path is about to run. Covered today: system, user and assistant turns whose content is a string or all-text parts, plus the sampling parameters each provider maps. Everything else declines, including tool calls, tool results, images, extended thinking, `response_format`, prompt caching, and `topK` on Bedrock, which Python routes by base model through the model catalog the core cannot read. Parity is pinned rather than asserted. The shared conversation builder mirrors Python's `anthropic_messages_pt` for the surface it accepts: consecutive same-role turns merge, the final assistant turn is right-stripped, and empty text becomes the same placeholder Python substitutes. Converse diverges on both of those, so the Bedrock config declines blank text and any conversation that opens or closes on an assistant turn, which makes both divergences unreachable rather than papered over. `usage` folds cache tokens into `prompt_tokens` and reports the same `prompt_tokens_details` split Python does, so cost tracking agrees either way. The response deliberately carries no `id`, so the `chatcmpl-` id LiteLLM already minted survives. Bedrock signs with the credentials the Python handler already resolved, handed down through `optional_params`, rather than re-deriving them. Without that, an unrelated `AWS_ROLE_NAME` or `AWS_PROFILE_NAME` in the environment outranks explicit keys during classification and the two paths would sign as different principals. The Converse URL Python built is passed through untouched for the same reason, since Python encodes the model id itself. Two plumbing fixes were needed for the flag to work at all, both found on a live proxy rather than by reading. `rust` was absent from the key set `completion()` forwards into `get_litellm_params`, so the opt-in never reached the chat completions handlers and the gate was never consulted. Registering it as a litellm param elsewhere keeps it out of the provider body; this keeps it in `litellm_params`, where the handlers read it. Review round 1 found that a Rust failure re-entered the Python path after pre-call logging had already run, so callbacks fired twice for one request. The fix went at the root rather than at the symptom, because the same re-entry also re-issued the provider call and billed the customer twice for work already done. The bridge now separates the two cases: anything raised before the request goes out declines and the host serves it on Python, while a failure after it is surfaced as an `APIError` carrying the upstream status, which LiteLLM's exception mapping already understands. Since a decline is the same attempt continuing rather than a second one, the fallback no longer re-logs pre_call, so exactly one fires per request either way. Review round 2 caught the hole that fix left: a config reports the same error variants on either side of the provider call, so a response the core could not normalize (`MissingField`, or an unsupported content block) was being classed as a pre-send decline and retried. The handler now re-tags every error raised while normalizing a response the provider already answered, so the retryable set can only contain failures raised before the request went out. Round-trip tests drive a stub upstream and assert exactly that: a body missing `usage`, a body carrying a `tool_use` block, and a 429 all come back as errors the host will not retry, while a well-formed body round-trips. The route-owned `client.rs` was also flagged, and it is kept deliberately. It is part of the documented route template: `litellm-rust/ADDING_A_PROVIDER.md` and `crates/core/CLAUDE.md` both list `client.rs` as one of a route module's files, and `crates/core/src/messages/client.rs` is the reference implementation this mirrors. The core cannot reach LiteLLM's Python HTTP handler, which lives in the host; `core/CLAUDE.md` puts serving and transport concerns outside the core on purpose. It follows the workspace's Network I/O rules: one client behind a `OnceLock` rather than one per request, with both a connect and a full-request timeout, and rustls. Round 3 found the same lifecycle defect on the synchronous Anthropic path, which the earlier fix had only closed for the async one. It is closed the same way and pinned by three mutation checks, including one that the ordinary path still logs, so the suppression cannot swallow a log it was never meant to. Every invariant above is pinned by a mutation check: 30 mutants, 30 killed. Round 4 took the veria finding that the opt-in was request-controlled. `rust` is a litellm param, `route_llm_request` splats a proxy request body straight into the router, and the gate reads the merged `litellm_params`, so an authenticated caller could send `rust: true` and pick a transport and a callback surface the deployment never chose. A spy on the gate settled it rather than reading: driven with the kwarg it saw `litellm_params["rust"] is True`, and the control without it saw the key absent. The flag now sits in `_BANNED_REQUEST_BODY_PARAMS`, so it is a deployment decision again, liftable only by the same admin opt-in as the rest of that list, and covered under `extra_body` for free. The check runs in `pre_db_read_auth_checks`, so it also closes the same caller-controlled path on `/v1/messages`, where `_maybe_rust_anthropic_messages` has read this flag since before this PR: the same spy, driven through `litellm.anthropic_messages`, saw the caller's `rust=True` arrive there too. The responses-websocket route is not affected in either direction, since it builds its request body server-side and no caller field ever reached its gate. Deleting the entry fails three of the five new tests. One knock-on is worth naming rather than leaving to be found. `_config_base_for_health_check` reads the same list, and treats any banned param in a connection-test body as "this request describes its own connection", so it drops the configured credentials. A `/health/test_connection` body that echoes a Rust deployment's `litellm_params` verbatim now probes without them. No dashboard flow sends the field, and the Add Model wizard has no config base to drop from, so this reaches a hand-written caller only. Narrowing that set is the surgical fix if it ever bites; weakening the ban is not. The LIT002 count is resolved rather than argued, so `lint` is green. It counted twelve new dict literals. Ten of them the bridge JSON-encodes or logging callbacks consume as dicts, and `MappingProxyType` breaks both at runtime (`json.dumps` rejects a mappingproxy, and the response converter rewrites the dict it is handed), so those carry a `# mutable-ok` naming the reason: nine comments, since one line holds a nested literal. The last two went for real, by deleting the `rust_kwargs` bundles and passing the nine arguments by keyword instead. `**dict` unpacking is unchecked, so writing them out also drops twenty basedpyright errors across the three files. Round 5 is the same lifecycle defect once more, on the synchronous Bedrock path. Round 3 closed it for Anthropic by capturing the gate's answer and guarding the Python-path `pre_call` with it; Bedrock still called the gate inline, so nothing downstream could tell that the request had already been logged, and a synchronous call that the gate accepted and the core then declined logged twice. It is closed the same way, with the same comment explaining why the async branch does not need it. Two mutation checks, run separately: removing the guard fails the decline test, and inverting it also fails the control that an ordinary request with no opt-in still logs exactly once, so the suppression cannot swallow a log it was never meant to. Round 6 closed the second half of veria's original sentence, which the ban did not touch: the Rust path emitted no `post_call` at all. That is not conditional on who set the flag, so an operator's own `rust: true` lost it too, since `post_call` is raised inside the provider transform the core replaces. Measured rather than read: a `CustomLogger` on a Router deployment with `rust: true` and no request kwarg observed `['pre_api_call', 'success']` and no `post_api_call`, with the other two events as the positive control that the logger was wired and reachable. So `original_response` was unset on every Rust-served request, which OTel, Arize and two guardrail hooks read. The bridge now takes a `ResponseObserver` and calls it on success only, from both `chat_completions` and `achat_completions`, so the two paths cannot drift the way the pre_call suppression twice did. `response_logger` builds the observer, so the handlers share one implementation rather than each growing a closure, and hoisting it out of `completion` is also what keeps that function under the C901 ceiling. A decline never calls it, because the Python path that serves the request raises its own. Each hook site was mutated separately rather than both at once: dropping the synchronous one fails the two synchronous tests, dropping the asynchronous one fails only the asynchronous test, and the decline tests hold either way. The payload is the core's normalized response rather than the provider's wire body, which is the closest thing that crosses the bridge; the `/v1/messages` Rust route still has this gap and is out of scope here. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 90f4bd0e6c4e1b8d78cab1434cd4f850a2850d4c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(router): honor key-level tag filtering in pre-routing and pin auto-router e2e regressions
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Auto-router fixes shipped to the customer had no e2e regression pins - Tag-split routing, alias pricing, heuristic scope, and Responses routing could silently regress How it solves it: - 13 live-proxy pins in tests/e2e/router covering tracker items R-01 through R-07 - Coverage registry cells for every pin; the Responses pin is proven fail-before-fix - Tracker inventory maps every item to a pin, delegation, or follow-up - Fixes a router gap the CI run surfaced: request-level enable_tag_filtering, which the proxy sets from key and team router_settings, now also gates pre-routing marker capture, so the suite scopes tag filtering to its own keys instead of flipping the shared proxy's config and breaking concurrent suites ## User Flow Before: a regression in tag-split auto-routing ships unnoticed and the gateway's users see it first 1. A platform admin registers a plain deployment and a tagged auto-router marker under one model name via POST /model/new and turns on tag filtering via POST /config/update 2. A routing regression like the Aug 12 one ships in a new proxy release; no automated check exercises this setup 3. A developer sends an untagged POST /v1/chat/completions to the shared name and gets 400 "Unmapped LLM provider auto_router" instead of an answer 4. A Codex user sends POST /v1/responses with an x-litellm-tags header and hits the same 400 5. The failures surface as production incidents and support tickets before the release can be rolled back After: the same regression now fails the e2e suite by name before a release reaches users 1. The suite itself registers the same setup via POST /model/new against a live proxy and mints its keys via POST /key/generate with `"router_settings": {"enable_tag_filtering": true}`, so filtering rides only its own requests 2. It sends tagged and untagged POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, and /v1/responses requests to the shared name and reads back from the spend logs which deployment served each one 3. A release carrying the regression turns the run red, naming the broken behavior, for example the semantic auto-router Responses pin failing with the exact 400 above 4. The regression is caught in CI and users keep getting answers from the deployment their tags select ## Coverage matrix Every Fixed or Delivered item in the customer issue tracker, with where its regression protection lives. signal.title: feat(openai): add gpt-5.6 model family to registry
signal.text: TLDR The GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models were released in July 2026 but were never added to the LiteLLM model registry. Because of this: * Cost tracking returns $0 for these models. * Using `tool_choice` results in an `UnsupportedParamsError`. This PR adds all three models to the required registry files with their pricing, context window, and supported capabilities. Pricing Pricing is based on the OpenAI documentation: * gpt-5.6-sol: $5/M input, $30/M output, $0.50/M cached input * gpt-5.6-terra: $2/M input, $12/M output, $0.20/M cached input * gpt-5.6-luna: $0.20/M input, $1.20/M output, $0.02/M cached input All three models support: * 1M+ context * Vision * tool_choice * Reasoning * Prompt caching Problem LiteLLM currently does not have registry entries for these three GPT-5.6 models. As a result, LiteLLM does not have the model metadata required for pricing and capability detection. For example, when a developer sends a request using `gpt-5.6-sol` with: ``` { "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "tool_choice": "auto" } ``` LiteLLM currently returns: ``` 400 BadRequestError: UnsupportedParamsError ``` This happens because `tool_choice` is not recognized as a supported parameter for the model. Requests using these models can also appear in the LiteLLM logs with $0 spend because the pricing information is missing from the registry. What this PR changes This PR adds `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-luna` to both LiteLLM registry JSON files. Each entry includes: * Input token pricing * Output token pricing * Cached input pricing * Context window information * Vision support * Tool choice support * Reasoning support * Prompt caching support No unrelated behavior is changed. User flow before this PR A developer sends: ``` POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions ``` with: ``` { "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "tool_choice": "auto" } ``` LiteLLM returns an `UnsupportedParamsError` because the model is missing from the registry. The request can also be logged with $0 spend because LiteLLM does not know the model's pricing. User flow after this PR The developer sends the same request. LiteLLM recognizes that `gpt-5.6-sol` supports `tool_choice`, forwards the request to OpenAI, and returns the response normally. The request is also logged using the correct token pricing instead of $0 spend. Relevant issues There is currently no open issue for this. The models were released in July 2026 but were not added to the LiteLLM registry. Testing This change can be tested locally without making live OpenAI API requests because the changes are limited to model registry metadata. For example: ``` python -c "import litellm; info = litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'); print(info)" ``` Before this PR: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'))" ``` returns: ``` NotFoundError: gpt-5.6-sol not found ``` And: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.supports_tool_choice(model='gpt-5.6-sol', custom_llm_provider='openai'))" ``` returns: ``` False ``` After this PR: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'))" ``` returns the model metadata, including values such as: ``` input_cost_per_token: 5e-06 max_input_tokens: 1050000 ``` And: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.supports_tool_choice(model='gpt-5.6-sol', custom_llm_provider='openai'))" ``` returns: ``` True ``` The registry tests also pass: ``` python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai/test_gpt56_registry.py -v ``` Result: ``` 8 passed ``` Type New Feature Caveats * Pricing is based on OpenAI documentation as of August 2026 and may need to be updated if OpenAI changes its pricing. * There is no live end-to-end API test because access to the GPT-5.6 models is not universally available. Behavior before and after is identical for every request. 1. A developer sends any request through a guardrail that redacts content, for instance POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a multimodal message 2. The same fragments are redacted, the same image parts are left alone, and the same payload reaches the guardrail service 3. signal.title: fix(guardrails): take caller identity on /guardrails/apply_guardrail from auth, not the body
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Caller metadata decides identity on `/guardrails/apply_guardrail` - A caller can claim any alias or team id - Guardrails keyed on that metadata can be steered How it solves it: - Authenticated identity is layered over caller metadata - Uses the same sanitizer the in-line request path uses - Non-identity metadata still passes through untouched ## User Flow Before: a guardrail configured to treat one team differently can be talked into it by anyone 1. An admin runs a guardrail that behaves differently for a known key alias or team id, reading it from request metadata 2. A caller sends POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail with `"metadata": {"user_api_key_alias": "<the privileged alias>"}` and their own text 3. The response comes back as if the request came from that alias, so text the guardrail would otherwise act on is returned untouched After: the same request is judged on who the caller actually is 1. The caller sends the same POST with the same forged `metadata` 2. The proxy overwrites the identity fields with the ones authentication established for that key 3. The guardrail runs against the real identity, so the forged alias buys nothing, while any other metadata the caller sent still reaches the guardrail ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? The route is admin-only, so the master key is used; its authenticated alias is empty, which is exactly what has to win over the alias the body claims. ``` $ # 1) forged identity in the body $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/guardrails/apply_guardrail \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"guardrail_name":"gg-skip-alias","text":"scan me","metadata":{"user_api_key_alias":"e2e-batch-worker"}}' 200 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/_count # payloads the guardrail received {"records":1} $ # 2) the same call without the forged alias, for contrast 200 {"records":1} ``` Before this change the first call returned `{"records":0}`: the forged alias matched the exemption and the guardrail never ran. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `request_data` now always carries authenticated metadata - Callers relying on it being absent will see it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 2a7f02826f811a2bfa4e88201bea5de60d62431a. signal.title: fix(a2a): return SSE (text/event-stream) for message/stream instead of NDJSON
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - A2A `message/stream` returned `application/x-ndjson` - Official a2a-sdk client rejects that and raises `SSEError` - Guardrail stream errors were serialized twice, arriving as strings How it solves it: - Emit `text/event-stream` with `data: <json>

` framing - Matches the SSE path already used by `tasks/resubscribe` - Guardrails yield error objects; the endpoint owns serialization ## User Flow Before: a developer using the official a2a-sdk client cannot stream from an agent behind the gateway; the call dies before the first event is read 1. They point the SDK client at `https://litellm-domain/a2a/my-agent` and call the streaming send with `Accept: text/event-stream` 2. The gateway answers `200` with `content-type: application/x-ndjson` and bare JSON-RPC objects, one per line 3. The SDK raises `SSEError` complaining the content type is not `text/event-stream`, so no Task, StatusUpdate or Message event is ever surfaced to their app 4. If a guardrail blocks the stream halfway, whatever the client does receive is a quoted JSON string rather than a JSON-RPC error, so the rejection reads as unparseable output instead of a refusal After: the same client streams the agent's events incrementally and sees blocks as real JSON-RPC errors 1. They point the SDK client at `https://litellm-domain/a2a/my-agent` and call the streaming send with `Accept: text/event-stream` 2. The gateway answers `200` with `content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` and one `data: {...}` line per event, each terminated by a blank line 3. The SDK yields Task, StatusUpdate and Message events as they arrive; with `A2A-Version: 1.0` the events carry 1.0 envelopes (`task`/`statusUpdate`/`message`, `ROLE_AGENT`) 4. If a guardrail blocks the stream halfway, the final event is `data: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": ..., "error": {"code": -32603, ...}}`, which the client surfaces as an error rather than as text ## Relevant issues Fixes #35027 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against a local A2A 0.3 streaming agent, same request as the issue (`Accept: text/event-stream`, `A2A-Version: 1.0`, `SendStreamingMessage`) Shared setup, an agent registered in config.yaml pointing at an upstream that serves `text/event-stream` ```yaml general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 agents: - agent_name: my-agent agent_card_params: url: http://127.0.0.1:9999 ``` The request, used identically on both sides ``` curl -sS --no-buffer -D - -o body.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:4000/a2a/my-agent' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'A2A-Version: 1.0' \ --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"a2a-stream-test","method":"SendStreamingMessage","params":{"message":{"messageId":"msg-stream-test","role":"ROLE_USER","parts":[{"text":"Hello streaming"}]}}}' ``` ### Before (589f6859d8) 1. Run the request above; the response headers show NDJSON ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: application/x-ndjson ``` 2. The body holds bare JSON-RPC objects, one per line, with no SSE framing, so the a2a-sdk client raises `SSEError` ``` {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"task": {"id": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"statusUpdate": {"taskId": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"message": {"messageId": "m-1", "role": "ROLE_AGENT", "parts": [{"text": "Hello streaming"}]}}} ``` ### After (04e2c0d808) 1. Run the same request; the response is now SSE ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8 ``` 2. Every JSON-RPC object is framed as `data: <json>

`, so the unmodified a2a-sdk client consumes Task, StatusUpdate and Message events incrementally; the 1.0 envelope conversion still runs because the request set `A2A-Version: 1.0` ``` data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"task": {"id": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"statusUpdate": {"taskId": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"message": {"messageId": "m-1", "role": "ROLE_AGENT", "parts": [{"text": "Hello streaming"}]}}} ``` 3. Add `sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds: 1` under `litellm_settings`, restart, and point the agent at an upstream that waits 6s before its first event; the same request is now held open by comment pings and carries the anti-buffering hint, so an idle-timeout hop stops dropping a healthy stream while the agent is still thinking ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK cache-control: no-cache x-accel-buffering: no content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8 ``` ``` : ping : ping : ping : ping : ping : ping data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"task": {"id": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"statusUpdate": {"taskId": "task-1", "contextId": "ctx-1", "status": {"state": "TASK_STATE_WORKING"}}}} data: {"id": "a2a-stream-test", "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"message": {"messageId": "m-1", "role": "ROLE_AGENT", "parts": [{"text": "Hello streaming"}]}}} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_handle_stream_message` (the `message/stream` handler) now returns `StreamingResponse(..., media_type="text/event-stream")` and frames every chunk as `data: <json>

` through a small `_sse_event` helper, covering the SDK-hooked path, the raw passthrough path, and the not-installed / invalid-params / mid-stream error branches. This restores the intent of #20365 (reverted by #20446) on top of the current version-aware streaming code, and brings `message/stream` in line with the SSE framing `tasks/resubscribe` already uses through `_forward_jsonrpc_sse` The revert in #20446 carried no rationale in its description or commits, and the file has since been rewritten with version negotiation and proxy-hook streaming; NDJSON was never valid for the A2A JSON-RPC binding, so this re-applies SSE rather than reverting the revert verbatim Framing is now owned by one layer. The unified guardrail used to serialize its in-stream JSON-RPC error itself (a leftover from NDJSON, where the newline was the frame); under SSE that string would be JSON-encoded a second time and reach the client as a quoted string instead of an error object. It now returns the error as a mapping through `_a2a_jsonrpc_error_chunk`, and the endpoint's `_sse_chunk` parses any chunk that still arrives pre-serialized, so a hook emitting a JSON string cannot produce a bare-string SSE payload Both SSE routes now build their response through one `_sse_streaming_response` helper, so `message/stream` picks up the keepalive pings and buffering hint `tasks/resubscribe` already had; a slow first event no longer leaves the body idle for its whole time-to-first-token, and nothing changes until an operator sets `sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds` ## QA runbook - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_frames_events_as_sse - message/stream returns text/event-stream and frames each JSON-RPC object as one SSE event - [ ] Register a streaming A2A 0.3 agent in `agents` pointing at an upstream that serves `text/event-stream` - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `Accept: text/event-stream` and `method: SendStreamingMessage` - [ ] Expect response `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and each event on its own `data: {...}` line terminated by a blank line - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it asserts the exact media_type and `data:`/`

` framing that the a2a-sdk client validates, so reverting to NDJSON fails it - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_rejects_invalid_params_with_32602 - invalid params stream back a -32602 JSON-RPC error as a single SSE event - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `method: SendStreamingMessage` and a malformed `message` - [ ] Expect `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and one `data: {...}

` event whose body is a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it pins both the error framing and the media_type on the early-return path - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_frames_preserialized_jsonrpc_error_once - a chunk that is already a serialized JSON-RPC object is framed once, not double-encoded - [ ] Configure a guardrail that blocks mid-stream on an A2A agent - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `method: SendStreamingMessage` and content the guardrail rejects - [ ] Expect the final SSE event to be `data: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", ..., "error": {"code": -32603, ...}}`, an object rather than a quoted JSON string - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it fails if the endpoint JSON-encodes an already serialized chunk a second time, which is exactly the bug it guards - tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/unified_guardrails/test_unified_guardrail.py::TestStreamingTransform::test_emit_streaming_http_error_a2a_yields_jsonrpc_chunk - the guardrail yields the in-stream error as an object, leaving framing to the endpoint - [ ] Same live flow as above; no separate client step - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it pins the layer boundary, so re-adding `json.dumps` in the guardrail fails it - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_proxy_hook_path_frames_errors_as_sse and ::test_handle_stream_message_frames_mid_stream_failure_as_sse_error and ::test_handle_stream_message_frames_upstream_call_failure_as_sse_error - failures before and during streaming reach the client as `data:`-framed JSON-RPC errors on both the hooked and unhooked paths - [ ] Point an agent at an upstream that closes the connection mid-stream - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `method: SendStreamingMessage` - [ ] Expect the last event to be `data: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", ..., "error": {"code": -32603, ...}}` rather than a bare NDJSON line or a truncated stream - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it covers the error serializers that a2a-sdk clients parse, which NDJSON framing silently broke - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_forwards_unparseable_chunk_as_sse_event - a non-JSON chunk still leaves as one well-formed SSE event instead of killing the stream - [ ] Same live flow; no separate client step - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it pins the fallback in the chunk coercion helper - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_endpoints.py::test_handle_stream_message_pings_while_the_upstream_agent_is_still_silent and ::test_handle_stream_message_is_untouched_while_keepalives_are_unconfigured - keepalive comment frames hold a silent stream open, and the stream is unchanged while the interval is unset - [ ] Set `sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds` in config.yaml and point an agent at an upstream that waits several seconds before its first event - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `method: SendStreamingMessage` and watch the response with `curl --no-buffer` - [ ] Expect `: ping` comment frames and `x-accel-buffering: no` while the agent is silent, then the real `data:` events; with the setting removed, expect no pings and no buffering header - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it fails if the SSE response skips the keepalive wrapper, which is what let idle-timeout hops drop healthy streams - tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_a2a_version_e2e.py::test_proxy_streaming_serves_1_0_envelopes - a 1.0 client streaming through the proxy receives 1.0 envelopes over SSE - [ ] Register a 1.0-pinned agent whose upstream speaks 0.3 SSE - [ ] POST to `/a2a/<agent>` with `A2A-Version: 1.0` and `method: SendStreamingMessage` - [ ] Expect `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `data:`-framed events carrying 1.0 `message` envelopes - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey; it exercises both SSE framing and version conversion end to end ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d9b7b3a8b453454a941afbc484200770 Requested by: @yassin-berriai
