signal.title: feat(otel): attribute Prisma database spans to PostgreSQL instead of localhost
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Database work shows up in APM as `litellm-server -> localhost`. Prisma's Python client talks to a local Rust query engine over loopback HTTP, so anything instrumenting the transport (ddtrace's httpx patching, an httpx OTEL instrumentor) names the peer `localhost`, and litellm's own `postgres` span carried nothing better: `service=postgres`, `call_type=get_data`, and no `db.*` at all - An operator staring at a slow auth or budget lookup could not tell it was PostgreSQL time, and had no server address to correlate the window against the database's own metrics How it solves it: - Datastore service spans (`postgres`, `batch_write_to_db`, `redis`) now carry `db.system.name`, `db.system` and `db.operation.name`, and are emitted as `CLIENT` spans instead of `INTERNAL`, so a backend that types spans from kind plus `db.system` renders them as database calls - PostgreSQL spans also carry `server.address`, `server.port` and `db.namespace` parsed from `DATABASE_URL`. Only host, port, database and schema are read; the user, password, IAM token and every other query parameter are never touched, so no credential can reach an exporter, and no SQL text or bind value is ever attached - Both OTel paths are covered: the default v1 integration and the opt-in v2 logger share one resolver, so v2's existing `db.system.name` mapping is no longer a second copy of the same table `db.system` is dual-emitted alongside the semconv-current `db.system.name` because Datadog's OTLP intake still infers a span's database type from the older key. `db.namespace` follows the PostgreSQL semconv `{database}|{schema}` shape, with Prisma's literal default `public` schema left implicit. The match is case-sensitive: Prisma quotes the schema name, so `?schema=PUBLIC` provisions a second schema alongside `public` with its own tables, and folding the two into one namespace would report two different schemas as the same database. A DSN whose password carries an unencoded `/`, `#` or `?` truncates the URL authority, which makes `urlparse` report the username as the host and the credential tail as the path, query or fragment. Postgres drivers reject such a string outright (`P1013`, so the proxy cannot start on it), and the parser refuses it rather than deriving an endpoint from a mis-split authority: it rejects a raw database segment holding `@` or `/`, and any DSN whose userinfo `@` fell outside the netloc, which is what the `#` and `?` spellings look like. A hostless `postgresql:///litellm`, which Prisma does accept as a local-socket DSN, yields `db.namespace` with no server address instead of nothing. ## User Flow Nothing to configure. A deployment already exporting OTel spans through the generic `otel` callback, or through `arize_phoenix`, `weave_otel`, `agentops`, `levo`, `logfire` or `langtrace`, gets the attributes on its next restart. The `arize` and `langfuse_otel` callbacks deliberately no-op both service hooks (`arize.py:113`, `langfuse_otel.py:427`), so they never received DB spans and still do not. Before: an on-call engineer chasing p99 latency on the gateway sees the wait blamed on `localhost` and cannot tell it is database time 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and watch the request in their tracing backend 2. Inside the request they find a span named `postgres`, tagged only `service=postgres`, `call_type=get_data`, `table_name=combined_view`, typed as internal work 3. Their backend's service map shows the gateway talking to `localhost`, the loopback peer of the local query engine, so filtering the request by database calls returns nothing 4. They cannot line the slow window up against their database's own metrics, because no span names a database host or port After: the same span identifies PostgreSQL and the exact server, so it shows up as a database call and correlates with the database's metrics 1. The admin restarts the proxy with the same config, nothing new to set 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and open the same request 3. The `postgres` span is now typed as an outbound client call and carries `db.system.name=postgresql`, `db.operation.name=get_data`, `server.address` and `server.port` of the real database and `db.namespace` of the database it reads, with the old `service`, `call_type` and `table_name` tags still there 4. Filtering the trace by database calls returns the `postgres` and `batch_write_to_db` spans, and the address on them matches the host in their database dashboard, so the slow window can be lined up against it 5. No DSN username or password appears on any span, and cache spans still say `db.system=redis` with no database address borrowed from the Postgres DSN ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5436 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on a real Postgres, real Gemini calls, spans exported over OTLP to Langfuse Cloud and read back through Langfuse's own API. Base and head legs ran the same requests against the same database; the launcher printed `litellm.__file__` and a fix-symbol probe on each leg so the tree under test is not in doubt. Rig: ```bash docker run -d --name litfix-pg-5436 -p 15436:5432 \ -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm -e POSTGRES_USER=llmproxy -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=dbpassword9090 postgres:16 export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://llmproxy:dbpassword9090@192.168.1.244:15436/litellm?schema=public" export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel" export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="Authorization=Basic <langfuse pk:sk>" export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="litellm-server" python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config rig/config.yaml --port 20436 --use_prisma_db_push curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:20436/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gemini-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' ``` Before, the `postgres` span as Langfuse stored it. Nothing identifies PostgreSQL and there is no server to correlate against, so the only host in the trace is the query engine's loopback address: ```json { "call_type": "get_data", "service": "postgres", "table_name": "combined_view" } ``` After, the same span from the same request shape: ```json { "call_type": "get_data", "db.namespace": "litellm", "db.operation.name": "get_data", "db.system": "postgresql", "db.system.name": "postgresql", "server.address": "192.168.1.244", "server.port": "15436", "service": "postgres", "table_name": "combined_view" } ``` `?schema=public` is in the DSN and correctly does not appear in `db.namespace`. The port is the database's, not the query engine's ephemeral loopback port. Read back with: ```bash curl -s -u "$LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY:$LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY" \ "$LANGFUSE_HOST/api/public/observations?limit=25" \ | jq '.data[] | select(.name=="postgres") | .metadata.attributes' ``` Span kinds and the negative cases, captured from the raw OTLP export on the same run: ``` postgres kind=CLIENT db.system=postgresql server.address=192.168.1.244 server.port=15436 db.namespace=litellm batch_write_to_db kind=CLIENT db.system=postgresql server.address=192.168.1.244 server.port=15436 db.namespace=litellm auth kind=INTERNAL (no db.* attributes) router kind=INTERNAL (no db.* attributes) ``` With `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` set, the proxy logged `read-replica routing enabled via DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` and the endpoint attributes correctly dropped out while the system and operation stayed: ``` postgres kind=CLIENT {"call_type": "get_data", "db.operation.name": "get_data", "db.system": "postgresql", "db.system.name": "postgresql", "service": "postgres", "table_name": "combined_view"} ``` No credential from the DSN appeared anywhere in the exported payload on any leg, checked by substring search over the full protobuf-decoded export. To view the two traces in the Langfuse UI (same project, before then after): 1. https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/cmrmn6k7s00d0ad0dz7kyag1e/traces/e22670fc344a189b7c45a328e831f361 2. https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/cmrmn6k7s00d0ad0dz7kyag1e/traces/ba93049c4ea11c1ecd449e1aff43ed4f Open the `postgres` observation in each and compare the metadata attributes panel. Re-verified on a second rig, this time exporting to a local Jaeger so the spans can be read straight off the collector. Base leg at `0b82b087fd` (litellm_internal_staging), head leg at `e2980c7753`, same Postgres, same request shape, real Anthropic calls, both legs into one Jaeger instance: ``` base postgres kind=internal {call_type, service, table_name} base batch_write_to_db kind=internal {call_type, service} head postgres kind=client db.system=postgresql db.system.name=postgresql db.operation.name=get_data server.address=172.16.18.2 server.port=15436 db.namespace=litellm (call_type, service, table_name still present, span name still "postgres") head batch_write_to_db kind=client same endpoint attributes, db.operation.name=_PROXY_track_cost_callback head redis kind=client db.system=redis, no server.address (it does not borrow the Postgres DSN) head auth/router/self/proxy_pre_call/litellm_request kind=internal, no db.* or server.* ``` With `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=True` the v2 logger produced the same endpoint attributes on `postgres get_data`, `postgres get_key_object` and `batch_write_to_db _PROXY_track_cost_callback`, alongside the `litellm.service.*` keys it already emitted. With `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` set, the endpoint attributes dropped out and only the system and operation stayed. Grepping the Jaeger API export for the DSN user and password returned zero hits on every leg ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) Behavior changes worth calling out: - `postgres`, `batch_write_to_db` and `redis` service spans change span kind from `INTERNAL` to `CLIENT`. That is what lets a backend classify them as database calls; a dashboard filtering those spans by kind would need updating. Span names are unchanged on the v1 path, deliberately, so anything keyed on the name `postgres` keeps working - Three to five attributes are added per datastore span. Nothing in the repo asserts an exact attribute set on a service span, and no span-attribute limit is configured, so this is additive - `db.system` is a superseded semconv key. It is emitted for Datadog compatibility during the migration window, not as the primary The endpoint is resolved from the environment on every span rather than cached, because `DATABASE_URL` is not static: the RDS IAM refresh rebuilds it from `DATABASE_HOST` and friends on every rotation, and the DB-backed `environment_variables` overlay can rewrite those keys after startup with no blocklist covering them. One residual gap remains, and it is the inverse: that overlay changes `os.environ` without reconnecting the live Prisma client, so between the rewrite and the next reconnect a span names the newly configured server while queries still reach the old one. Naming the live connection instead of the environment would need this module to reach into the proxy's Prisma client, which is the wrong direction for a layer the SDK imports, so the window is documented rather than closed. It self-corrects at the next reconnect What this does not cover, and why the Linear reference is `Refs` rather than `Resolves`: - The ticket asks that a backend be able to separate local Prisma transport time from downstream query time. litellm's span is a single duration covering pool acquisition, the loopback hop and the query, because the query engine does not report that split back to the Python client. Making it separable needs a span around the engine call itself, which is a hot-path change I did not want to fold in here. The docs section explains how to bound it today using the APM's own transport span plus the database's query timing - When a read replica is configured, litellm names no endpoint at all rather than naming the writer. `RoutingPrismaWrapper` picks reader or writer per Prisma call, underneath the span, so naming the primary would pin replica read latency onto the wrong instance. Per-call reader/writer attribution is the follow-up - Datadog was not exercised directly; no account is available on this machine. The `db.system` and `CLIENT`-kind decisions come from Datadog's published OTLP mapping rather than from an observed Datadog trace ## QA runbook Docs PR: BerriAI/litellm-docs#869. No new env vars, so the two can merge in either order. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/934d355ed6c742249c43b0f2201ec93b Requested by: @yucheng-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 512ae259a8c456bc8f80caa51b94a1246a35bce2. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(batches): aggregate reasoning tokens and per-line pass/fail counts
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Completed batch cost/usage silently drops reasoning tokens even when the provider reports them - Nothing counts or logs how many requests inside a batch succeeded vs failed - Failures reported only in a batch's separate error file are invisible to cost tracking How it solves it: - Aggregates `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` across successful batch output lines - Counts successful/failed requests in the same single pass over the output file - Also fetches the batch's `error_file_id` (when present) and folds its failures into the count - Surfaces both new counts on the SpendLogs row the same way `batch_models` already does ## User Flow Before: a developer running a batch with a reasoning model and a mix of good/bad requests gets no reasoning-token accounting and no idea how many requests actually failed 1. They submit a 2-line batch to `POST /v1/batches` (one valid request, one with an invalid `temperature`) against a reasoning model 2. Once the batch reaches `completed`, they check their SpendLogs entry for that batch's retrieve call 3. The entry shows a real dollar cost and total token count, but nothing about reasoning tokens, and no way to tell that 1 of the 2 requests actually failed After: the same batch's SpendLogs entry tells the full story 1. They submit the same 2-line batch to `POST /v1/batches` 2. Once the batch reaches `completed`, they check their SpendLogs entry for that batch's retrieve call 3. The entry's usage now includes `reasoning_tokens` for the reasoning model's actual thinking tokens, and `metadata.batch_successful_requests` / `metadata.batch_failed_requests` correctly show 1 and 1 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real batch submitted against OpenAI (`gpt-5-mini`, reasoning model), 2 input lines: one valid request, one with an invalid `temperature: 999` to force a genuine per-request failure. No mocks; real batch job, real $ cost. Verified at the SDK layer (`litellm.aretrieve_batch` / `_handle_completed_batch`), which is where this fix lives and where both the proxy and SDK batch-cost paths converge. ### Before (973329e986) 1. Ran the completed batch through the pre-fix `_handle_completed_batch`: ``` cost: 0.00011 models: ['gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07'] usage: Usage(completion_tokens=107, prompt_tokens=24, total_tokens=131, completion_tokens_details=None, prompt_tokens_details=None) (no successful_requests/failed_requests field exists on this return shape at all) ``` 2. `completion_tokens_details` is `None` even though the completion actually used 64 reasoning tokens, and there is no way to know 1 of the 2 requests failed ### After (02cf319b48) 1. Ran the same completed batch through the fixed `_handle_completed_batch`: ``` cost: 0.00011 successful_requests: 1 failed_requests: 1 reasoning_tokens: 64 ``` 2. `reasoning_tokens` now correctly reports 64, and `failed_requests: 1` matches OpenAI's own `request_counts` (`completed=1, failed=1, total=2`) exactly - the failed line lives only in the batch's `error_file_id`, which the fix now also reads ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Anthropic/Bedrock extended-thinking batches do not get reasoning-token estimates in this PR; that requires plumbing the raw thinking-block text through a separate code path and is left as follow-up - Vertex's raw (non-default `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation`) response shape treats a null `response` field as the only failure signal, since no distinct error shape is established for that path ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ui): move the model info edit form off antd Form
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The model info edit form still runs on antd `Form` - Its cache control child reads a key nothing registers - That read throws a caught `TypeError` on the add model form - PTU rules only existed as antd validator wrappers How it solves it: - Edit form moves to react-hook-form, zod and shadcn - Cache control's live binding moves up to its parent - Antd's touched-on-change semantics are now tracked explicitly ## User Flow The edit form is a refactor, so that walk is step-for-step identical and the PR's job is to keep step 5 byte-identical while the controls underneath change. The cache control walk does change, because today it fails Before: an admin edits a deployment and the save works, but adding a cache control point logs an error 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models and click a deployment row 2. On the Model Settings tab they click Edit Settings 3. They change Input Cost (per 1M tokens) from 30 to 45 and add the tag `production` 4. They click Save Changes and see "Model settings updated successfully" 5. The deployment now reports `input_cost_per_token` 0.000045 and `tags` `["production"]` 6. On http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models they open the Add Model tab, turn Cache Control on and pick a role 7. The browser console shows `Error updating cache control points: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` and the LiteLLM Params box never picks the point up 8. They submit anyway and the deployment still stores the injection point, because the save reads the point from the form rather than that box After: the same admin does the same thing, gets the same deployment, and the console stays quiet 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models and click a deployment row 2. On the Model Settings tab they click Edit Settings 3. They change Input Cost (per 1M tokens) from 30 to 45 and add the tag `production` 4. They click Save Changes and see "Model settings updated successfully" 5. The deployment now reports `input_cost_per_token` 0.000045 and `tags` `["production"]` 6. signal.title: feat(e2e): add record/replay transport seam and fixture bundle format
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every e2e run needs a live proxy and real provider keys - Reruns bill providers again; offline re-checks are impossible How it solves it: - `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=live|record|replay` picks the transport; unset stays live - Record wraps the live transport, writing one JSON file per interaction - Replay serves recorded interactions with no proxy and no provider keys - A bundle older than seven days hard-fails collection naming its age - A passed replay that leaves recorded interactions unconsumed fails at teardown ## User Flow Before: a harness developer cannot rerun an e2e suite without a live proxy and provider keys, so every rerun bills the provider again 1. They boot the proxy and run `uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v`: 1 passed after streaming a real completion 2. They rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`: the variable is ignored, the run hits the live proxy and bills the provider again 3. They stop the proxy and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`: the run errors at setup with `No live proxy at http://localhost:33038: ... Connection refused` After: the same developer records the run once and replays it with the proxy stopped and no provider key 1. They boot the proxy and run the same command with the mode unset: 1 passed, behavior identical to today down to the terminal output 2. They rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`: 1 passed, the header names the bundle (`e2e fixture mode: record -> .../tests/e2e/.fixtures`), and the bundle holds `manifest.json` (record timestamp, harness version) plus one JSON file per HTTP interaction with auth header values redacted 3. They stop the proxy, clear `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`: 1 passed with zero traffic to proxy or provider, the header naming the recording (`e2e fixture mode: replay <- .../.fixtures (recorded 2026-08-18T21:35:35+00:00, harness 6bf535bb8f)`) 4. Once the bundle is more than seven days old, the same replay refuses to collect, naming its age: `fixture bundle at .../tests/e2e/.fixtures is stale: recorded 2026-08-08T17:00:00+00:00, age 10d4h exceeds the 7-day limit; re-record with E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record` 5. If the test later makes fewer calls than its recording holds, the replayed run passes its body but fails at teardown: `replay incomplete for llm_translation/...::test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done: 1 of 7 recorded interactions never consumed, next is get /v1/models; re-record with E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5729 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: one live proxy serves both sides (this PR only touches tests/e2e, so the proxy is identical), booted with ``` uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config lit5729_proxy_config.yaml --port 33038 ``` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 store_model_in_db: true ``` Every pytest command below runs with `LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:33038` on `tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py`, whose one test registers a model, mints a key, and streams a real OpenAI completion through the proxy ### Before (6d32d4081d) #### Mode unset (default live) 1. `uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. `test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done PASSED`, `1 passed in 15.84s`, a real completion billed #### Record mode 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. `1 passed in 18.21s`: the variable is ignored, the run bills the provider and captures nothing 3. `ls tests/e2e/.fixtures` -> `ls: tests/e2e/.fixtures: No such file or directory` #### Replay with the proxy stopped and OPENAI_API_KEY empty 1. Stop the proxy, then `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay OPENAI_API_KEY= uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. `Failed: No live proxy at http://localhost:33038: ... Connection refused`, `1 error in 0.05s` #### Stale bundle 1. No bundle or freshness concept exists: `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` with the proxy up simply runs live and bills the provider, `1 passed in 21.79s` ### After (6bf535bb8f) #### Mode unset (default live) 1. `uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. `1 passed in 16.08s` with no fixture header line: unset behaves exactly as today #### Record mode 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. Header `e2e fixture mode: record -> .../tests/e2e/.fixtures`, then `1 passed in 15.60s` against the live proxy 3. `find tests/e2e/.fixtures -type f | sort` -> ``` manifest.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0000-post-model-new.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0001-get-v1-models.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0002-post-key-generate.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0003-stream-chat-completions.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0004-post-key-delete.json test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done-2856f092/0005-post-model-delete.json ``` 4. `cat tests/e2e/.fixtures/manifest.json` -> `{"format_version": 1, "recorded_at": "2026-08-18T21:35:35.603823Z", "harness_version": "6bf535bb8f"}` 5. `grep -rh '"authorization"\|"x-litellm-api-key"' tests/e2e/.fixtures | sort -u` -> `"authorization": "<redacted>"`, and `grep -roh 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' tests/e2e/.fixtures | sort -u` finds exactly one token: the ephemeral virtual key the test minted and deleted, no master or provider key #### Replay with the proxy stopped and OPENAI_API_KEY empty 1. Stop the proxy, then `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay OPENAI_API_KEY= uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` 2. Header `e2e fixture mode: replay <- .../tests/e2e/.fixtures (recorded 2026-08-18T21:35:35.603823+00:00, harness 6bf535bb8f)`, then `1 passed in 15.03s` with the proxy dead and no provider key #### Stale bundle 1. Back-date the manifest's `recorded_at` by ten days, then rerun the replay command 2. Collection aborts: `ERROR: fixture bundle at .../tests/e2e/.fixtures is stale: recorded 2026-08-08T17:00:00+00:00, age 10d4h exceeds the 7-day limit; re-record with E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record` #### Replay that leaves recorded interactions unconsumed 1. Copy the bundle aside and pad it with one extra trailing interaction (`cp .../0001-get-v1-models.json .../0006-get-v1-models.json`), then rerun the replay command with `E2E_FIXTURE_DIR` pointing at the copy 2. The test body passes, then teardown fails it: `Failed: replay incomplete for llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py::TestChatStreamContract::test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done: 1 of 7 recorded interactions never consumed, next is get /v1/models; re-record with E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats - Replay matches per-test call order; content-based keys are LIT-5741 - Streaming chunk fidelity (LIT-5742) and provider scoping (LIT-5745) follow - CI wiring is LIT-5748; nothing runs record or replay in CI yet - Response bodies stored verbatim; the bundle stays gitignored - Record and replay make per-test unique markers deterministic so replay lines up ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/test_fixture_transport.py::TestSelectTransport::test_record_wraps_live_and_starts_a_fresh_bundle and ::TestRecordingTransport::test_passes_the_result_through_and_writes_one_file_per_call - signal.title: fix(vector_stores): stop leaking stored credentials in direct search debug logs
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Valkey vector store searches dumped their whole call state to debug logs - That dump carries connection settings, auth objects, and request headers - Any future direct (non-HTTP) vector store provider inherits the same leak How it solves it: - Direct searches now pass a synthetic `provider://vector_store_id` endpoint - Debug logs print a one-line request summary instead of the state dump - One shared helper covers both sync and async direct search paths ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin running a Valkey-backed vector store with debug logging on finds their gateway's internal call state written to stdout on every search 1. They register a Valkey store under `vector_store_registry` with `valkey_host`, `valkey_port`, and `valkey_password`, then start the proxy with `--detailed_debug` 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search with `{"query": "what is valkey", "max_num_results": 1}` and get back a normal 200 with scored matches 3. They tail the proxy log and find a single ~10,000 character line holding the store's connection settings, the resolved auth object for the calling key, the inbound request headers, and the full search response 4. Anyone with read access to those logs, including a shipped log aggregator, sees that blob on every search After: the same search logs a one-line summary and nothing else 1. Same registry entry, same `--detailed_debug` start 2. Same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search, same 200 with the same scored matches 3. The proxy log now shows `Request Sent from LiteLLM: direct vector store search: valkey://litellm-qa-docs` and no call-state blob 4. Log readers and aggregators see only the store id and provider, so nothing about the connection or the caller's key travels with the log line ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once for both sides. Valkey 8 with valkey-search on port 6390, `requirepass sup3r-s3cret-valkey-pw`, holding a real 3072-dim HNSW/COSINE index `litellm-qa-docs` with 6 documents. Embeddings come from real Vertex AI `gemini-embedding-001` calls, so each search below costs real money. ```yaml # /tmp/valkey_leak_qa_config.yaml vector_store_registry: - vector_store_name: valkey-qa-docs litellm_params: vector_store_id: litellm-qa-docs custom_llm_provider: valkey valkey_host: 127.0.0.1 valkey_port: 6390 valkey_password: sup3r-s3cret-valkey-pw litellm_embedding_model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001 litellm_embedding_config: vertex_project: vertex-check-481318 vertex_location: global litellm_settings: log_raw_request_response: true callbacks: ["langfuse"] general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-raw-request-leak ``` ### Before (2059033352) 1. Start the proxy at the merge base: ``` $ litellm --config /tmp/valkey_leak_qa_config.yaml --port 4077 --detailed_debug > /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log 2>&1 & ``` 2. Run a real search (real Vertex embedding, real Valkey KNN): ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4077/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-raw-request-leak' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":"what is valkey","max_num_results":1}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"what is valkey","data":[{"score":0.7358313202860001,"content":[{"text":"Valkey is an open source high-performance key-value datastore, forked from Redis and stewarded by the Linux Foundation.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:valkey","filename":"kb:valkey"}]} ``` 3. The debug logger emitted the entire call state as one line: ``` $ grep -c "litellm_logging.py:1232 - .*{'litellm_trace_id'" /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log 1 $ grep "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log | head -1 | wc -c 9924 ``` 4. Reading that line shows the store's connection settings, the resolved key auth object, the inbound headers, and the full response payload: ``` $ grep "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log | head -1 | cut -c1-260 15:30:54 - LiteLLM:DEBUG: litellm_logging.py:1232 - {'litellm_trace_id': '0ca033dd-3835-4772-acb7-0754e4e4c3a5', 'litellm_call_id': '2f5a003f-f39e-42fb-a59d-014775333217', 'input': '', 'litellm_params': {'acompletion': None, 'allm_passthrough_route': None, 'api_key' ``` ``` $ grep "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log | head -1 | grep -o "'valkey_host': '[^']*', 'valkey_port': [0-9]*" | head -1 'valkey_host': '127.0.0.1', 'valkey_port': 6390 $ grep "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_before_dbg.log | head -1 | grep -oc "UserAPIKeyAuth(token=" 1 ``` ### After (f6220e97f2) 1. Start the proxy at the PR tip, same config, same port: ``` $ litellm --config /tmp/valkey_leak_qa_config.yaml --port 4077 --detailed_debug > /tmp/proxy_after_dbg.log 2>&1 & ``` 2. Run the identical search, which still returns the identical result: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4077/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-raw-request-leak' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":"what is valkey","max_num_results":1}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"what is valkey","data":[{"score":0.7358313202860001,"content":[{"text":"Valkey is an open source high-performance key-value datastore, forked from Redis and stewarded by the Linux Foundation.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:valkey","filename":"kb:valkey"}]} ``` 3. The call-state dump is gone: ``` $ grep -c "litellm_logging.py:1232 - .*{'litellm_trace_id'" /tmp/proxy_after_dbg.log 0 $ grep "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_after_dbg.log | head -1 | wc -c 67 ``` 4. What the debug logger prints instead is a one-line summary naming only the provider and store id: ``` $ grep -A 3 "litellm_logging.py:1232" /tmp/proxy_after_dbg.log | head -3 15:31:43 - LiteLLM:DEBUG: litellm_logging.py:1232 - Request Sent from LiteLLM: direct vector store search: valkey://litellm-qa-docs ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Valkey is today's only direct vector store provider - Debug line format changed for direct searches only ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ui): drop @tremor/react and the theming scaffolding it needed
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Tremor has zero component imports left in the app - Its package, shim and theme tokens still ship - Its palette safelist doubles the stylesheet we serve - The date-fns overrides pin outlived its conflict How it solves it: - Drops `@tremor/react` and regenerates the lockfile - Deletes `tremor-v3-compat.css` and the `@theme` token block - Drops the safelist, cutting shipped CSS by 61% - Removes the four leftover tremor test mocks ## User Flow Before: an admin using the dashboard downloads a 512 KB stylesheet on first load, more than half of which is colour utilities no page asks for 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-requests and the page renders 2. The browser fetches the app stylesheet, 511,903 bytes across the CSS chunks 3. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=usage and every chart, badge and chip is coloured correctly 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and the Total Spend and Max Budget figures read at their usual size and weight After: the same admin walks the identical path, sees the identical pages, and downloads 200 KB instead 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-requests and the page renders the same 2. The browser fetches 200,050 bytes across the CSS chunks, a 61% cut 3. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=usage and every chart, badge and chip is coloured exactly as before 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and the Total Spend and Max Budget figures read at their usual size and weight ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5746 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signal.title: fix(ui): stop alerting settings writing unusable values into stored config
signal.text: > **Deferred, not ready to merge.** Everything here changes behaviour rather than migrating it, and the current mandate is migration with today's behaviour preserved. Parked as a draft until the behaviour fixes are picked up as their own piece of work. The branch and its tests are complete; see the known-behaviour note below ## Known behaviour this would change, measured at staging `3f15dc3287` Both of these are shipped today and are longstanding, not recent regressions: - `dynamic_form.tsx:52` sends `null` when a numeric alerting field is emptied - `dynamic_form.tsx:57` sends the whole React change event, not the typed text The `null` is the one with real consequences. `/config/field/update` stores it because `ConfigGeneralSettings` types `alerting_args` as a plain dict and never checks contents, and `SlackAlertingArgs` then rejects the stored value on every config reconcile. Reachable with an ordinary two-field edit, and it survives a reload. The change event is inert in practice. `renderControl` only reaches that branch for a `field_type` outside `Integer` and `Boolean`, and `/alerting/settings` hard-codes all nine fields to those two, so the branch never renders against a real proxy. Forced open in a test it does not corrupt anything either, because the event's circular fiber reference makes `JSON.stringify` throw before the request is built, so the save is dropped rather than written. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Emptying a numeric alerting field stored an unusable value - The proxy then rejected its own stored alerting settings on every reload - The page claimed success even when the save was refused How it solves it: - Emptied fields are dropped instead of sent as null - Both saves are awaited, and a refusal now surfaces as an error - The text control reports the typed text, not the raw event ## User Flow Before: an admin who clears a numeric alerting field silently poisons the proxy's saved alerting settings 1. Sign in and open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=settings, then the Alerting tab 2. Empty the `daily_report_frequency` box and switch `slack_alerting` on 3. Click Update Settings and see "Wait 10s for proxy to update." 4. Reload the page; `daily_report_frequency` shows its old value, so it looks like nothing happened 5. From here on the proxy log reports the saved alerting settings as invalid on every refresh, and later changes on the same page stop taking effect until the saved settings are cleared by hand 6. If the proxy refuses the save outright, the page still shows the same "Wait 10s for proxy to update." and no error After: the same edit saves cleanly, and a refusal is visible 1. Sign in and open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=settings, then the Alerting tab 2. Empty the `daily_report_frequency` box and switch `slack_alerting` on 3. Click Update Settings and see "Wait 10s for proxy to update." 4. Reload the page; `daily_report_frequency` shows the proxy default, which is what emptying it asks for 5. The proxy log stays quiet and later changes on the same page keep taking effect 6. If the proxy refuses the save, the page shows the refusal instead of claiming success ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Deferred; behaviour change, and the mandate is migration only - Backend still accepts any `alerting_args` shape; API callers can reproduce it - The text control never renders today; that part is hygiene - Saving still requires changing at least one field, unchanged ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Feature]: first-party Microsoft Agent 365 governance for MCP tool calls (pre-call authorization, post-call audit)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Ship a first-party Microsoft Agent 365 integration for the MCP gateway so that every MCP tool call the proxy makes is authorized against Agent 365 before it runs, out of the box, with nothing more than a guardrail entry (UI or config.yaml) and Entra credentials. Governance teams that standardize on Agent 365 (agent inventory, Entra Agent ID, Purview and Defender policies, and the Microsoft 365 admin center) want the gateway's tool calls to show up there like any other agent's, and today each deployment has to hand-write that bridge as a custom hook What the integration is, as confirmed with the Agent 365 team on 2026-08-13 (they demoed a working proof of concept built on the gateway's pre-MCP-call hook against a Docker LiteLLM): Agent 365 exposes a hosted REST endpoint they call "ATG Lite" (Agent 365 Tooling Gateway lite; a misnomer they acknowledged, since it is neither a gateway nor limited to tools). It is the same hook service that agents built with the Agent 365 SDK already talk to. Before executing a tool, the gateway POSTs the pending tool call to it with an Entra bearer token minted for a Microsoft-provided scope. ATG Lite runs Microsoft Defender real-time threat detection on the call (blocking prompt injection or malicious content in the tool arguments), records the call for Agent 365 observability, and returns an allow or block verdict, which the gateway enforces. Their architecture diagram, redrawn: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Local agent] -- "1 tool call" --> P[Pre-MCP-call hook] subgraph LiteLLM gateway P -- "7 allow" --> G[MCP gateway] end P -- "2 authorize" --> T[ATG Lite] T -- "6 allow / block" --> P T -- "3" --> D[Microsoft Defender] D -- "4 allow / block" --> T T -- "5" --> O[Agent 365 observability] G -- "8" --> S1[MCP server 1] G -- "8" --> S2[MCP server 2] P -. "block" .-> A ``` LiteLLM owns calls 2 and 6 (7 and 8 exist today). Calls 3, 4, and 5 are Microsoft's, run inside ATG Lite, and are nothing LiteLLM implements or sees. Microsoft's policy is not to share their proof-of-concept code, so what they will hand over is the calling pattern for the endpoint (URL, request and response payloads, and the Entra scope) plus a test tenant to validate against; the prior art they pointed at is Anthropic's [inference hooks for Claude Enterprise](https://claude.com/blog/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks), an allow/deny webhook that also runs on MCP tool calls. Every ATG Lite call is asynchronous on their side except the real-time Defender check, which is synchronous and adds latency to the tool call. They would like something a shared enterprise customer can try within roughly two weeks of that meeting Their hard requirements: turning this on must not require injecting a Python script and redeploying or restarting the gateway (their proof of concept did, and they called that out as the main adoption blocker). Ideally it is an "Agent 365" preset the admin picks on the guardrails page in the UI, or a `guardrails:` entry in config.yaml, with the Entra tenant id, client id, and client secret either read from environment variables or entered in the UI and stored encrypted. Auth is a client-credentials Entra token, the same pattern the existing Microsoft Purview guardrail uses, so it works regardless of what IdP the gateway uses for inbound auth (Okta, anything), but the customer needs an Entra tenant with an app registration that consents to Microsoft's first-party Agent 365 app; the fully non-Entra case is an open question on their side. A later step they care about is exchanging the caller's own Entra token (on-behalf-of) when the gateway's inbound auth is Entra JWT, so per-user RBAC flows through to ATG Lite the way it does for their SDK agents, but that is out of scope for the first cut Context on the Microsoft 365 admin center side, which needs no LiteLLM change: the admin center already has (in preview) Settings > Agent settings > AI gateway > "Add LLM gateway", which takes the gateway URL and admin key, discovers the gateway's MCP servers into the Tools registry (publisher = the gateway URL), lists each server's tools and the teams allowed to use it, and can toggle a team's access Allowed/Blocked, writing back to the gateway's per-team MCP permissions. That runs against the gateway's existing admin APIs. This issue is only about the tool-call authorization hook Public references for the Agent 365 surfaces involved: the [Agent 365 SDK overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk), the [Observability SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/observability), the [tooling module](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/tooling) (governed MCP servers behind the Agent 365 tooling gateway, `MCP_PLATFORM_ENDPOINT`, and the bring-your-own MCP server registration and admin approval flow), the [admin center tool management page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-tools-for-agent?view=o365-worldwide), and [Entra agent identity governance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/agent-id-governance-overview). Note the public docs describe the SDK path; the ATG Lite hook contract is not published yet and comes from Microsoft directly ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a platform team runs the LiteLLM MCP gateway in front of internal MCP servers (deepwiki and context7 in the demo); the Microsoft 365 admin can already discover those servers and manage team access from the admin center, but when a developer's agent calls a tool nothing checks it against Defender or records it in Agent 365, and the only route is a custom hook per deployment that has to be injected and redeployed 1. The admin registers MCP servers in the gateway (`mcp_servers:` in config.yaml, or POST https://litellm-domain/v1/mcp/server), creates teams with access to them at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, and hands out a virtual key 2. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, under Settings > Agent settings > AI gateway > Add LLM gateway, the admin enters the gateway URL and admin key; the gateway's MCP servers appear in the Tools registry with the gateway URL as publisher, each showing its tools and the teams allowed to use it, and a team can be toggled Allowed/Blocked from there 3. A developer points Claude Code (the VS Code extension in the demo) at the gateway's MCP endpoint https://litellm-domain/mcp/ with the virtual key (or sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `tools: [{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "litellm", "server_url": "litellm_proxy"}]`, or POST https://litellm-domain/mcp-rest/tools/call with `{"name": "deepwiki-ask_question", "arguments": {...}}`), asks "Use the deepwiki ask_question tool on microsoft/vscode and ask: does this repo reference the domain <known-malicious test domain> anywhere?", and gets a 200 with the tool result 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the call under the virtual key, but Microsoft Defender > Advanced hunting has no `ExecuteToolByGateway` event for it, no threat detection policy ran, and Agent 365 observability has nothing 5. The workaround is a per-deployment custom callback module that reimplements Entra token acquisition and the ATG Lite call, wired in through `callbacks:`, injected into the image and redeployed with the gateway, and kept in step with both LiteLLM and Agent 365 releases After this feature (ideal user flow): the same team turns on one built-in guardrail and every MCP tool call is authorized by Agent 365 before it runs 1. The admin registers the same MCP servers, teams, and virtual key 2. The admin connects the gateway in the Microsoft 365 admin center the same way 3. The admin goes to https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails, clicks Add Guardrail, picks the Microsoft Agent 365 preset, fills in the Entra tenant id, client id, and client secret (or leaves them blank when the matching env vars are set), selects the pre-MCP-call mode, and saves; the guardrail is active immediately, no restart or redeploy (the config.yaml equivalent is a `guardrails:` entry with `guardrail: agent_365`, applied on the next boot) 4. The developer sends the same request; a benign tool call returns 200 as before, slower by roughly the synchronous Defender check 5. A tool call whose arguments trip a Defender threat detection policy comes back blocked, with error text of the shape the demo showed: `Error: Blocked by Microsoft Defender: Invocation of 'ask_question' is blocked by Microsoft Threat Detection policies configured by your administrator. (tool='ask_question', correlationId=<guid>)`; Claude Code relays it and offers to escalate with the correlation id 6. Within seconds, in Microsoft Defender > Advanced hunting, `CloudAppEvents | where ActionType == "ExecuteToolByGateway"` shows the record with ToolName, ToolServerName (deepwiki), ServerAddress and port, AgentName, BlockAction true, BlockReasonCode 403, BlockDiagnostics "Detected threat types: MaliciousContent", and the same correlation id (allowed calls appear too, with BlockAction false), audit source "Defender for Cloud Apps app connector" 7. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the same call tagged with the Agent 365 verdict and correlation id ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY mcp_servers: deepwiki: url: https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp transport: http guardrails: - guardrail_name: agent-365-governance litellm_params: guardrail: agent_365 mode: [pre_mcp_call, post_mcp_call] tenant_id: os.environ/AGENT365_TENANT_ID client_id: os.environ/AGENT365_CLIENT_ID client_secret: os.environ/AGENT365_CLIENT_SECRET default_on: true ``` Env vars: `OPENAI_API_KEY` (redacted), `AGENT365_TENANT_ID`, `AGENT365_CLIENT_ID`, `AGENT365_CLIENT_SECRET` (placeholder values, the run never gets far enough to use them) Version or commit: 1.98.0, litellm_internal_staging at 6d32d4081d Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: ``` $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config agent365_config.yaml --port 24942 INFO: Waiting for application startup. ... File ".../litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 5361, in load_config init_guardrails_v2( File ".../litellm/proxy/guardrails/init_guardrails.py", line 29, in init_guardrails_v2 initialized_guardrail = IN_MEMORY_GUARDRAIL_HANDLER.initialize_guardrail( File ".../litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_registry.py", line 503, in initialize_guardrail raise ValueError(f"Unsupported guardrail: {guardrail_type}") ValueError: Unsupported guardrail: agent_365 ERROR: Application startup failed. Exiting. ``` What stopped me there: step 3 of the ideal flow dead-ends. There is no built-in `agent_365` guardrail, so the proxy refuses the config with `Unsupported guardrail: agent_365`, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails has no Agent 365 preset to pick. The Agent 365 team's own proof of concept got past this only by injecting a Python script into the image and redeploying, which is exactly what they want gone ### What a fix PR should look like A first-party guardrail under `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/agent_365/` registered as `agent_365` (a `SupportedGuardrailIntegrations` member plus the initializer and class registry entries in the package's `__init__.py`, mirroring `microsoft_purview/__init__.py`), built on the pre-MCP-call seam that already exists: the `MCPPreCallRequestObject` / `MCPPreCallResponseObject` contract, so it can block with `should_proceed=False` and ATG Lite's block message (the client then sees the same "Blocked by Microsoft Defender ..." text with the correlation id), the same shape as the Cisco AI Defense MCP mixin in `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/cisco_ai_defense/cisco_ai_defense_mcp.py`. That is calls 2 and 6 and it is the whole first cut. `during_mcp_call` and the post-call seams (`async_post_mcp_tool_call_hook`, `post_mcp_call`) stay out unless Microsoft's calling pattern asks for a post-execution report; observability happens inside ATG Lite from the pre-call, so the SDK's `ExecuteToolScope` span exporter path is not needed here Payload: whatever Microsoft's calling pattern specifies once they share it; expect at least the tool name, MCP server name and URL, the arguments, and the caller identity (virtual key alias, user id, team) plus the gateway's agent identity, with a response carrying an allow/block verdict, a block reason and message, and a correlation id. Since it is a preview endpoint, take the endpoint URL as a config field with a default (`api_base`) so preview and sovereign-cloud URLs work without a release Auth: a client-credentials token from `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token` for the scope Microsoft provides, cached until expiry, exactly what `microsoft_purview/base.py` `_get_access_token` does today, so extract that into a shared helper both guardrails use rather than a third copy or a second MSAL flow, and support the workload identity path (federated credential or managed identity) that `litellm/llms/azure/common_utils.py` already handles for Azure model calls, for AKS deployments without secrets. The `incoming_bearer_token` the MCP pre-call path already exposes to guardrails is the hook for the later on-behalf-of user-token exchange UI: a `GuardrailConfigModel` returned from `get_config_model()` with `ui_friendly_name` "Microsoft Agent 365", so it shows up as a preset at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails via `/guardrails/ui/provider_specific_params`; `POST /guardrails` already hot-initializes DB guardrails, which is what satisfies Microsoft's no-restart requirement Latency and failure: the real-time Defender check is synchronous, so a `timeout` in seconds and `fail_open` (default false, so a governance outage blocks rather than silently allows), with the verdict, correlation id, and check latency recorded on the request's metadata so the logs page can show them Config surface: `guardrail: agent_365` with `tenant_id`, `client_id`, `client_secret` (or `use_workload_identity`), `api_base`, optional `agent_id`, `timeout`, and `fail_open`, all accepting `os.environ/` references, plus the usual `mode` and `default_on`. Docs: a new page next to `docs/mcp_guardrail.md` in the docs repo covering setup, the Entra app registration and consent steps, and what shows up in Defender advanced hunting and the Microsoft 365 admin center, linked from the MCP guardrails page and the guardrails index. Tests: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/agent_365/test_agent_365.py` covering allow, block, timeout, and fail-closed against a stubbed HTTP boundary (dependency-injected client, no monkeypatching) plus token acquisition, and a live proof in the test tenant Microsoft provides showing the `ExecuteToolByGateway` record in Defender advanced hunting. Out of scope: registering the gateway itself as an Agent 365 agent (a one-time Entra blueprint step admins do with the a365 CLI), the admin center gateway discovery (works today via the admin key), the on-behalf-of user-token exchange (follow-up), and non-MCP tool calls ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(mcp): attach per-user BYOK credential when listing tools for non-oauth2 auth types
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - BYOK servers on non-oauth2 auth types list zero tools - tools/call then fails with "Tool not found", not 401 How it solves it: - list path now injects the stored per-user BYOK credential - mirrors the `is_byok` gate the tool-call path already uses ## User Flow Before: a user who stored their own key for a BYOK MCP server sees no tools at all through the gateway, so their agent can never call one 1. In the dashboard they open their BYOK server and store their personal key, and the server shows the credential as connected 2. Their MCP client connects to `POST http://localhost:4000/mcp/` with their virtual key and sends `tools/list` 3. The response is `200` with `"tools": []` and `"litellm.ai/server_outcomes": {"<server>": {"status": "auth_required", "http_status": 401}}`, so the client shows no tools 4. Calling the tool by name anyway comes back as "Tool not found" rather than an auth error, so nothing hints that the stored key was never sent After: the same `tools/list` returns the server's tools and the tool runs with that user's own key 1. Same setup, the credential is stored and shows as connected 2. Same `tools/list` through `POST http://localhost:4000/mcp/` with the same virtual key 3. The response now lists the server's tools, prefixed by server name 4. `tools/call` on a listed tool returns real upstream results, billed to that user's own key ## Relevant issues Fixes #34786 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, same live proxy on `localhost:4000` with Postgres and `store_model_in_db: true`, and a real streamable-HTTP MCP server on `127.0.0.1:9100` that wraps a live web-search API and rejects any request whose `X-API-Key` is missing or wrong with `401 {"error": "unauthorized"}` 1. Register it as BYOK with a non-oauth2 auth type and no server-level credential ``` curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"server_name": "byok_exa", "alias": "byokexa", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9100/mcp/", "transport": "http", "auth_type": "api_key", "is_byok": true}' ``` 2. Create a non-admin user plus a virtual key for them, then store that user's own upstream key ``` curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server/$SERVER_ID/user-credential" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"api_key": "'"$UPSTREAM_KEY"'"}' {"server_id":"9cc43514-...","has_credential":true} ``` 3. `list_tools.sh` runs the MCP client handshake with that user's virtual key (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`) and prints the tool count; `call_tool.sh` sends `tools/call` for the listed tool ![before and after tools/list and tools/call through the gateway](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..RB1VbOeUsj_V4gUHXJYr3mfj5-2ZShUN9e8HCLXrIKI) ![dashboard MCP server with the per-user BYOK credential connected](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..sO6FmD7okhlK0fNetuFHatd95ZjM5fQpu7lkf-fAgbA) ### Before (6c4059aacc) 1. `./list_tools.sh` ``` tool count: 0 payload: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": {"_meta": {"litellm.ai/server_outcomes": {"byokexa": {"status": "auth_required", "http_status": 401}}}, "tools": []}} ``` 2. The upstream logs the discovery attempt as `401` because the stored key never left the gateway ### After (3f7db4afef) 1. `./list_tools.sh` ``` tool count: 1 - byokexa-exa_search ``` 2. `./call_tool.sh` ``` MCP Overview - LiteLLM -- https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp Using your MCP - LiteLLM -- https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp_usage MCP Server Usage | liteLLM -- https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp_servers ``` 3. The upstream logs both the discovery and the search as `200`, and the search results come from the live provider, not a fixture ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_fetch_and_filter_server_tools` in the aggregate list path only resolved a per-user credential when `auth_type == oauth2`, so a BYOK server declaring `authorization` / `bearer_token` / `api_key` / `basic` / `token` connected upstream with no credential at all, got a 401, and the aggregator's fail-open `except MCPUpstreamAuthError: return []` silently dropped it; `execute_mcp_tool` gates on `is_byok` instead and was already correct, so the tool never even got registered for a later call. The list path now resolves the stored credential the same way: ```python if server.is_byok and server.auth_type != MCPAuth.oauth2 and server_auth_header is None: server_auth_header = await _get_byok_credential(server, user_api_key_auth) ``` oauth2 BYOK keeps its existing per-user token path, and a request that already carries a per-server auth header still wins. When no credential is stored the behavior is unchanged (the server is omitted from the aggregate listing rather than failing the whole list), matching how the fan-out handles every other unauthenticated server. Test is parametrized over the five non-oauth2 auth types and asserts the credential reaches `_get_tools_from_server`; all five fail on the parent commit and pass with the fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only the MCP protocol list path, not the dashboard REST one - Dashboard MCP Tools tab still shows a fetch error - #30180 fixes both paths and supersedes this ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f4699e222aab44d5a016abc259d9f19b Requested by: @yucheng-berri

signal.title: [Bug] BYOK MCP servers with non-oauth2 auth_type never list tools (per-user credential not checked in tools/list)
signal.text: ### What happened A BYOK-enabled MCP server (`is_byok: true`) using a non-`oauth2` `auth_type` (e.g. `authorization`, `bearer_token`, `api_key`, `basic`, `token`) never surfaces its tools. The per-user credential is stored successfully (`has_user_credential: true`), but `tools/list` always returns empty for that server, and a subsequent `tools/call` by name fails with "Tool not found" — never even reaching the (correctly BYOK-aware) tool-call auth resolution. ### Why it matters BYOK only actually works end-to-end for `auth_type: oauth2` servers. Any BYOK server configured with a simpler auth type (which is the natural choice when the upstream just wants a raw `Authorization`/`X-API-Key` header, e.g. Elastic's Kibana Agent Builder MCP, which requires `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) silently never lists its tools for any user, making BYOK effectively non-functional outside the OAuth2 case. ### Root cause (traced in `v1.93.0`) Two code paths resolve per-user MCP credentials, and they're inconsistently gated: - **`MCPServerManager.call_tool`** (`litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py`, calls `_resolve_byok_mcp_auth_header`) — gated purely on `server.is_byok`. Correct, auth_type-agnostic. - **`_fetch_and_filter_server_tools`** (`litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py`, the `tools/list` aggregation path) — its per-user credential injection is gated to `server.auth_type == MCPAuth.oauth2` in both branches: ```python if ( not migrated_to_v2 and server.auth_type == MCPAuth.oauth2 and getattr(server, "needs_user_oauth_token", False) and user_api_key_auth is not None ): db_headers = await _get_user_oauth_extra_headers_from_db(...) ... elif not migrated_to_v2 and extra_headers is None and server.auth_type == MCPAuth.oauth2: extra_headers = await _get_user_oauth_extra_headers_from_db(...) ``` Neither branch checks `server.is_byok`. For a BYOK server with e.g. `auth_type: authorization`, no credential is attached, litellm connects to the upstream with no auth at all, gets a real `401`, and the multi-server aggregator's fail-open handling (`except MCPUpstreamAuthError: return []`) silently absorbs it — so the tool is never registered under any name, and a later `tools/call` fails with "Tool not found" rather than an auth error. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Register an MCP server with `is_byok: true` and `auth_type: "authorization"` (or `bearer_token`/`api_key`/`basic`/`token`), no server-level `credentials`. 2. As a non-admin user, connect via the UI's BYOK "Connect" flow and submit a personal API key — confirm `GET /v1/mcp/server` shows `has_user_credential: true` for that user. 3. Call `GET /v1/mcp/tools` (or the server's own `/{server_name}/mcp` `tools/list`) as that same user — the server contributes zero tools. 4. Call `POST /mcp-rest/tools/call` for a known tool name on that server — fails with "Tool ... not found", not an auth error. ### Suggested fix In `_fetch_and_filter_server_tools`, extend the credential-injection condition to also cover BYOK servers, e.g. `server.auth_type == MCPAuth.oauth2 or server.is_byok`, mirroring the gate already used correctly in `_resolve_byok_mcp_auth_header`/`call_tool`.

signal.title: perf(db): index LiteLLM_SpendLogs on (api_key, startTime)
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Logs tab key filter has no supporting index - Every page turn full-scans the whole date window - Pegged a customer's Aurora writer at 99.7% CPU How it solves it: - Adds an `(api_key, startTime DESC)` index on `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` - Plain build, so partitioned deployments can migrate too - Partition and unpartition runbooks carry the index ## User Flow Before: an admin filtering the Logs tab by a virtual key waits seconds per page, and the database CPU climbs the whole time 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and pick a 6 month date range 2. They paste a virtual key into the Key Hash filter and hit Search 3. The table spins before the first 50 rows land 4. They click through to page 2, then page 3, and each click costs the same wait again 5. The database CPU stays pinned for as long as they keep paging, and every other request through the proxy slows down with it After: the same filter returns quickly, and paging no longer moves database CPU 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and pick the same 6 month date range 2. They paste the same virtual key into the Key Hash filter and hit Search 3. The first 50 rows land immediately 4. Page 2 and page 3 land just as fast 5. Database CPU is flat throughout, so other traffic through the proxy is unaffected Operators who run spend logs as a partitioned table get the same result. On the previous revision of this PR their upgrade stopped instead: `prisma migrate deploy` failed with `cannot create index on partitioned table "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" concurrently` and the proxy never came up on the new version. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5767 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This one is not visible through a proxy response body, since the change is a query plan plus whether the migration can be applied at all. Both sides below run against Postgres 14 with the committed migrations applied and 300,000 spend log rows over 180 days across 500 distinct keys, once on a plain table and once on a table converted with `db_scripts/partition_spend_logs.sql`. Shared setup, run once per database before each capture: ```bash prisma migrate deploy --schema schema.prisma psql -c " INSERT INTO \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" (request_id, call_type, api_key, spend, total_tokens, \"startTime\", \"endTime\", model) SELECT 'req-'||g, 'acompletion', 'hash-'||(g % 500), 0.01, 100, now() - (interval '180 days') * (g::float/300000), now() - (interval '180 days') * (g::float/300000) + interval '2 seconds', 'gpt-5.6' FROM generate_series(1,300000) g;" psql -c 'VACUUM (ANALYZE) "LiteLLM_SpendLogs";' ``` The paged select below is what the Logs tab issues for one key over the window: ```bash psql -c " EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, COSTS OFF) SELECT request_id, api_key, spend, \"startTime\" FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" WHERE \"startTime\" >= now() - interval '180 days' AND \"startTime\" <= now() AND api_key = 'hash-42' ORDER BY \"startTime\" DESC LIMIT 50 OFFSET 400;" ``` ### Before (c6fad3683d for the query plans, ab3bcb95ef for the migration) #### Migration on a partitioned LiteLLM_SpendLogs 1. Convert the table with the runbook, then apply the statement this PR shipped in its previous revision: ```bash psql -f db_scripts/partition_spend_logs.sql psql -c 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_api_key_startTime_idx" ON "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"("api_key", "startTime" DESC);' ``` 2. Postgres refuses it, so `prisma migrate deploy` aborts and the upgrade stops: ``` ERROR: cannot create index on partitioned table "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" concurrently ``` #### Logs tab paged select, plain table 1. Run the paged select above against the merge base schema, which has no api_key led index 2. It parallel seq-scans and sorts, discarding 99,800 rows per worker over 5,531 buffers: ``` Limit (actual time=11.894..15.026 rows=50 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=5531 -> Gather Merge (actual time=11.820..15.007 rows=450 loops=1) Workers Planned: 2 Workers Launched: 2 -> Sort (actual time=10.257..10.265 rows=183 loops=3) Sort Key: "startTime" DESC Sort Method: quicksort Memory: 42kB Buffers: shared hit=5531 ``` #### Logs tab paged select, partitioned table 1. Run the same paged select against the partitioned shape without the new index 2. Same full scan, this time on the partition: ``` Limit (actual time=11.401..14.404 rows=50 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=5406 read=125 -> Gather Merge (actual time=11.324..14.383 rows=450 loops=1) -> Sort (actual time=9.845..9.854 rows=184 loops=3) Sort Key: "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"."startTime" DESC -> Parallel Seq Scan on "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_pdefault" "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" (actual time=0.024..9.762 rows=200 loops=3) Filter: ((api_key = 'hash-42'::text) AND ("startTime" <= now()) AND ("startTime" >= (now() - '180 days'::interval))) Rows Removed by Filter: 99800 Planning Time: 0.492 ms Execution Time: 14.442 ms ``` ### After (85c5153aec) #### Migration on a partitioned LiteLLM_SpendLogs 1. Apply the migration file this PR ships to the converted table: ```bash psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f litellm-proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations/20260818000000_add_spendlogs_api_key_start_time_idx/migration.sql ``` 2. It succeeds, and the index lands on the partitioned parent so every current and future partition inherits it: ``` CREATE INDEX ``` ``` relkind | relname ---------+-------------------------------------------- p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_pkey p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_startTime_idx p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_startTime_request_id_idx p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_end_user_idx p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_session_id_idx p | LiteLLM_SpendLogs_api_key_startTime_idx ``` 3. A full `prisma migrate deploy` on an empty database still ends clean, and `prisma migrate diff --from-schema-datamodel schema.prisma --to-migrations litellm-proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations` reports no drift: ``` All migrations have been successfully applied. No difference detected. ``` #### Logs tab paged select, plain table 1. Run the same paged select 2. It reads only the matching rows, 458 buffers and 1.4 ms, with nothing removed by filter: ``` Limit (actual time=1.239..1.368 rows=50 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=453 read=5 -> Index Scan using "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_api_key_startTime_idx" on "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" (actual time=0.038..1.349 rows=450 loops=1) Index Cond: ((api_key = 'hash-42'::text) AND ("startTime" >= (now() - '180 days'::interval)) AND ("startTime" <= now())) Buffers: shared hit=453 read=5 Planning Time: 0.398 ms Execution Time: 1.399 ms ``` #### Logs tab paged select, partitioned table 1. Run the same paged select 2. The inherited partition index is used, 455 buffers and 1.4 ms: ``` Limit (actual time=1.191..1.327 rows=50 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=449 read=6 -> Index Scan using "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_pdefault_api_key_startTime_idx" on "LiteLLM_SpendLogs_pdefault" "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" (actual time=0.031..1.311 rows=450 loops=1) Index Cond: ((api_key = 'hash-42'::text) AND ("startTime" >= (now() - '180 days'::interval)) AND ("startTime" <= now())) Buffers: shared hit=449 read=6 Planning Time: 0.509 ms Execution Time: 1.357 ms ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Index costs roughly 1.5 to 2 GB per 44 GB table - Adds write amplification on the hottest insert path - The build takes a write lock for its duration, so operators who cannot pause spend-log inserts should pre-build the index before upgrading, CONCURRENTLY on a plain table or per partition plus ATTACH on a partitioned one; the migration then no-ops on the index name - Logs tab `team_id`, `user`, `model` filters remain unindexed ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/602728dfb5fe4ffeb35eba62bdff3ad9
