signal.title: refactor(ui): move the admin, SSO, SCIM, alerting and fallback forms off tremor
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nine admin screens still render through `@tremor/react` - Tremor is being removed, so these files block it - Their `no-restricted-imports` suppressions stay stale meanwhile How it solves it: - Swaps tremor primitives for the shadcn layer - Keeps antd forms, modals and selects untouched - Prunes the nine tremor import suppressions these files carried - Fixes the three parity traps the mechanical mapping introduced - Alerting alignment, the CloudZero key reveal toggle, the SCIM divider gap ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin configures Okta SSO and reviews the SCIM and alerting screens, and every control on those pages is drawn by tremor 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=admin-panel and land on the SSO Settings tab 2. They press Configure SSO, pick Okta / Auth0 in the provider dropdown and tick Use Role Mappings, and the modal fills with client, endpoint, scope and team fields 3. They close the modal, switch to Security Settings and see the security card, the three action buttons and the teal "Login without SSO" callout 4. They press Allowed IPs and read the allowed address table inside the modal 5. They press UI Access Control, pick Restricted SSO Group and get the group name field 6. They switch to the SCIM tab and copy the SCIM tenant URL, then read the "Using SCIM" callout above the token form 7. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logging-and-alerts, switch to Alerting Settings and read each setting name, its value box and its In DB or In Config chip 8. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=router-settings, switch to Fallbacks and press Add Fallbacks to configure a chain 9. If they reach the CloudZero export modal, they paste an API key into a masked field and press its reveal toggle to check what they pasted After: the same admin walks the same steps and sees the same screens, now drawn by the shadcn layer 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=admin-panel and land on the SSO Settings tab 2. They press Configure SSO, pick Okta / Auth0 in the provider dropdown and tick Use Role Mappings, and the modal fills with the same client, endpoint, scope and team fields 3. They close the modal, switch to Security Settings and see the same security card, the same three action buttons and the same "Login without SSO" notice, now in the shared blue info style 4. They press Allowed IPs and read the same allowed address table inside the modal 5. They press UI Access Control, pick Restricted SSO Group and get the same group name field 6. They switch to the SCIM tab and copy the same SCIM tenant URL, then read the same "Using SCIM" notice above the token form 7. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logging-and-alerts, switch to Alerting Settings and read the same setting names, value boxes and chips, with the per-row reset control now fitting on screen at 1440px instead of being pushed past the right edge 8. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=router-settings, switch to Fallbacks and press Add Fallbacks to configure a chain exactly as before 9. The CloudZero API key field still masks what they paste and still reveals it on the toggle, now drawn by the shared PasswordInput control instead of tremor ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5746 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides were captured against the same live proxy and the same database, with the dashboard dev server pointed at it. The side by side composites for every case live on the `litellm_shadcn_tremor_admin_0817_screenshots` branch as `<case>.png`. ### Before (4d57bf0bdd) #### admin_security_settings 1. Open /admin-panel and click the Security Settings tab 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_admin_0817_screenshots/admin_security_settings__before.png) #### admin_allowed_ips_modal 1. From Security Settings, click Allowed IPs 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_admin_0817_screenshots/admin_allowed_ips_modal__before.png) #### admin_ui_access_control_modal 1. From Security Settings, click Add SSO, pick Okta / Auth0 and tick Use Role Mappings 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_admin_0817_screenshots/admin_add_sso_modal__before.png) #### admin_scim_tab 1. Open /admin-panel and click the SCIM tab 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_admin_0817_screenshots/admin_scim_tab__before.png) #### admin_sso_settings_modal 1. signal.title: fix(bedrock): add cost map entries for gpt-5.6 on Bedrock Converse
signal.text: ## Problem The gpt-5.6 family (luna / sol / terra) is registered in the cost map **only** as `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*`. Calling these models over the regular Bedrock Converse route silently loses tool calling and reasoning. That route matters because `bedrock_mantle` authenticates with a Bearer Bedrock API key, while `bedrock/converse/...` goes through SigV4 and honours `aws_role_name`. Anyone doing cross-account role assumption (per-tenant billing, tag routing) has to use the Converse route. ## Root cause `AmazonConverseConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` appends `tools` only when `base_model` starts with `anthropic`/`mistral`/`cohere`/`meta.llama3-1|3-2|3-3`/`meta.llama4`/`amazon.nova`, or when `supports_function_calling()` resolves True from the cost map. `BedrockModelInfo.get_base_model("bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna")` returns `openai.gpt-5.6-luna`, which matches no prefix and has no cost map entry. So `tools`, `tool_choice`, `thinking` and `reasoning_effort` are all excluded, and with `drop_params: true` the request returns 200 with the model answering as if no tools were offered. Reproduced on 1.97.0: ```python from litellm.llms.bedrock.chat.converse_transformation import AmazonConverseConfig p = AmazonConverseConfig().get_supported_openai_params(model="bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna") "tools" in p # False "reasoning_effort" in p # False ``` Through a proxy, `tool_choice: "required"` also gets dropped: `finish_reason` comes back `stop` with `tool_calls: null`, while `claude-sonnet-5` with the identical schema returns `finish_reason: tool_calls`. This is not a Bedrock limitation. A direct call works: ``` aws bedrock-runtime converse --model-id us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna \ --messages '[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"..."}]}]' \ --tool-config file://tools.json # stopReason: tool_use ``` ## Fix Adds bare, `us.` and `global.` prefixed entries with `litellm_provider: bedrock_converse` and `mode: chat`. This matches how every other Bedrock model is keyed, including `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` and the existing `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` entries. Pricing mirrors the published `bedrock_mantle/` values, including the above-272k tiers and cache costs. Data-only change. No logic touched, and the existing `bedrock_mantle/` entries are unchanged, so the Responses-path behaviour is unaffected. ## Verification With the patched map on 1.97.0: | model | tools | tool_choice | reasoning_effort | |---|---|---|---| | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | `get_model_info()` resolves `litellm_provider: bedrock_converse`, `mode: chat`, and the correct per-token pricing. Both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup are kept in sync. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: fix(cost_calculator): recognize the ultrafast service tier in cost calculation
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `service_tier: "ultrafast"` was unknown to cost calculation - Ultrafast usage was silently billed at standard rates - `*_ultrafast` pricing keys in config broke requests entirely How it solves it: - Adds `ultrafast` to the known service tiers - Resolves `*_ultrafast` cost keys, falling back to standard when absent - Accepts `*_ultrafast` custom pricing keys in deployment litellm_params - Regenerates dashboard schema.d.ts for the new pricing fields ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin cannot bill ultrafast traffic correctly, and configuring ultrafast prices breaks the deployment 1. The admin adds `input_cost_per_token_ultrafast` and `output_cost_per_token_ultrafast` to a model in the proxy config 2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"service_tier": "ultrafast"` 3. The request fails with 400 `input_cost_per_token_ultrafast: Extra inputs are not permitted` 4. If the admin removes those keys, the same request succeeds but `x-litellm-response-cost` shows the standard rate, undercharging ultrafast usage After: the same config bills ultrafast traffic at ultrafast rates 1. The admin adds `input_cost_per_token_ultrafast` and `output_cost_per_token_ultrafast` to a model in the proxy config 2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"service_tier": "ultrafast"` 3. The response returns 200 and `x-litellm-response-cost` reflects the ultrafast rates 4. The same request without `service_tier` is still billed at standard rates ## Relevant issues Fixes #37326 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5750 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? OpenAI rejects `service_tier: "ultrafast"` for accounts not enrolled in the limited preview, so the live run uses a Bedrock deployment with custom ultrafast pricing, which exercises the same tier cost resolution ```yaml model_list: - model_name: ultrafast-demo litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 input_cost_per_token: 1e-06 output_cost_per_token: 5e-06 input_cost_per_token_ultrafast: 1e-05 output_cost_per_token_ultrafast: 5e-05 cache_read_input_token_cost_ultrafast: 5e-07 cache_creation_input_token_cost_ultrafast: 1.25e-05 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (ceeab01b0d) #### Standard /v1/chat/completions (no service_tier) 1. `curl -sD - -X POST http://localhost:21729/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"ultrafast-demo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi in one word"}],"max_tokens":16}'` 2. Observed: `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0`, body `litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"The model returned the following errors: cache_creation_input_token_cost_ultrafast: Extra inputs are not permitted"}`; the unrecognized pricing keys leak into the provider request and break the deployment even without a tier #### Ultrafast /v1/chat/completions 1. Observed: identical `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request` with `cache_creation_input_token_cost_ultrafast: Extra inputs are not permitted` #### Ultrafast /v1/messages 1. `curl -sD - -X POST http://localhost:21729/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"ultrafast-demo","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi in one word"}],"service_tier":"ultrafast"}'` 2. Observed: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 3.2000000000000005e-05` for 12 input and 4 output tokens, the standard rate (12 * 1e-06 + 4 * 5e-06); ultrafast would be 3.2e-04, so this route does not leak the keys but still bills the tier at standard ### After (e67373304d) #### Standard /v1/chat/completions (no service_tier) 1. Same curl as before 2. Observed: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 3.2000000000000005e-05` for 12 input and 4 output tokens, the standard rate; see the observations below #### Ultrafast /v1/messages 1. Same curl as before 2. Observed: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 3.7000000000000005e-05` for 12 input and 5 output tokens, the standard rate; see the observations below QA observations (control runs with `service_tier: "flex"` on the same Bedrock model, plus an OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` deployment with custom flex pricing): - Bridged /v1/responses and /v1/messages ignore request-side tiers for billing - Flex control bills standard at both commits: pre-existing, left alone - OpenAI-native flex bills correctly on all three endpoints (tier echoed) - /v1/messages never leaked pricing keys, no breakage there, left alone - Bedrock rejects forwarded flex on chat completions: unrelated, left alone ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - OpenAI has not published numeric ultrafast rates yet - So no `*_ultrafast` prices were added to the model registry - Registry rates can be added once OpenAI publishes them - Until then, deployments can set custom `*_ultrafast` pricing - Without ultrafast keys, cost still falls back to standard rates - Bridged responses/messages ignore request-side tiers for billing, pre-existing - Price-map schema test needs ultrafast keys when registry rates land - Docs custom-pricing pages don't list the ultrafast suffixes yet ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/14bc0a0ff7da4d3b862f7e785e4ed9eb Requested by: @mateo-berri - [x] e67373304da5985fe2f813b7f24ac8aa3c132d27 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: [Feature]: Support OpenAI's new "ultrafast" service_tier in cost calculation
signal.text: ### The Feature OpenAI recently launched a new `service_tier` value, `"ultrafast"`, for the Responses/Chat Completions APIs (currently limited/invite-only preview, announced 2026-08-13, Cerebras-hardware-backed, exclusive to `gpt-5.6-sol`). See https://openai.com/index/previewing-ultrafast/ Requests already pass through litellm today since `service_tier` is typed as a plain string (not a `Literal`), and `_map_openai_params` only checks the param *name* is in the allowlist, not its value. However, **cost calculation silently falls back to standard/default pricing** for any `service_tier` not in `ServiceTier` (currently only `FLEX` and `PRIORITY` — see `litellm/types/utils.py`, `class ServiceTier(Enum)`), via `_get_service_tier_cost_key` in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py`: ```python def _get_service_tier_cost_key(base_key: str, service_tier: Optional[str]) -> str: if service_tier is None: return base_key if service_tier.lower() in [ServiceTier.FLEX.value, ServiceTier.PRIORITY.value]: return f"{base_key}_{service_tier.lower()}" return base_key ``` This is the same class of silent-undercounting bug as #37046 (priority billed at default rate for gpt-4o/4.1). ### Motivation, pitch Without native support, any deployment that enables `service_tier="ultrafast"` will log costs at the standard rate while the provider bills at the (much higher) ultrafast rate — a silent cost-tracking gap with no warning or error. We're hitting this now since OpenAI has published sticker pricing that is roughly 10x standard for this tier, and we want accurate cost attribution before enabling it for our users. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? signal.title: feat(vector_stores): add Valkey as a managed vector store provider
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No vector store provider for Valkey / valkey-search - Managed vector store pipeline assumed every provider speaks HTTP How it solves it: - New valkey provider embeds the query and runs a KNN FT.SEARCH - BaseDirectVectorStoreConfig lets RESP datastores bypass the HTTP pipeline - Admin UI Add Vector Store modal gains a Valkey provider, with a plain-English setup checklist, explicit per-field tooltips, and the embedding model picked from the proxy's models like Milvus and S3 Vectors - Also registrable via vector_store_registry in the proxy config - Bounded socket timeouts so unreachable hosts cannot pin workers ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin whose document embeddings already live in Valkey cannot search them through the gateway 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and click Add Vector Store: the provider dropdown offers Bedrock, S3 Vectors, pgvector, Vertex AI, OpenAI, Azure, and Milvus, but no Valkey 2. There is no provider value they can pass to POST http://localhost:4000/vector_store/new that would make POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/{id}/search read from their Valkey index, so their documents stay unreachable After: the same admin registers the Valkey index and searches it from the API, the UI, and the config 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and click Add Vector Store: the dropdown now shows Valkey with its logo, and selecting it reveals host, port, password, TLS, embedding model, text field, and vector field inputs plus a setup checklist spelling out that LiteLLM only searches an index they already built, that vector search must be enabled on the server, and that the embedding model and field names must match what they stored 2. They enter their Valkey host and port, the FT index name as the Vector Store ID, and pick the embedding model from the proxy's models, click Create, and see the store listed with provider Valkey 3. On the Test Vector Store tab they type a question and get their own documents back ranked by score 4. The same store answers POST http://localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/{id}/search with an OpenAI-shaped results page, and an identical entry declared under vector_store_registry in the proxy config works without touching the UI or the management API ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4842 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All proofs captured at 10a95d0dd3 against a live proxy on localhost:4842, with real Vertex AI embedding calls (vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001) costing real money. The datastore is a valkey/valkey-bundle container (valkey-search module loaded) on localhost:6390, holding an FT index named litellm-qa-docs over 6 HASH docs whose embedding field was seeded with the same model API path: create the store, search it twice, delete it ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/vector_store/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"vector_store_id": "litellm-qa-docs", "custom_llm_provider": "valkey", "vector_store_name": "Valkey QA Docs", "litellm_params": {"valkey_host": "localhost", "valkey_port": 6390, "litellm_embedding_model": "vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001"}}' {"status":"success","message":"Vector store litellm-qa-docs created successfully","vector_store":{"vector_store_id":"litellm-qa-docs","custom_llm_provider":"valkey","vector_store_name":"Valkey QA Docs",...,"litellm_params":{"valkey_host":"localhost","valkey_port":6390,...,"litellm_embedding_model":"vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001",...},"team_id":null,"user_id":"default_user_id"}} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "how do I pull a great espresso shot?", "max_num_results": 3}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"how do I pull a great espresso shot?","data":[{"score":0.787654995918,"content":[{"text":"To brew great espresso, use freshly roasted beans ground fine, 18 grams in, 36 grams out in about 28 seconds at 93 degrees Celsius.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:espresso","filename":"kb:espresso"},{"score":0.53844845295,"content":[{"text":"Laminated croissant dough requires folding cold butter into the detrempe over several turns to build flaky layers.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:croissant","filename":"kb:croissant"},{"score":0.451147139072,"content":[{"text":"Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun; its thin carbon dioxide atmosphere and iron oxide dust give it a reddish appearance.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:mars","filename":"kb:mars"}]} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "open source fork of Redis", "max_num_results": 2}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"open source fork of Redis","data":[{"score":0.755149245262,"content":[{"text":"Valkey is an open source high-performance key-value datastore, forked from Redis and stewarded by the Linux Foundation.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:valkey","filename":"kb:valkey"},{"score":0.543505072594,"content":[{"text":"Python asyncio provides an event loop for cooperative multitasking, with coroutines scheduled via async and await syntax.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:asyncio","filename":"kb:asyncio"}]} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/vector_store/delete -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"vector_store_id": "litellm-qa-docs"}' {"status":"success","message":"Vector store litellm-qa-docs deleted successfully"} ``` Config path: the same store declared in the proxy config instead of the management API (run at the identical tree, before the temporary config edit was reverted) ``` vector_store_registry: - vector_store_name: valkey-config-kb litellm_params: vector_store_id: litellm-qa-docs custom_llm_provider: valkey valkey_host: localhost valkey_port: "6390" litellm_embedding_model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001 ``` ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-qa-docs/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "planet with a red surface", "max_num_results": 2}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"planet with a red surface","data":[{"score":0.7229921817780001,"content":[{"text":"Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun; its thin carbon dioxide atmosphere and iron oxide dust give it a reddish appearance.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:mars","filename":"kb:mars"},{"score":0.44688546657600003,"content":[{"text":"Python asyncio provides an event loop for cooperative multitasking, with coroutines scheduled via async and await syntax.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:asyncio","filename":"kb:asyncio"}]} ``` After the review-fix commit 27450db07e (list-query join plus bounded socket timeouts) the live search path was re-verified: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4842/v1/vector_stores/litellm-ui-kb/search -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query": "what is Valkey?", "max_num_results": 1}' {"object":"vector_store.search_results.page","search_query":"what is Valkey?","data":[{"score":0.7467186450959999,"content":[{"text":"Valkey is an open source high-performance key-value datastore, forked from Redis and stewarded by the Linux Foundation.","type":"text"}],"file_id":"kb:valkey","filename":"kb:valkey"}]} ``` UI path, verified end to end on the built dashboard: 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and go to Manage Vector Stores, then click + Add Vector Store 2. Pick Valkey in the provider dropdown (renders with the Valkey logo) and note the setup alert plus the seven provider fields appearing 3. Fill Vector Store ID with the FT index name, Valkey Host, Valkey Port, and Embedding Model, then click Create and see the success toast and the new row with provider Valkey 4. Open the Test Vector Store tab, select the store, submit a query like "how do I make croissants flaky?", and see the matching doc as Result 1 with the highest score Add New Vector Store modal with Valkey selected: ![Add New Vector Store modal with the Valkey provider, setup alert, and connection fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_lit_4842_screenshots/valkey_ui_add_modal.png) Manage Vector Stores after creation: ![Manage Vector Stores table listing the store with provider Valkey](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_lit_4842_screenshots/valkey_ui_manage_row.png) Test Vector Store tab returning the seeded docs ranked by score: ![Test Vector Store tab showing six ranked results with the croissant doc first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_lit_4842_screenshots/valkey_ui_test_results.png) ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Search only: file ingestion is not supported, valkey is excluded from the RAG upload dropdown - Docs page is written but must land in the separate docs repo - provider_endpoints_support.json docs link 404s until that docs page lands - Requires the valkey-search module and a pre-created FT index over HASH docs ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(anthropic-bridge): opt-in demotion of mid-turn system messages
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code 2.1+ sends mid-conversation system-role reminder messages - OpenAI accepts those anywhere, strict chat templates do not - Qwen3 on vLLM rejects the whole request with a 400 How it solves it: - new opt-in env flag `LITELLM_DEMOTE_MIDTURN_SYSTEM` - system rows after index 0 become user rows on the `/v1/messages` bridge - the leading system prompt keeps its role and position - without the flag nothing changes ## User Flow Before: a developer points Claude Code at a proxy fronting a local vLLM model and every real session dies on the second turn 1. The proxy admin routes `claude-*` to `hosted_vllm/qwen3` and the developer sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the proxy 2. Claude Code sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages carrying its system prompt plus a conversation that includes a mid-turn system reminder 3. The request comes back 400: `Hosted_vllmException - {"error":{"message":"System message must be at the beginning.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}` 4. Claude Code prints `API Error: 400` and the session is unusable against that backend After: the same session completes, reminders included 1. The proxy admin routes `claude-*` to `hosted_vllm/qwen3`, sets `LITELLM_DEMOTE_MIDTURN_SYSTEM=true`, restarts the proxy, and the developer sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the proxy 2. Claude Code sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with the same mid-turn system reminder 3. The response is 200 and the model visibly follows the reminder text, which now reaches it as a user turn 4. Claude Code works end to end against the local model ## Relevant issues Related: #26879 covers the same failure class on the Responses API surface ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. A live vLLM worker serving Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (the strict-template backend), one proxy config, one payload shaped like Claude Code's requests (top-level system, then a mid-turn system reminder between user turns): ```yaml # config.yaml model_list: - model_name: local-qwen litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/qwen-3.8-fp8-27b-code-1m api_base: http://127.0.0.1:15020/v1 api_key: dummy ``` ```json {"model": "local-qwen", "max_tokens": 200, "system": "You are a terse assistant.", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Say hi."}, {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "<system-reminder>Answer in exactly two words.</system-reminder>"}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "Say hi again."}]} ``` ### Before (340d30867e) 1. `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4010` 2. `curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:4010/v1/messages -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json`, observed: `{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Hosted_vllmException - {"error":{"message":"System message must be at the beginning.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}. Received Model Group=local-qwen
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}}` ### After (625c8b36d7) 1. `LITELLM_DEMOTE_MIDTURN_SYSTEM=true litellm --config config.yaml --port 4011` 2. The identical curl against port 4011, observed: `{"id":"chatcmpl-95a37fbb8a6bfbc4","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"local-qwen","stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":91,"output_tokens":61},"content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"We need answer exactly two words due system reminder? ..."},{"type":"text","text":"

Hi again."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"}` 3. The reply is exactly two words, so the demoted reminder still reached the model as instruction content ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - process-wide env flag, applies to every model behind the bridge - only the `/v1/messages` bridge path is changed - default stays the in-place behavior #34290 introduced deliberately ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat: add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search as a native search provider
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #31819 Enables Anthropic-native `web_search` (and the Claude Code WebSearch tutorial flow) for Bedrock users with an all-AWS search backend — related to the provider matrix in `docs/my-website/docs/search/index.md` and `docs/my-website/docs/tutorials/claude_code_websearch.md`. ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All proofs are fully e2e against a **real AgentCore Gateway** (`websearchgateway-*.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp` with a `web-search` connector target) and **real Bedrock Claude calls**. Captured at commit `6fef231f`. **1. Direct `litellm.search()`** (real gateway, SigV4): ``` $ python -c "import litellm; resp = litellm.search(query='python 3.13 release date', search_provider='agentcore', max_results=3); ..." - What's New In Python 3.13 — documentación de Python | https://docs.python.org/es/3.15/whatsnew/3.13.html - Python Release Python 3.13.3 | https://python.org/downloads/release/python-3133/ - wikipedia.org | https://wikipedia.org ``` **2. Claude Code request shape through the proxy** (`web_search_20250305` + forced `tool_choice`, `websearch_interception` + this provider, Bedrock Claude Sonnet): ``` $ curl http://localhost:4000/v1/messages ... -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet", "tools": [{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": 8}], "tool_choice": {"type": "tool", "name": "web_search"}, ...}' content block types: ['web_search_tool_result', 'tool_use'] - What's New In Python 3.13 — documentación de Python | https://docs.python.org/es/3.15/whatsnew/3.13.html - Python Release Python 3.13.3 | https://python.org/downloads/release/python-3133/ - Python Release Python 3.13.1 | https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3131/ ``` **3. Real Claude Code CLI end-to-end** (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` → proxy → Bedrock, WebSearch executed by this provider; zero client-side config): ``` $ ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000 claude -p "Use the WebSearch tool to find the release date of Python 3.13..." --allowedTools WebSearch Sources: - [Python 3.13.0 (final) released](https://blog.python.org/2024/10/python-3130-final-released) - [PEP 719 – Python 3.13 Release Schedule](https://peps.python.org/pep-0719/) ``` Bearer-token mode was additionally verified against a real `CUSTOM_JWT` gateway (Cognito `client_credentials` token) with AWS ambient credentials deliberately removed, including a full Claude Code CLI round-trip. Unit tests: ``` $ pytest tests/search_tests/test_agentcore_search.py -q 13 passed $ pytest tests/search_tests/test_tavily_search.py test_brave_search.py test_searxng_search.py -q # regression for shared handler change 20 passed, 3 skipped ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Adds **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search** (`search_provider: agentcore`) as a native search provider. Web Search on AgentCore is an AWS-managed web index (GA June 2026) exposed as an MCP tool on an AgentCore Gateway — no third-party search API or key, and queries never leave AWS. Combined with `websearch_interception`, this gives Bedrock users a pure-YAML way to make Claude Code / Anthropic-native `web_search_20250305` work: ```yaml search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-search litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://<gateway-id>.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp # MCP tool name is "<target-name>___WebSearch". Defaults to # "web-search-tool___WebSearch" (the target name used in the AWS docs' # boto3/CLI examples). Set this when your gateway target has a different # name, e.g. created via the agentcore CLI: # tool_name: MyWebSearchTarget___WebSearch # AWS_IAM gateway: explicit keys, or omit to use the default credential chain aws_access_key_id: os.environ/AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID aws_secret_access_key: os.environ/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY # CUSTOM_JWT gateway alternative: api_key: os.environ/AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: ["bedrock"] search_tool_name: agentcore-search ``` - **`AgentCoreSearchConfig`** (`litellm/llms/bedrock/search/transformation.py`): `BaseSearchConfig + BaseAWSLLM`. Transforms the unified search request into an MCP `tools/call`, parses plain-JSON and SSE-framed MCP responses into `SearchResponse`, propagates MCP errors, truncates queries to the 200-char gateway limit. Auth follows the gateway's inbound authorizer: SigV4 (`bedrock-agentcore` service; signing region auto-derived from the gateway URL) or OAuth2 bearer token (`api_key` / `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN`). - **`BaseSearchConfig.sign_request()`** (new optional hook, no-op by default): mirrors the existing `sign_request` pattern in `anthropic_messages`/`chat`. The search HTTP handler (sync + async) sends a signed body verbatim when present — re-serializing would invalidate the signature. No behavior change for the 17 existing search providers (regression suite passing above). - Registers `SearchProviders.AGENTCORE` + config-map entry. - 13 unit tests in `tests/search_tests/test_agentcore_search.py`. **Notes / known limitations** - **`tool_name`**: the gateway exposes the connector as `<target-name>___WebSearch`, where `<target-name>` is chosen by the user at target creation. The default (`web-search-tool___WebSearch`) matches the AWS documentation's boto3/CLI setup examples; targets created with other names need `tool_name` set explicitly (misconfiguration surfaces as a propagated MCP "tool not found" error, not a silent failure). Auto-discovery via `tools/list` was considered and deliberately left out: a gateway can legitimately host multiple `*___WebSearch` targets (e.g. with different domain-filter policies), and silently picking one would be worse than an explicit config error. - **Admin UI**: the search-tool create form currently has no `api_base` field, so UI-driven setup requires the `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` env var on the proxy; config.yaml setup (above) is unaffected. Adding the field to the form is a UI-side follow-up that would also benefit other self-hosted providers (e.g. searxng).

signal.title: fix(team_callback_endpoints): omit credential callback_vars instead of masking them
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reading a team's callbacks handed back a `***REDACTED***` marker - Posting that payload back stored the marker as the real credential - The row encrypts and looks legitimate; team logging silently stops working How it solves it: - Credential callback_vars are omitted from the read response, not masked - An absent key cannot be written over a stored credential - No write path needs to learn about a marker ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin cloning one team's logging config onto another team silently gives the second team a dead credential 1. They call GET https://litellm-domain/team/TEAM_A/callback and get back `{"langsmith_api_key": "***REDACTED***", "langsmith_project": "prod"}` 2. They post that same `callback_vars` object to POST https://litellm-domain/team/TEAM_B/callback and get HTTP 200 3. Nothing warns them, and team B's stored Langsmith key is now the literal text `***REDACTED***` 4. Team B's requests log nothing to Langsmith, and every read of the config keeps showing a credential that looks configured After: the same clone carries the shared configuration and visibly leaves the credential to be filled in 1. They call GET https://litellm-domain/team/TEAM_A/callback and get back `{"langsmith_project": "prod"}` with no credential field at all 2. They post that same `callback_vars` object to POST https://litellm-domain/team/TEAM_B/callback and get HTTP 200 3. Team B is stored with the project name and no Langsmith key, so the missing credential is visible on the next read 4. Team A's real credential is untouched, and no request can turn a read of this endpoint into an overwrite of a stored secret ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5110 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on a real Postgres. Values are read back out of the database and decrypted, so the evidence is the stored row, not the API echo. Shared setup ``` docker run -d --name litfix-pg-5110 -p 15110:5432 -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm \ -e POSTGRES_USER=llmproxy -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=dbpassword9090 postgres:16 export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://llmproxy:dbpassword9090@localhost:15110/litellm" export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-1234 export LITELLM_SALT_KEY=lit5110-salt-key-32-bytes-aaaaaa python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 20110 --use_prisma_db_push ``` Team A is seeded once with a real credential: ``` curl -X POST localhost:20110/team/$A/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"callback_name":"langsmith","callback_type":"success", "callback_vars":{"langsmith_api_key":"lsv2-REAL-WORKING-KEY","langsmith_project":"prod"}}' ``` ### Before (8159f240c4, the merge base at capture time) #### Cloning team A's callback config onto team B 1. Read team A's config ``` $ curl -s localhost:20110/team/$A/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"status":"success","data":{"team_id":"8ef61fb6...","success_callbacks":["langsmith"], "failure_callbacks":[], "callback_vars":{"langsmith_api_key":"***REDACTED***","langsmith_project":"prod"}}} ``` 2. Post that exact `callback_vars` payload to team B ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST localhost:20110/team/$B/callback \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"callback_name":"langsmith","callback_type":"success", "callback_vars":{"langsmith_api_key":"***REDACTED***","langsmith_project":"prod"}}' HTTP 200 ``` 3. Decrypt both rows straight out of Postgres ``` 8ef61fb6 langsmith_api_key = 'lsv2-REAL-WORKING-KEY' 40903df7 langsmith_api_key = '***REDACTED***' ``` Team B now holds the marker as an encrypted credential, with no validation error at any point. #### Overwriting a team's own credential through POST /team/update 1. Seed team D with a real key, then send the marker back through the team update route ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST localhost:20110/team/update \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"team_id":"'$D'","metadata":{"logging":[{"callback_name":"langsmith", "callback_type":"success","callback_vars":{"langsmith_api_key":"***REDACTED***", "langsmith_project":"prod"}}]}}' HTTP 200 ``` 2. Decrypt team D out of Postgres ``` team D at rest: {'langsmith_api_key': '***REDACTED***', 'langsmith_project': 'prod'} ``` The real key is gone, replaced in place by the marker. This second case is why the fix is on the read side; every write path would otherwise need its own marker rule, and missing one destroys credentials silently. ### After (433aef58e5) #### Cloning team A's callback config onto team E 1. Read team A's config; the credential key is absent rather than masked ``` $ curl -s localhost:20110/team/$A/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"status":"success","data":{"team_id":"8ef61fb6...","success_callbacks":["langsmith"], "failure_callbacks":[],"callback_vars":{"langsmith_project":"prod"}}} ``` 2. Post that exact `callback_vars` payload to a fresh team E ``` HTTP 200 ``` 3. Decrypt both rows straight out of Postgres ``` 8ef61fb6 callback_vars at rest = {'langsmith_api_key': 'lsv2-REAL-WORKING-KEY', 'langsmith_project': 'prod'} ac130867 callback_vars at rest = {'langsmith_project': 'prod'} ``` Team A's credential is untouched and team E carries the shared configuration with no fabricated secret. #### Legacy teams still on the deprecated callback_settings shape 1. A team whose row predates encryption at rest, holding a plaintext secret ``` $ curl -s localhost:20110/team/$L/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"team_id":"6448d8ab...","success_callbacks":["gcs_bucket"],"failure_callbacks":[], "callback_vars":{"gcs_bucket_name":"legacy-bucket"}} ``` The plaintext secret does not escape, and the bucket name is still readable. #### A team whose callback_vars are all credentials ``` $ curl -s localhost:20110/team/$S/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"team_id":"24f19d4b...","success_callbacks":["langfuse"],"failure_callbacks":[], "callback_vars":{}} ``` `success_callbacks` still reports langfuse as active, so an empty `callback_vars` is not mistaken for an unconfigured team. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Behavior changes Credential-bearing `callback_vars` keys are absent from this response rather than present with a marker. The response is a partial config, not a safe round trip: the metadata write paths replace `logging` wholesale, so echoing the payload back still drops the stored credential. What it can no longer do is store a fabricated one in its place. That changes the failure mode of a cloned config, and the direction depends on whether a destination field survives the drop. This was measured on a base-vs-head A/B with real Gemini calls exported to a real Langfuse project, cloning a config and then reading the traces back through the Langfuse API: | cloned team config | base 00e1f25e9b | head 16b1e6e7f6 | | --- | --- | --- | | keys plus `langfuse_host` | marker sent as basic auth to the team host, no trace | credentials absent and host present, so `allow_env_credentials` blocks the proxy credential and the callback no-ops, no trace | | keys only, no host | marker rejected as credentials, no trace | no dynamic credentials, so the global logger exports the team's request into the proxy-level Langfuse project | Only the fourth cell changed to something a reader would not expect, and it was observed rather than reasoned: the target team's prompt and completion land in the proxy operator's own project. The state itself is not new, since any team registering a callback with only non-secret vars reaches it today, and the endpoint is admin-gated so the actor could already point that team anywhere. It is quieter than the old failure, so a caller cloning a config has to re-supply the credential. `gcs_path_service_account` and `posthog_api_key` have no equivalent `allow_env_credentials` guard, so the same shape applies to them. Datadog fails closed. The Langfuse passthrough route improves: it now returns a 400 naming the missing dynamic credentials instead of forwarding the marker as basic auth. A value that fails to decrypt after a salt-key rotation is likewise omitted rather than marked. It was already non-functional at request time, so nothing working is hidden, but the response no longer distinguishes "not configured" from "configured but undecryptable". ## Caveats (if any) - `***REDACTED***` stays defined here for audit-log redaction - Write paths still accept the marker as an ordinary string - `/team/info` still returns these credentials unmasked, tracked in LIT-5102 - The marker constant was not consolidated; see below ## Why this endpoint diverges from the in-repo precedent Two endpoints already implement the alternative, teaching the write path to read the marker as "keep the saved value" (`_merge_over_saved` in `coordination_redis_endpoints.py` and `cache_settings_endpoints.py`). That was not reused here for two reasons. Team callback config has four write paths rather than one, and missing any of them destroys credentials silently. And `logging` is a list, so a restore needs stable per-entry identity rather than a flat key match. For the same reason the marker constant was not consolidated into `litellm/constants.py`. In those two cache endpoints the marker is a round-trippable sentinel the write path honours; here it is a display string with no write meaning. One shared constant would conflate the two and invite exactly the "the write path must know about the marker" assumption that produced this bug. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ui): move the MCP server forms and detail tabs off tremor
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The MCP server screens still render through tremor primitives - tremor has to go before the dashboard can drop it - Its buttons submit forms by accident inside antd forms How it solves it: - Moves six MCP components onto the shadcn button, input and tab primitives - Keeps the connect and settings tab strips underlined on a divider, the way tremor drew them - Keeps antd modals, forms and selects for the antd pass - Pins the tab mount contract with two regression tests - Prunes the six no-restricted-imports suppressions these files no longer need ## User Flow Before: an admin registering an MCP server walks the whole flow on the old primitives, and pressing Enter in the form fires whichever control happens to come first 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers, click "+ Add New MCP Server" and then "+ Custom Server" 2. They fill in the server name, pick "Streamable HTTP (Recommended)" as the transport, and type the server URL 3. In Authentication they pick OAuth, then fill Client ID and Client Secret, each with an eye button to check what they pasted 4. Pressing Enter in any field activates Cancel, or "Authorize & Fetch Token" while the OAuth block is open, so the form never submits 5. They click "Add MCP Server", open the new server, and move between Overview, MCP Tools and Settings 6. Inside Settings they type a value on Server Configuration, switch to Cost Configuration and back, and the value is still there After: the same admin walks the same steps on the standard primitives, and Enter now submits the form the way the rest of the dashboard behaves 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers, click "+ Add New MCP Server" and then "+ Custom Server" 2. They fill in the server name, pick "Streamable HTTP (Recommended)" as the transport, and type the server URL 3. In Authentication they pick OAuth, then fill Client ID and Client Secret, each with an eye button to check what they pasted 4. Pressing Enter in any field submits through "Add MCP Server", which is now the only submit control in the form 5. They click "Add MCP Server", open the new server, and move between Overview, MCP Tools and Settings 6. Inside Settings they type a value on Server Configuration, switch to Cost Configuration and back on the same underlined strip, and the value is still there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5746 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Every shot below was taken against a live proxy on :4711 with the real MCP server row in its database, the dashboard dev server on the merge base for Before and on the PR tip for After. Click the "LiteLLM Proxy" tab inside that panel ![connect_litellm__after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_mcp_0817_screenshots/connect_litellm__after.png) #### server_settings 1. Open the qa_github_mcp server, click "Settings", and stay on "Server Configuration" ![server_settings__after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_mcp_0817_screenshots/server_settings__after.png) #### server_cost 1. This is a deliberate move onto the standard type scale that the earlier waves also made, not a pixel parity port - Enter in the create form submits instead of cancelling - The five secret fields moved to antd so the reveal survives - Modals, forms and selects stay on antd for now - Prunes shared suppressions, so it needs a rebase after sibling merges ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ui): move the add model and credential forms off tremor
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The add model and credential forms still render through tremor - tremor is being retired, so every remaining import blocks the removal - Nine files here kept a stale lint suppression for that import How it solves it: - Text inputs move to the shadcn Input, text moves to sized paragraphs - Provider secret fields move to antd's Input.Password, so the reveal survives - The advanced settings accordion becomes a bordered Base UI collapsible - The Team-BYOK toggle moves to the Base UI switch - Prunes the tremor lint suppressions these nine files no longer need ## User Flow Before: an admin onboarding an Azure deployment walks the whole task on the tremor rendering, where the secret boxes carry a reveal eye and the empty cost boxes carry a grey Type hint 1. They open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints/ and click the Add Model tab, and the provider picker, the model name box, the model mappings table and a collapsed Advanced Settings box are on screen 2. They pick Azure in the provider picker, and the model name box turns into a free text box with a help line under it 3. They type a deployment name, and the model mappings table fills in with an editable public model name box 4. They scroll to the credential boxes and fill API Base, API Version, Azure API Key, Azure AD Token and Client Secret, and each secret box offers an eye button to check what they pasted 5. They open Advanced Settings, turn Custom Pricing on, and the Input Cost and Output Cost boxes show a grey Type hint while the two cache cost boxes show their own hints 6. They move to the LLM Credentials tab, click Add Credential, and fill the same provider boxes in the modal, where the API key box again offers the eye button 7. They open a model from All Models and click Re-use Credentials, and name the saved credential in the modal After: the same admin walks the same seven steps and reaches the same result, with the same fields, labels, hints and buttons, except that the reveal eye on the secret boxes is now antd's and three boxes no longer carry the grey Type hint 1. They open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints/ and click the Add Model tab, and the provider picker, the model name box, the model mappings table and a collapsed Advanced Settings box are on screen 2. They pick Azure in the provider picker, and the model name box turns into a free text box with a help line under it 3. They type a deployment name, and the model mappings table fills in with an editable public model name box 4. They scroll to the credential boxes and fill API Base, API Version, Azure API Key, Azure AD Token and Client Secret, and each secret box still offers an eye button to check what they pasted, now the antd one 5. They open Advanced Settings, turn Custom Pricing on, and the Input Cost and Output Cost boxes are now empty instead of showing the grey Type hint, while the two cache cost boxes keep their own hints 6. They move to the LLM Credentials tab, click Add Credential, and fill the same provider boxes in the modal, where the API key box keeps its eye button but starts empty instead of showing the Type hint 7. They open a model from All Models and click Re-use Credentials, and name the saved credential in the modal ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5746 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs use the same Admin UI dev server recipe against the same live proxy: `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` on port 3000, `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` pointing at a proxy on port 4000 that already holds the models used below, signed in as the proxy admin. The Before run is the merge base, the After run is this PR's tip, and every case walks the same clicks on both. Nothing in the run writes: no case saves, creates or deletes anything. The side by side composites for each case live on `litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots` as `<case>.png`. The two cases that show a secret field were recaptured on the tip that puts the reveal back, and the rest are unchanged by that commit. ### Before (4d57bf0bdd) #### add-model-form 1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints/ and click the Add Model tab 2. The provider picker, the LiteLLM model name box, the model mappings table, the mode picker and the health check help line are on screen ![add-model-form before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-form__before.png) #### add-model-public-model-name 1. API Base, API Version, Base Model, Azure API Key, Azure AD Token, Tenant ID, Client ID and Client Secret render with their placeholders, and the three secret boxes carry an eye button ![add-model-azure-credentials before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-azure-credentials__before.png) #### add-model-advanced-settings 1. Click the LLM Credentials tab 2. The credential table renders with its empty state and the Add Credential button ![credentials-tab before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/credentials-tab__before.png) #### credentials-add-modal 1. The modal renders Credential Name, the provider picker, API Base, OpenAI Organization ID and the OpenAI API Key box, which shows the Type hint and an eye button ![credentials-add-modal before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/credentials-add-modal__before.png) #### reuse-credentials-modal 1. The Reuse Credentials modal renders the prefilled credential name box, Need Help, Cancel and Reuse Credentials ![reuse-credentials-modal before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/reuse-credentials-modal__before.png) ### After (741638ff49f03e79c7105d96d5cbf12893e0bc6e) #### add-model-form 1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints/ and click the Add Model tab 2. The same provider picker, model name box, model mappings table, mode picker and health check help line are on screen ![add-model-form after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-form__after.png) #### add-model-public-model-name 1. On the Add Model tab, type `claude-sonnet-4-5` into the LiteLLM model name box 2. The model mappings table fills in with the same editable public model name box holding the same value ![add-model-public-model-name after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-public-model-name__after.png) #### add-model-azure-credentials 1. On the Add Model tab, pick Azure in the provider picker and scroll to the credential boxes 2. The same eight boxes render with the same placeholders, and the three secret boxes still carry an eye button, drawn by antd now ![add-model-azure-credentials after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-azure-credentials__after.png) #### add-model-advanced-settings 1. On the Add Model tab, click Advanced Settings and then the Custom Pricing toggle 2. The box opens with the same border and chevron, and the Team-BYOK toggle and the API Key box sit above it in the same place ![add-model-advanced-settings after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-advanced-settings__after.png) #### add-model-custom-pricing 1. Input Cost and Output Cost are empty instead of showing the Type hint, the two cache cost boxes keep Defaults to Input Cost if blank, and the LiteLLM Params box and its help line follow ![add-model-custom-pricing after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-model-custom-pricing__after.png) #### add-auto-router-modal 1. Click the Auto-Routers tab and then Add Auto Router 2. The dialog opens with the same Auto Router Name box, template picker, detailed configuration section and footer buttons ![add-auto-router-modal after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/add-auto-router-modal__after.png) #### credentials-tab 1. Click the LLM Credentials tab 2. The credential table renders identically, byte for byte against the Before capture ![credentials-tab after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/credentials-tab__after.png) #### credentials-add-modal 1. On the LLM Credentials tab, click Add Credential 2. The modal renders the same five rows, and the OpenAI API Key box keeps its eye button while losing the Type hint ![credentials-add-modal after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_add-model_0817_screenshots/credentials-add-modal__after.png) #### reuse-credentials-modal 1. signal.title: refactor(ui): move the virtual key create and edit forms off tremor
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The key create and edit forms still render tremor primitives - Two component libraries style the same dashboard page - tremor buttons have no type, so cancel submitted forms How it solves it: - Accordion becomes Collapsible, Grid and Col become grid divs - Text and Title become real paragraphs and headings on the standard type scale - TextInput becomes the shadcn Input, tremor Button becomes shadcn Button - Prunes the four no-restricted-imports suppressions these files shed ## User Flow Before: an admin creating and then editing a virtual key works through a page whose form controls come from tremor, and the Cancel button in the key edit drawer quietly saves the key on its way out 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. The modal opens on Key Ownership, with Owned By radios, Organization and Team pickers 3. They pick an owner, fill in Key Name, then expand Optional Settings and its MCP, Agent, Logging, Router, Model Aliases, Key Lifecycle and Advanced Settings panels 4. They click Create Key and copy the generated key out of the confirmation dialog 5. Back on the same page they click the key row, open the Settings tab and click Edit Settings 6. They change their mind and click Cancel, and the drawer closes after also submitting the form, so whatever they typed is saved After: the same admin walks the identical path on shadcn controls, and Cancel only cancels 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. The modal opens on Key Ownership, with Owned By radios, Organization and Team pickers 3. They pick an owner, fill in Key Name, then expand Optional Settings and its MCP, Agent, Logging, Router, Model Aliases, Key Lifecycle and Advanced Settings panels 4. They click Create Key and copy the generated key out of the confirmation dialog 5. Back on the same page they click the key row, open the Settings tab and click Edit Settings 6. They click Cancel, the drawer closes, and nothing is saved ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5746 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a live proxy holding real keys, teams, organizations and MCP servers, with the dashboard dev server pointed at it. Baseline ran the merge base, the after run ran this PR's tip, and both runs walked the same clicks: open Virtual Keys, open the create modal on each Owned By variant, expand Optional Settings and every sub-panel inside it, then open a key and edit it. The side-by-side composites for every case live on the `litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots` branch as `<case>.png`. ### Before (4d57bf0bdd) #### keys_list 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/keys_list__before.png) #### create_key_owned_by_you 1. Click "+ Create New Key" 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_owned_by_you__before.png) #### create_key_owned_by_service_account 1. Click "+ Create New Key", then pick Service Account under Owned By 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_owned_by_service_account__before.png) #### create_key_owned_by_another_user 1. Click "+ Create New Key", then expand Optional Settings 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_optional_settings__before.png) #### create_key_mcp_agent_logging 1. Expand Optional Settings, then MCP Settings, Agent Settings and Logging Settings 2. ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_mcp_agent_logging__before.png) #### create_key_router_and_model_aliases 1. Click "+ Create New Key" 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_owned_by_you__after.png) #### create_key_owned_by_service_account 1. Click "+ Create New Key", then expand Optional Settings 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_optional_settings__after.png) #### create_key_mcp_agent_logging 1. Expand Optional Settings, then MCP Settings, Agent Settings and Logging Settings 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_mcp_agent_logging__after.png) #### create_key_router_and_model_aliases 1. Expand Optional Settings, then Router Settings and Model Aliases 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_router_and_model_aliases__after.png) #### create_key_lifecycle 1. Expand Optional Settings, then Key Lifecycle 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_lifecycle__after.png) #### create_key_advanced_settings 1. Expand Optional Settings, then Advanced Settings 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/create_key_advanced_settings__after.png) #### key_edit_view_top 1. Scroll the same edit form to its footer 2. ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_shadcn_tremor_keys_0817_screenshots/key_edit_view_bottom__after.png) ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Cancel in the key edit drawer no longer saves the key - Bare tremor TextInputs came with a default "Type..." placeholder that shadcn Input has no equivalent for, so the Key Alias fields in both forms now rely on their labels alone - tremor Text rendered at the themed text-tremor-default, which globals.css sets to 0.775rem and grey, so the text-sm replacement is 14px and near-black, and Title's 1.025rem becomes a real heading. This is a deliberate move onto the standard type scale that the earlier waves also made, so read the screenshots as a restyle and not a pixel-parity port - Buttons take shadcn's palette: primary black, secondary grey - These forms keep their antd Modal, Form, Select and textareas - Refuted: adding a made-up Key Alias placeholder, which invents copy - Prunes shared eslint-suppressions.json, so sibling sweeps need rebases ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse streaming buffers input_json_delta for the entire duration of large tool_use calls, causing 60–150s+ silent SSE gaps on /v1/messages
signal.text:
### What happened? When using LiteLLM Proxy's Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint with a Bedrock Claude model through `bedrock/converse`, streaming stalls during large `tool_use` calls. If the model emits a large tool call argument payload, for example a `Write` or `Edit` tool call with a large `file_text` argument, LiteLLM sends the initial SSE events normally, then stops sending bytes for tens of seconds or longer. After the tool argument generation finishes, LiteLLM flushes many `input_json_delta` chunks all at once. This causes clients or intermediaries with idle timeouts to close the stream before the delayed chunks arrive. ### Reproduction 1. Configure LiteLLM Proxy with a Bedrock Claude model using the Bedrock Converse path. 2. Send a streaming request to `/v1/messages`. 3. Use a prompt/tool setup that causes the model to emit one large `tool_use` block, such as writing or editing a large file. 4. Observe raw SSE timing from the client side or proxy side. ### Observed behavior The stream starts normally: ```text t=0.00s event: message_start t=0.05s event: content_block_start (text) t=0.12s event: content_block_delta (text) t=0.18s event: content_block_stop t=0.20s event: content_block_start (tool_use) ``` Then no bytes are written to the response stream for a long period: ```text ... no SSE bytes for ~110s ... ``` After that, all tool argument deltas arrive in a burst: ```text t=110.4s event: content_block_delta (input_json_delta) x1 t=110.4s event: content_block_delta (input_json_delta) x2 ... 500+ input_json_delta chunks delivered within a few hundred ms t=110.7s event: content_block_stop t=110.7s event: message_delta t=110.7s event: message_stop ``` The delayed data is not lost. It eventually arrives complete, but only after being buffered for nearly the full duration of the tool argument generation. ### Expected behavior `input_json_delta` chunks for `tool_use` arguments should be forwarded incrementally as they are received from Bedrock `ConverseStream`. Large tool arguments should not be buffered until the entire `tool_use` block is complete. ### Impact The long silent period can trigger idle timeouts in clients, reverse proxies, load balancers, or other intermediaries. The client-side failure appears as a truncated stream or connection closed mid-response, even though the upstream model generation is still in progress. ### Relevant LiteLLM area This appears to affect the Bedrock Converse streaming path used behind the Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint. Likely related area: ```text litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/converse_handler.py ``` Specifically, the handling of Bedrock `ConverseStream` `contentBlockDelta` events for `toolUse.input` fragments and their conversion into Anthropic-format `input_json_delta` events. ### Code change applied as a workaround As a local mitigation, we wrapped the `/v1/messages` streaming response iterator and inject Anthropic-compatible SSE `ping` events whenever no upstream bytes are received for a fixed interval. The workaround does not change the Bedrock/LiteLLM internal buffering behavior. It only prevents downstream idle timeouts while LiteLLM is silent. The added behavior is: ```python _SSE_PING_EVENT = ( ":" + " " * 4096 + "
" + 'event: ping
data: {"type": "ping"}

' ) ``` Then the upstream `body_iterator` is wrapped so that: - real upstream SSE chunks are forwarded unchanged; - if no upstream chunk arrives within 5 seconds, a `ping` SSE event is yielded; - once upstream chunks resume, normal forwarding continues. Conceptually: ```python async def _sse_ping_keepalive_iterator(body_iterator, interval_seconds=5): while True: try: chunk = await asyncio.wait_for( body_iterator.__anext__(), timeout=interval_seconds, ) yield chunk except asyncio.TimeoutError: yield _SSE_PING_EVENT.encode("utf-8") except StopAsyncIteration: break ``` The 4KB SSE comment padding is included before the `ping` event to force immediate flushing through buffering intermediaries such as reverse proxies. This prevents client/proxy/load-balancer idle timeout disconnects during the silent gap, but the underlying streaming issue remains: `input_json_delta` chunks still arrive in a burst after the tool argument generation completes. ### Suggested upstream fix The Bedrock Converse streaming handler should emit `toolUse.input` fragments as Anthropic-format `input_json_delta` events immediately when each Bedrock `contentBlockDelta` event is received. The likely fix is to avoid accumulating the full tool input before emitting Anthropic deltas. Each Bedrock tool input fragment should be converted and yielded immediately from the streaming transformation path. ### LiteLLM version ```text v1.90.0 ``` ### Related issues checked I checked the following related issues and did not find an exact match: - #11747: Bedrock streaming responses buffered in 1024-byte chunks. Related Bedrock streaming area, but this issue concerns text chunking, not full buffering of `tool_use` argument deltas. - #20711: Responses API streaming drops tool call argument deltas. Different API path and data-loss behavior. - #25321: `/v1/messages` streaming adapter drops tool arguments for non-Anthropic models. Different backend behavior; this issue is delayed delivery, not missing arguments. - #18655: Similar burst behavior, but on the OpenAI Responses API bridge path rather than Bedrock Converse. - #18667: JSON parsing failure in tool call arguments. Different failure mode.
