signal.title: fix(advisor): resolve the advisor sub-call through the proxy router
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - advisor sub-calls ignored `model_list` and dialed api.anthropic.com - every advisor use failed where egress blocks Anthropic - no fallbacks applied to the advisor model group How it solves it: - advisor sub-call now resolves through the proxy router - router match covers exact `model_name`, `model_group_alias`, and wildcard patterns - advisor context excludes in-sequence system rows (e.g. Claude Code hook output), which providers reject once the question turn is appended after them - keeps SDK path when the router can't resolve the model - caller-supplied advisor api_key/api_base still bypasses the router ## User Flow Before: a developer using Claude Code against the gateway sends the advisor tool with a model group backed by a non-Anthropic provider, and every advisor use fails because the gateway leaves the network to reach Anthropic directly 1. A gateway admin configures `claude-opus-5` in `model_list`, pointing at a non-Anthropic deployment, and an executor model group on the same provider 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-sonnet-5"` and `"tools": [{"type": "advisor_20260301", "name": "advisor", "model": "claude-opus-5"}]` 3. The executor asks for advice, and the gateway leaves for `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` instead of the configured deployment 4. The request comes back `401 authentication_error, x-api-key header is required`, and on a deployment whose egress blocks Anthropic it instead hangs until the connect timeout 5. The only escape is pointing `ANTHROPIC_API_BASE` at one static endpoint, which applies to every request that resolves to Anthropic and gets no failover After: the same request keeps the advisor traffic on the configured deployment, so the developer gets the final answer 1. Same configuration as above 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same advisor tool, including sessions whose history carries mid-conversation system rows from Claude Code hooks 3. The advisor turn goes to the deployment configured for `claude-opus-5`, with its credentials and its fallbacks 4. The response is a normal `200` with the assistant's final text, and nothing left the network toward Anthropic ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5307 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Claude Code as the end-user client, real AWS Bedrock calls (costing real $), no mocks. Both runs used the same config where both model groups are backed by Bedrock, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` was empty so a leak to Anthropic is visible as a 401 ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 - model_name: claude-opus-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (6d32d4081d) 1. Boot the proxy with the config above and no Anthropic key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= litellm --config config.yaml --port 52789 --detailed_debug > before.log 2>&1` 2. Launch real Claude Code against it with the advisor tool enabled: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:52789 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-1234 ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5 CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_ADVISOR_TOOL=1 claude --advisor claude-opus-5` 3. Ask: `Consult your advisor first, then tell me: what is a good name for a function that reverses a string?` 4. Claude Code never answers; it loops on the advisor turn leaking to Anthropic: ``` ✻ 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"x-api-key header is required"},"request_id":"req_011CeAryheSqr2vjj4itKE1Y"}. Received Model Group=claude-sonnet-5 · Retrying in 1s · attempt 3/10 ``` 5. Count upstream hosts with `grep -oE "https://(api\.anthropic\.com|bedrock-runtime[a-z0-9.-]*\.amazonaws\.com)[A-Za-z0-9/._:%-]*" before.log | sort | uniq -c`: ``` 16 https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages 10 https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5/invoke 1 https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5/invoke-with-response-stream ``` ### After (4e8efa041d) 1. Boot the proxy exactly as in Before, on port 52790, logging to after.log 2. Launch the same Claude Code command against port 52790 and ask the same question 3. Claude Code consults the advisor and answers normally: ``` ⏺ Advisor's take: use reverse if context already implies string (s.reverse()), otherwise reverseString, matching your language's casing. ``` 4. The same host count now shows the advisor turn on the configured Bedrock deployment and nothing reaching api.anthropic.com: ``` 1 https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-opus-5/invoke 2 https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5/invoke 1 https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5/invoke-with-response-stream ``` 5. after.log shows the advisor sub-call resolved by the router: `Inside ageneric_api_call_with_fallbacks() - model: claude-opus-5` with `advisor_sub_call: True` in its metadata ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `_inject_max_uses_error` is still dead code, left for a follow-up - `can_handle()` still ignores `max_uses`, so `max_uses: 0` hard-fails instead of degrading - SDK callers with no proxy router keep the old provider inference - in-sequence system rows are stripped from every advisor sub-call, including mid-array ones that would stay valid, so deliberate mid-conversation system content never reaches the advisor - the advisor model is not checked against the calling key's model access; pre-existing, and this PR narrows what it can reach from the public Anthropic API to configured deployments ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/30b92ea437414112bc07ad85626aea31 Requested by: @shivamrawat1 - [x] 4e8efa041de3b4c0d4493c17a8fc20e7de05ca52 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: fix(router): forward target_model_names on file uploads to litellm_proxy deployments
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Batch file uploads fail when a deployment targets another LiteLLM proxy - The second proxy gets a bare upload with no routing hint and errors or misroutes How it solves it: - Router forwards target_model_names via extra_body for litellm_proxy deployments - extra_body lands as a multipart field, exactly what the second proxy's /v1/files reads - litellm_proxy is now an OpenAI-compatible files and batches provider ## User Flow Before: a developer whose batch client talks to a front LiteLLM proxy that forwards to a second LiteLLM proxy cannot upload batch input at all 1. The front proxy admin declares `gpt-5.6-batch` as a `litellm_proxy/gpt-5.6-batch` deployment with `api_base` set to the second proxy's URL and a key issued by that second proxy; the second proxy serves `gpt-5.6-batch` on a real OpenAI deployment 2. The developer sends POST https://front-proxy/v1/files as multipart with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-5.6-batch`, and their JSONL file 3. They get 400 `LiteLLM doesn't support litellm_proxy for 'create_file'. Only ['openai', 'azure', 'vertex_ai', 'manus', 'anthropic'] are supported` 4. Working around it, the admin re-declares the deployment as `openai/gpt-5.6-batch` with the same `api_base`, and the developer repeats the same POST 5. They now get 500 `files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.` because the second proxy received the file with no `target_model_names` and no model to route on 6. If the second proxy admin adds a `files_settings` entry, the same POST returns 404 `Resource not found` whenever the second proxy's target deployment is Azure-backed, since the upload was sent in OpenAI shape to whatever the default provider was 7. The developer never receives a file id, so POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches is never possible After: the same upload is routed to the second proxy's target deployment and the batch completes through both hops 1. The front proxy admin declares `gpt-5.6-batch` as a `litellm_proxy/gpt-5.6-batch` deployment with `api_base` set to the second proxy's URL and a key issued by that second proxy; the second proxy serves `gpt-5.6-batch` on a real OpenAI deployment 2. The developer sends POST https://front-proxy/v1/files as multipart with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-5.6-batch`, and their JSONL file 3. They get 200 with a file object whose `id` is the front proxy's long scrambled unified id, `purpose: batch`, `status: uploaded` 4. They send POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches with that `input_file_id`, `endpoint: /v1/chat/completions`, `completion_window: 24h`, `model: gpt-5.6-batch` and get 200 with a batch id 5. GET https://front-proxy/v1/batches/{batch_id} eventually returns `status: completed` with `request_counts: {"completed": 1, "failed": 0, "total": 1}` and the real OpenAI model in `model` 6. The batch results are read from the second proxy with GET https://second-proxy/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content, which returns the OpenAI batch output line with the assistant reply and token usage (fetching it through the front proxy is a pre-existing gap, see Caveats) ## Relevant issues Fixes #36176 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5347 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: two chained proxies from this repo, both with a database and managed files. Proxy B on port 33417 serves `gpt-5.6-batch` backed by `openai/gpt-5.5` with a real OpenAI key. Proxy A on port 25002 serves `gpt-5.6-batch` as a `litellm_proxy/gpt-5.6-batch` deployment with `api_base: http://localhost:33417` and proxy B's key, plus `gpt-5.6-batch-workaround` as the issue's `openai/gpt-5.6-batch` deployment against the same `api_base`. Input file: ``` {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "gpt-5.6-batch", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one word."}], "max_completion_tokens": 16}} ``` ### Before (852368d72f, merge base) #### Upload through the litellm_proxy deployment 1. `curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5347-a" -F purpose="batch" -F target_model_names="gpt-5.6-batch" -F file=@batch.jsonl` 2. Observed: ``` {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: LiteLLM doesn't support litellm_proxy for 'create_file'. Only ['openai', 'azure', 'vertex_ai', 'manus', 'anthropic'] are supported.. Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-batch\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` #### Upload through the issue's openai/ workaround deployment 1. Same curl with `-F target_model_names="gpt-5.6-batch-workaround"`, the `openai/gpt-5.6-batch` deployment pointing at proxy B 2. Observed, reproducing the reported error: ``` {"error":{"message":"Error code: 500 - {'error': {'message': 'files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.', 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': '500'}}. Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-batch-workaround\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":"None","param":"None","code":"500"}} ``` ### After (c18d50b521, behavior-identical at tip 76a2340685) #### Upload through the litellm_proxy deployment 1. `curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5347-a" -F purpose="batch" -F target_model_names="gpt-5.6-batch" -F file=@batch.jsonl` 2. Observed, the upload succeeds through both hops (proxy A managed files -> proxy B managed files -> OpenAI): ``` {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07dW5pZmll...","bytes":199,"created_at":1787085578,"filename":"modified_file.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} ``` 3. Decoding the unified id shows proxy B ran its own managed files flow, its inner id wrapping a real OpenAI file id (`llm_output_file_id,file-W5G96mWZwwttfazFEWdEMV`) 4. `curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5347-a" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id": "<unified id from upload>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "model": "gpt-5.6-batch"}'` returns `"status": "validating"` with a batch id 5. `curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/batches/<batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5347-a"`, observed after two polls: ``` {"status": "completed", "request_counts": {"completed": 1, "failed": 0, "total": 1}, "model": "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23", ...} ``` 6. `curl -s http://localhost:33417/v1/files/<output_file_id>/content -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5347-b"` (proxy B, per the caveat) returns the actual OpenAI batch response, paid for with real tokens: `status: 200 | model: gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 | reply: Hello | usage: 16 total tokens` #### Upload through the issue's openai/ workaround deployment 1. Same curl with `-F target_model_names="gpt-5.6-batch-workaround"` still returns the 500 `files_settings is not set` error; this PR fixes the `litellm_proxy/` deployment path, which is the supported way to chain proxies ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Batch output and error file ids minted by proxy B pass through proxy A unwrapped, so their content is only fetchable from proxy B; pre-existing, follow-up filed as #37352 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 76a2340685 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: [Bug]: Client-supplied `store` and `prompt_cache_key` are silently dropped for OpenAI chat completions (accepted as "supported", never forwarded)
signal.text: ## What happened? When calling `litellm.completion()` (or the proxy `/v1/chat/completions`) for an OpenAI model with the OpenAI Chat Completions parameters `store` and/or `prompt_cache_key`, LiteLLM accepts the request without any error or warning, but **neither parameter is included in the outbound HTTP request to the provider**. `safety_identifier`, passed the same way, IS forwarded correctly. This is silent data loss of documented OpenAI parameters: - `prompt_cache_key` — OpenAI's cache-routing hint ([prompt caching guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching)). Losing it degrades cache hit rates for high-volume workloads without any visible symptom. - `store` — explicit opt-out/in for OpenAI request storage. Losing `store: false` silently discards a data-governance declaration. Both params were added to the *supported params* lists in PR #20989 (so `drop_params`/`UnsupportedParamsError` no longer reject them), but the forwarding plumbing was never completed — see root cause below. Verified on `v1.90.2` and still present on `main` as of 2026-07-14. ## Minimal reproduction (no proxy needed, no API key needed) ```python import json, threading from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer captured = {} class Capture(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_POST(self): captured["body"] = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))) resp = json.dumps({"id": "x", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 1, "model": "gpt-x", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2}}).encode() self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(resp))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(resp) def log_message(self, *a): pass srv = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 18123), Capture) threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start() import litellm litellm.completion( model="openai/gpt-4o", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], store=False, # silently dropped prompt_cache_key="my-cache-key", # silently dropped safety_identifier="abc123", # forwarded correctly api_base="http://127.0.0.1:18123", api_key="test", ) srv.shutdown() print(json.dumps(captured["body"], indent=2)) ``` **Actual output** (body received by the server standing in for OpenAI): ```json { "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "model": "gpt-4o", "safety_identifier": "abc123" } ``` **Expected output**: the body should also contain `"store": false` and `"prompt_cache_key": "my-cache-key"`. The same happens through the proxy: POST `/v1/chat/completions` with all three params → only `safety_identifier` reaches the provider (verified by pointing a model's `api_base` at a request-recording mock). The proxy's spend logs make the loss visible indirectly: `hidden_params.optional_params` contains `safety_identifier` but never `store`/`prompt_cache_key`, even when the incoming request body contains them. ## Root cause The parameters are plumbed halfway: 1. `litellm/constants.py` → `OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETION_PARAMS` includes `"store"`, `"prompt_cache_key"`, `"safety_identifier"` — so `get_non_default_completion_params()` extracts all three from kwargs. 2. `litellm/llms/openai/chat/gpt_transformation.py` → `get_supported_openai_params()` `base_params` includes all three ("works across all models") — so nothing is rejected or dropped by `drop_params` logic (this half was added in #20989). 3. **But** `litellm/utils.py` → `get_optional_params()` builds its working set from its own function signature (`locals()`-based collection). `safety_identifier` exists there as a named parameter (also named in `completion()`/`acompletion()` in `litellm/main.py`), while `store` and `prompt_cache_key` are **not in the signature** — they arrive inside the anonymous `kwargs` dict, are never lifted into the passed-params scan, and are dropped before provider-request building. That is why `safety_identifier` (fully plumbed) survives while `store`/`prompt_cache_key` (allowlisted but not in the signature) vanish, with no error and no log line. ## Suggested fix Add `store: Optional[bool] = None` and `prompt_cache_key: Optional[str] = None` as named parameters to `get_optional_params()` in `litellm/utils.py` (and to `completion()`/`acompletion()` in `litellm/main.py`), mirroring exactly how `safety_identifier` was integrated. The supported-params lists and transformation mapping already handle the rest. ## Workaround Passing the params via `extra_body` bypasses the broken collection and produces a correct outbound body: ```python litellm.completion(..., extra_body={"store": False, "prompt_cache_key": "my-cache-key"}) ``` ## Environment - LiteLLM: `v1.90.2` (proxy and library both affected; also reproduced against current `main`, 2026-07-14) - Provider: `openai/*` chat completions (drop happens before provider dispatch, so any provider path via `get_optional_params` is affected) - Python 3.14 (not version-specific) ## Relevant log output No error and no warning is produced — that is the core of the problem: the parameters are accepted as supported and silently discarded. ## Related - #20989 added both params to the supported lists (intent was clearly to support them) — this issue is about the missing second half of that change. - #19225 is a different path (router fallback leaking the param to Bedrock), not this.

signal.title: fix(proxy): stop leaking the client_side_timeout marker to providers
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Setting any request timeout through the proxy broke strict providers - Bedrock returned 400 `client_side_timeout: Extra inputs are not permitted` - Body `timeout`/`request_timeout`/`stream_timeout` and `x-litellm-timeout` headers all triggered it How it solves it: - Registers `client_side_timeout` in the LiteLLM-only param list - The marker is now stripped before the provider payload is built - Router cooldown logic still sees it and keeps skipping caller-caused 408s ## User Flow Before: a developer who sets a request timeout gets a 400 from Bedrock instead of a completion 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "claude-sonnet-5", "timeout": 30` against a Bedrock deployment 2. The response is HTTP 400 with `BedrockException - {"message":"The model returned the following errors: client_side_timeout: Extra inputs are not permitted"}` 3. Sending the same request without a body timeout but with an `x-litellm-timeout: 30` header fails with the identical 400 4. Only requests with no timeout at all return 200 After: the same timeout-carrying requests complete normally 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "claude-sonnet-5", "timeout": 30` against a Bedrock deployment 2. The response is HTTP 200 with the model's completion 3. The same request with the `x-litellm-timeout: 30` header also returns 200 4. The timeout still applies: a deliberately tiny `x-litellm-timeout` still returns the usual 408 timeout error ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5755 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy booted with this config against real Bedrock (bearer token auth), `curl` as the client ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` ### Before (6d32d4081d) #### /v1/chat/completions with body `"timeout": 30` 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:31700/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi in one word"}],"max_tokens":10,"timeout":30}'` 2. HTTP 400: `{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {"message":"The model returned the following errors: client_side_timeout: Extra inputs are not permitted"}. signal.title: feat(complexity_router): custom classifier plugins via classifier_type 'custom'
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Complexity router offers only the built-in heuristic scorer or an LLM classifier - Operators cannot route tiers by their own business rules (team, spend, domain) - DB reconcile silently evicted every plugin-bearing auto-router one sync after startup How it solves it: - New `classifier_type: custom` runs an operator hook that returns the tier name - The hook reads request messages plus caller identity from the routing context - Failures, timeouts, and unknown tiers fall back exactly like a failed LLM classifier - Reconcile now resolves plugin dotted paths before hashing ids, so it stops evicting ## User Flow Before: a platform operator who wants their premium team routed to a stronger model has no way to teach the auto router that rule 1. They add `classifier_type: custom` with a `classifier_plugin` dotted path under `complexity_router_config` in their proxy config and start the proxy 2. Startup logs `Error creating deployment: 1 validation error for ComplexityRouterConfig, classifier_type: Input should be 'heuristic' or 'llm'` and drops the router 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "smart-router"` and get back `400 Invalid model name passed in model=smart-router` After: the same config routes each team where the operator's own rule says 1. They add the same `classifier_type: custom` block and start the proxy; startup lists the router normally 2. A member of team-research sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "smart-router"` and the reply comes back from the strong model 3. A member of team-support sends the identical prompt to the same URL and the reply comes back from the cheap model 4. In the logs page each request shows a routing decision with cause `classifier_plugin` and the tier the hook picked 5. If the hook errors or times out, the request still succeeds through the configured fallback and the decision row honestly reports which path ran ## Pre-Submission Checklist (optional but appreciated): - [x] I have included relevant documentation updates (stored in /docs/my-website) - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have added a screenshot or proof of the fix working locally - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] My PR passes all tests ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes New `classifier_type: "custom"` for the complexity router. A `ClassifierPlugin` protocol (async `classify(context) -> str | None`) sits next to `RoutingPlugin` in `litellm/types/router.py`; the hook receives the same `RoutingContext` routing plugins get, so caller identity (`user_api_key_team_id`, budgets, `user_api_key_auth_metadata`) is already in `context.metadata`. The returned tier name resolves through `resolve_classified_tier`, the same resolver the LLM verdict uses, so built-in tiers, `tier_labels`, and `tier_definitions` names all work; `tier_definitions` now accepts classifier_type `custom` alongside `llm`. A decline (`None`), raise, timeout (`classifier_plugin_timeout_ms`, default 3000), unknown tier, or tier without models falls back through the existing chain: `fallback_tier` on a custom tier set, else `classifier_fallback`. Routing decisions record the new `classifier_plugin` cause; fallback outcomes keep reporting the path that actually ran. The plugin resolves from a dotted path at proxy startup with a load-time check that `classify` is a coroutine function, and is closed off over HTTP like `plugins`. Session pinning stays enabled for classifier plugins (suppression remains for candidate-narrowing plugins, which are per-turn policy ceilings), and `adaptive` composes since it consumes the classified tier rather than producing it. Separate bug fix this surfaced: `_delete_deployment` re-reads the raw config and hashes `litellm_params` to compute the ids the config wants served, while the router's ids were hashed from the resolved params where plugin dotted paths are live instances. The mismatch made the DB reconcile evict every plugin-bearing auto-router one sync after startup, including routers using the existing `plugins` list. The fix pins `model_info.id` from the raw params at config load, before resolution swaps the dotted paths for instances, so both sides hash the same input by construction. The reconcile itself is untouched: it never imports plugin modules, a module broken on disk cannot stall cleanup for unrelated models, and any future param-transforming resolution is covered by the same pin. Considered and rejected: overloading `RoutingPlugin.run` with a tier side-channel in `context.signals` (a classifier produces a tier, it does not narrow candidates, and the two must compose), and a parallel router strategy package as in #30265 (a third value on the existing knob keeps one config surface). One asymmetry stated: `classifier_plugin` set while `classifier_type` is not `custom` raises at config load, stricter than how a stray `classifier_llm_config` is tolerated, because an operator who wired a hook and got silence is the worst failure mode and no UI writes this field defensively. UI is intentionally untouched (backend only): `classifier_plugin` holds a runtime object no JSON body can express, so the dashboard cannot create plugin routers. A follow-up will fix the two display mislabels (`autoRouterRows.ts` labels a plugin router "Heuristic"; the decision card renders the raw `classifier_plugin` cause string). ## Feature Demo Config (`classifier_plugin` resolves like `plugins` entries, module next to the config file): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: smart-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_default_model: claude-haiku complexity_router_config: classifier_type: custom classifier_plugin: custom_classifiers.tier_by_team classifier_plugin_timeout_ms: 3000 tiers: SIMPLE: claude-haiku REASONING: claude-sonnet ``` ```python # custom_classifiers.py class TierByTeam: async def classify(self, context): team = context.metadata.get("user_api_key_team_alias") return "REASONING" if team == "team-research" else "SIMPLE" tier_by_team = TierByTeam() ``` ## Proof it works: live proxy Live proxy on localhost:4472 (worktree venv, Postgres 16 in docker), master key auth, two teams (`team-research`, `team-support`) with one virtual key each, minted via POST /team/new and /key/generate. Every provider credential on this machine is currently dead (OpenAI and Anthropic both out of credits, Azure resource 404s, sandbox gateway token expired), so the tier models point at a local recording upstream serving /v1/chat/completions with distinct model names; the request path through auth, metadata stamping, classification, tier pools, and spend logging is the real one end to end. The three curls below rerun unchanged against real providers once a credential has credit. ### Before (base e2d8fc919f): plugin mode rejected at startup ``` 19:05:45 - LiteLLM Router:ERROR - router.py:7749 - Error creating deployment: 1 validation error for ComplexityRouterConfig classifier_type Input should be 'heuristic' or 'llm' [type=literal_error, input_value='plugin', input_type=str] ``` and the router never loads: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4472/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEARCH_KEY" \ -d '{"model": "smart-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' {"error":{"message":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=smart-router. ..."}} ``` ### After (PR tip): same prompt, two teams, two tiers ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4472/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEARCH_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "smart-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' reply: served by claude-sonnet-5 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4472/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "smart-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' reply: served by claude-haiku-4-5 ``` ### After: broken plugin falls back instead of failing the request `broken-router` uses a hook that raises on every call: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4472/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEARCH_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "broken-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' reply: served by claude-haiku-4-5 ``` with the proxy warning `ComplexityRouter: classifier plugin failed (tier lookup service is down), falling back to heuristic` ### After: spend logs attribute the decision honestly ``` $ docker exec clsplugin-pg psql -U postgres -t -A -c "select model_group, metadata::jsonb->'routing_decision'->>'cause', metadata::jsonb->'routing_decision'->>'tier', metadata::jsonb->'routing_decision'->'signals' from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" order by \"startTime\" desc limit 4;" smart-router|classifier_plugin|REASONING|["classifier-plugin:REASONING"] smart-router|classifier_plugin|SIMPLE|["classifier-plugin:SIMPLE"] broken-router|heuristic_scorer|SIMPLE|["short (7 tokens)", "simple (what is)"] ``` The plugin rows carry no score key (a plugin produces a tier, not a score); the fallback row reports the heuristic scorer with its score and signals, because cause records the path that ran ### After: routers survive the DB reconcile (the bug fix), stale deployments still evict ``` t+0s models: ['claude-haiku', 'claude-sonnet', 'smart-router', 'broken-router'] t+75s models: ['claude-haiku', 'claude-sonnet', 'smart-router', 'broken-router'] ``` Before the fix both auto-routers disappeared from /v1/models one reconcile (~1s) after startup and every request to them returned the 400 above ## Linear ticket ## Tests - `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_complexity_router.py`: config validation both directions, dispatch (plugin mode never invokes the scorer or the LLM), the full fallback matrix (decline, raise, timeout under a real wait_for, unknown tier, tier without pool, each against both classifier_fallback values and against fallback_tier on a custom tier set), composition with the narrowing plugins list, tier pinning kept enabled for classifier plugins, and routing decision contents (cause, no score, signal marker) - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py`: dotted path resolution, rejection of non-classifier objects and synchronous classify methods at config load, live instances passed through untouched - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_auto_router_endpoints.py`: classifier_plugin not settable over HTTP - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_update_llm_router_resilience.py`: plugin-bearing config models survive the reconcile; both tests fail with the fix reverted (verified). A broken plugin module at reconcile time skips cleanup instead of evicting valid deployments `make check` passes (ruff, budgets, basedpyright, dashboard API type sync) ## Caveats / follow-ups - Provider legs of the live proof ran against a local recording upstream because every provider credential on this machine is out of credits; the curls rerun unchanged against real providers - UI follow-up: add the plugin mode to the classifier picker as display-only and fix the two mislabels noted above - Docs follow-up: the classifier plugin guide goes to the litellm-docs repository per the docs convention; the package README stays code-focused - The LLM classifier keeps its pre-existing gap where a valid built-in tier with no configured pool escapes classifier_fallback; plugin mode does not inherit it, and closing it for the LLM path is a separate change <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit a77ed0e20994e6522109938f0d4f536946e54bae. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Bug]: Spend logs only record the first tool call and first LLM round for chained MCP calls on streaming /responses (require_approval="never")
signal.text: - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? When a streaming `/responses` request includes an MCP tool with `"require_approval": "never"` and the model chains several tool calls (model calls a tool, the gateway auto-executes it and calls the model again, the model calls another tool, then answers), the logs page and the spend logs table only show one row for the first MCP tool call and one row for a single LLM call. The follow-up LLM calls and every tool call after the first never get their own log entries. Expected: one spend log row per LLM call in the chain and one per tool execution. A side effect is that spend is undercounted, since tokens from the follow-up rounds are never written to spend logs I looked into why, and two things combine to cause it: 1. Every chained LLM call reuses the parent request's logging object. The follow-up calls copy the original request params (which contain `litellm_logging_obj` and `litellm_call_id`) in `litellm/responses/mcp/mcp_streaming_iterator.py` (`_create_follow_up_iterator`), so all rounds share one `Logging` object. `dispatch_success_handlers` in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` has a one-shot guard (`has_dispatched_final_stream_success`), so only the first round's `response.completed` ever reaches the success callbacks. The non-streaming path hits the same wall via `has_logged_async_success` 2. Every MCP tool call row is written with the same `request_id`. In `litellm/responses/mcp/litellm_proxy_mcp_handler.py` (`_execute_tool_calls`), `tool_logging_call_id` falls back to the parent `litellm_call_id` for every tool call in every round, and since a `CallToolResult` has no `id`, the spend row's `request_id` ends up identical for all of them. `request_id` is the primary key and inserts use `create_many(skip_duplicates=True)`, so only the first tool call row survives The same two problems exist in the chat completions MCP path (`litellm/responses/mcp/chat_completions_handler.py`) ## User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app streams `/responses` through an MCP tool with auto-execution sees most of the chain missing from the logs page, and the request is billed for less than it cost 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": true` and `tools: [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy", "require_approval": "never"}]` 2. The stream shows the model calling tool A (an `mcp_call` event), the gateway executing it, a follow-up model call, the model calling tool B, and a final follow-up with the answer text, ending in `response.completed` 3. Their app received the full chain over SSE, so the end user sees a correct answer 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see only one tool-call row (tool A) and one model row for the whole request; tool B and the two follow-up model calls have no rows 5. The key's reported spend for that request only includes the first model round's tokens After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request produces a log row for every model call and every tool call in the chain, and the spend matches what the provider actually billed 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": true` and `tools: [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy", "require_approval": "never"}]` 2. The stream shows the model calling tool A (an `mcp_call` event), the gateway executing it, a follow-up model call, the model calling tool B, and a final follow-up with the answer text, ending in `response.completed` 3. Their app received the full chain over SSE, so the end user sees a correct answer 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see one row per model call (three, each with its own response id) and one row per tool call (A and B) 5. The key's reported spend for that request includes every round's tokens ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: standard proxy config with an MCP server configured, and the client sends a tool entry `{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy", "require_approval": "never"}` on a streaming `/responses` request Version or commit: v1.97.0 How the bug was observed: I noticed this from my app rather than from a synthetic repro. My app stores the tool calls and their results to send them back on the next turn, and after a completed streamed response that contained several chained MCP tool calls, I realized some of those tool calls and follow-up model calls had no matching entries in LiteLLM's spend logs at all. The generation itself succeeded and the final answer was correct, so the gap is only on the logging side. I can provide screenshots of the logs page alongside the corresponding app-side tool call records if that would help ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0

signal.title: [Bug]: Batch/Files upload loses model/deployment routing when forwarded to a second LiteLLM proxy
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Uploading a file for the Batch API fails when one LiteLLM proxy is configured with a model deployment whose `api_base` points at a second LiteLLM proxy (a chained-proxy setup). The request that reaches the second proxy is a bare `/v1/files` upload with no `target_model_names` and no `model`, so it cannot be routed to the correct backend deployment on the second proxy. **Setup:** proxy A has `gpt-4.1-batch` configured with `litellm_params.model: openai/gpt-4.1-batch` pointing at proxy B's `api_base`. Client uploads with `client.files.create(file=..., purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": "gpt-4.1-batch"})` against proxy A. This is the documented managed-files pattern and works fine against a single proxy. Traceback confirms the request reaches proxy A's managed-files hook correctly (enterprise license, `target_model_names` present): ``` files_endpoints.py:route_create_file -> managed_files_obj.acreate_file managed_files.py:create_file_for_each_model -> llm_router.acreate_file router.py:create_file_for_deployment -> litellm.acreate_file files/main.py:acreate_file -> openai/openai.py:acreate_file openai_client.files.create(**create_file_data) ``` The bug is in `router.py::create_file_for_deployment` (`Router._acreate_file`): it builds the downstream `litellm.acreate_file(**{**data, "custom_llm_provider": custom_llm_provider, ..., **kwargs_copy})` call from only the deployment's static `litellm_params` plus the original `file`/`purpose` kwargs. It never forwards `target_model_names` or the resolved model into the downstream request. As a result, proxy B receives a bare upload, `custom_llm_provider` defaults to `"openai"` (the `Form` default in `files_endpoints.py::create_file`), and proxy B has no way to know which of its own deployments the file was meant for. If proxy B has no matching model/provider hint, it raises `files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.` (from `get_files_provider_config`). If a `files_settings` fallback entry is added on proxy B keyed to whatever provider it defaults to, credentials attach but the request still goes to the wrong endpoint shape for the actual target deployment (e.g., an OpenAI-shaped `/v1/files` call against an Azure-backed deployment returns a 404), because the original deployment identity was never recoverable. ## Expected behavior `create_file_for_deployment` should forward `target_model_names` (or the resolved model) to the downstream `acreate_file` call, e.g. via `extra_body`, so a second-hop LiteLLM proxy can route the upload to the correct deployment using the same managed-files mechanism, instead of falling back to a bare default provider. ## Related issues https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31867 documents the same class of bug for chat completions: `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig.transform_request()` silently drops internal routing metadata (`tags`, `litellm_session_id`) when one LiteLLM proxy forwards to another LiteLLM proxy as its backend. This issue is the Batch/Files equivalent, in a different code path (`router.py::create_file_for_deployment` rather than `litellm_proxy/chat/transformation.py`). ### Steps to Reproduce We reproduced this with a minimal repro chain (self-hosted Proxy A -> self-hosted Proxy B (intermediate proxy) -> Azure, Azure-only, no third-party proxy involved) and confirmed each stage: 1. No `files_settings` on the intermediate proxy: `files_settings is not set`. 2. `files_settings` keyed to a provider that doesn't match the bare upload's resolved provider: `api_key client option must be set` (fallback entry never selected). 3. `files_settings` keyed to match: credentials attach, but the intermediate proxy issues an OpenAI-shaped request against an Azure endpoint: `404 Resource not found`. ### Relevant log output ```shell Error code: 500 - {'error': {'message': 'files_settings is not set, set it on your config.yaml file.', 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': '500'}} Error code: 500 - {'error': {'message': 'The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable', 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': '500'}} Error code: 404 - {'error': {'code': '404', 'message': 'Resource not found'}} ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? `v1.91.3` (also confirmed unfixed in `v1.95.0`) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(azure_ai): strip non-OpenAI-spec message fields before request
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code multi-turn on `azure_ai` Foundry deployments fails with 400 - Assistant history carries `thinking_blocks` and nested `provider_specific_fields` - Strict OpenAI-compatible backends (Fireworks-served) reject them: "Extra inputs are not permitted" How it solves it: - `azure_ai` strips `thinking_blocks`, `provider_specific_fields`, `cache_control` before sending - Recursive strip also clears `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields` - Runs on a deep copy so fallbacks keep the original history - Mirrors what `fireworks_ai` and `mistral` already do ## User Flow Before: a developer running Claude Code through the proxy against a Fireworks-served Azure AI Foundry deployment gets a 400 on the second turn of every session 1. The proxy admin adds a deployment `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3` (or `azure_ai/fw-glm-5.2`) pointing at the Foundry endpoint and key 2. The developer sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to `https://litellm-domain` and starts Claude Code on that model 3. Their first prompt sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` and gets 200 back with a `thinking` block and the assistant's text 4. Claude Code sends the next `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with that assistant turn echoed back in `messages` 5. It gets HTTP 400 `Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[2].thinking_blocks'` and shows "API Error: 400"; every later turn fails the same way After: the second turn succeeds and the session keeps going 1. The proxy admin adds a deployment `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3` (or `azure_ai/fw-glm-5.2`) pointing at the Foundry endpoint and key 2. The developer sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to `https://litellm-domain` and starts Claude Code on that model 3. Their first prompt sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` and gets 200 back with a `thinking` block and the assistant's text 4. Claude Code sends the next `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with that assistant turn echoed back in `messages` 5. It gets 200 with the assistant's next reply and the session continues; tool-use turns that carry a thought signature go through the same way ## Relevant issues Fixes #33961 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5221 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live e2e run against a real Azure AI Foundry resource with a Fireworks-hosted `FW-Kimi-K3` deployment (a reasoning model, so every response carries reasoning content). Same proxy config on both legs, booted from the named commit with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port <port> --detailed_debug` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: FW-Kimi-K3 litellm_params: model: azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-1221 ``` Case 1 is the reported flow: real Claude Code pointed at the proxy (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-qa-1221 claude --model FW-Kimi-K3`), a two-turn conversation on `/v1/messages`. Case 2 is `/v1/chat/completions` with turn 1's assistant message echoed back verbatim in turn 2, the standard multi-turn client behavior: ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1221' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"FW-Kimi-K3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2? Answer in one word."}]}' > r1.json python3 -c " import json msg = json.load(open('r1.json'))['choices'][0]['message'] json.dump({'model': 'FW-Kimi-K3', 'messages': [ {'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is 2+2? Answer in one word.'}, msg, {'role': 'user', 'content': 'Now multiply that by 10. One word.'}]}, open('r2.json', 'w'))" curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1221' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @r2.json ``` Case 3 repeats the same echo-back shape on `/v1/responses` (turn 1's output items, a `reasoning` item plus a `message` item, echoed into turn 2's `input`) ### Before (6d32d4081d, litellm_internal_staging without this PR) Claude Code turn 1 answers, turn 2 dies with exactly the reported error: ``` > What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence. Thought for 1s (ctrl+o to expand) * 2+2 equals 4. > Now multiply that result by 10. * API Error: 400 litellm.BadRequestError: Azure_aiException - {"error":{"object":"error","type":"invalid_request_error", "code":"invalid_request_error","message":"Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[3].thinking_blocks', value: [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'The user is asking a simple arithmetic question...', 'signature': '', 'cache_control': {}}]"}} ``` The `/v1/chat/completions` round trip fails the same way: turn 1 returns 200 with message keys `content, provider_specific_fields, reasoning_content, role`, and echoing that message back gets ``` {"error": {"message": "litellm.BadRequestError: Azure_aiException - {\"error\":{...\"message\":\"Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[1].provider_specific_fields'\"}}...", "code": "400"}} 400 ``` The `/v1/responses` round trip returns 200 on both turns even here: that bridge never forwards the internal keys, so it is unaffected by the bug ### After (c6b40e9232, PR tip) Claude Code turn 2 now completes: ``` > What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence. Thought for 1s (ctrl+o to expand) * 2+2 equals 4. > Now multiply that result by 10. Thought for 1s (ctrl+o to expand) * 4 multiplied by 10 equals 40. ``` The `/v1/chat/completions` echo-back turn 2 returns 200 with content `Forty.`, and `/v1/responses` stays 200 on both turns, so no regression there. The backend accepted the echoed `reasoning_content` on the after leg, which confirms scoping the strip to `thinking_blocks`, `provider_specific_fields`, and `cache_control` is right. The added unit tests additionally assert the nested `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields` case from the issue is stripped while `content` and `tool_calls` are preserved, and that the caller's own message objects are not mutated ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Scope is `azure_ai` only; the `openai`-provider case in #32188 is a different path - `reasoning_content` is left in place; Fireworks-served backends accept it on replay ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- Disclosure from the author: I'm still newish to this codebase and paired with Claude Code to trace the adapter and transform path and to run the before/after proxy capture above. I read through the change myself and confirmed it against the issue's repro; glad to adjust anything - [x] c6b40e9232 passes /live-pr-risk <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit c6b40e923233df93f2b15d1c88ddbee9ebb71b36. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix: use resolved credentials in health checks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Hosted vLLM health checks discard resolved credentials - Healthy deployments can be reported as unavailable How it solves it: - Propagates the resolved API base into health checks - Propagates the resolved API key into health checks - Adds focused regression coverage for both values ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin health-checks a hosted vLLM deployment, but the check does not use the provider-resolved endpoint and credentials 1. The admin configures a `hosted_vllm/` model with its endpoint and API key 2. They send `GET http://localhost:4000/health` with the proxy master key 3. The deployment appears in `unhealthy_endpoints` with an authentication error 4. The admin configures the same `hosted_vllm/` model with its endpoint and API key 2. They send `GET http://localhost:4000/health` with the proxy master key 3. The health check sends the provider-resolved API base and API key upstream 4. signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Seven dashboard forms still used antd Form - Collapsed cache settings were silently dropped on save - Adding a provider discount fired two identical requests - These screens had light-only greys, so no dark mode How it solves it: - Moves each form onto react-hook-form plus the shadcn field kit - Keeps collapsed values in form state so saves stop dropping them - Drops the leftover form wrapper that double-fired the discount request - Swaps the neutral greys in touched files for semantic tokens - Verified in jsdom with repro steps, not a live proxy ## User Flow Before: an admin who has a Redis namespace and TTL configured loses both the moment they save any cache setting, unless they happen to expand Advanced Settings first 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=caching and see Cache Settings with Redis already configured 2. Advanced Settings is collapsed by default, so Namespace, TTL and Max Connections are not on screen 3. They change Host and press Save Changes, and the page reports success 4. They reload the page and expand Advanced Settings 5. Namespace, TTL and Max Connections are now blank, and the SSL toggle has flipped itself off After: the same save keeps every setting the admin never touched 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=caching and see Cache Settings with Redis already configured 2. Advanced Settings is collapsed by default, so Namespace, TTL and Max Connections are not on screen 3. They change Host and press Save Changes, and the page reports success 4. They reload the page and expand Advanced Settings 5. Namespace, TTL and Max Connections still hold their previous values, and SSL is still on ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screenshots are still to be captured against a live proxy, so this section carries the reproduction steps rather than images. Both behaviour changes are reproducible by hand and the steps below run identically at each hash. Where a step reports a payload I measured, it says jsdom, because that measurement came from the test environment and not from a live request. Shared setup: check out the hash, run `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` on a free port, point it at a proxy with Redis caching configured, and open the pages named below ### Before (035bd76669b210c0f385a76002064df355ebbea7) #### Case 1: cache settings survive a save with Advanced Settings collapsed 1. Configure the cache with a Host, a Namespace, a TTL and SSL enabled, then save with Advanced Settings expanded 2. Reload http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=caching and leave Advanced Settings collapsed 3. Change Host and press Save Changes 4. Reload the page and expand Advanced Settings 5. Observe Namespace, TTL and Max Connections blank, and SSL off 6. Payload measured in jsdom at this hash: the collapsed save sent `{type, host, port, ssl: false, ssl_check_hostname: false}`, dropping `namespace`, `ttl` and `max_connections` and inverting the loaded `ssl: true` #### Case 2: adding a provider discount issues one request, by click and by Enter 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-tracking and expand Provider Discounts 2. Press Add Provider Discount, pick a provider, enter 5, then press Add Provider Discount 3. With the browser network tab open, observe two identical requests for the single click 4. Repeat, but press Enter in the discount field instead of clicking, and observe two again 5. Measured in jsdom at this hash: each path produced two invocations with identical arguments ### After (00d1fa76f5672096d789fc05d104f6fc41ddfffe) #### Case 1: cache settings survive a save with Advanced Settings collapsed 1. Configure the cache with a Host, a Namespace, a TTL and SSL enabled, then save with Advanced Settings expanded 2. Reload http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=caching and leave Advanced Settings collapsed 3. Change Host and press Save Changes 4. Reload the page and expand Advanced Settings 5. Observe Namespace, TTL and Max Connections unchanged, and SSL still on 6. Payload measured in jsdom at this hash: the collapsed save sent `{type, host, port, ssl: true, ssl_check_hostname: false, namespace, ttl, max_connections}`, byte-identical to the expanded save #### Case 2: adding a provider discount issues one request, by click and by Enter 1. With the browser network tab open, observe a single request for the single click 4. Repeat, but press Enter in the discount field instead of clicking, and observe a single request 5. Measured in jsdom at this hash: each path produced one invocation, carrying the same arguments as before ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Payload parity proven in jsdom, not yet on a proxy - Caching parity rests on pre-existing tests kept green unedited - Advanced cache values now persist, so collapsed saves change payloads - Discount add drops from two requests to one - Margin modal never had Enter submission; left inert and pinned - Role trigger shows the role name; antd also showed its hint - CloudZero destination picker stays antd; check its labels when converted - Alerting integer fields still submit strings, matching today's behaviour - Alerting text fields save literal [object Object]; pre-existing, preserved here - Modals and tables keep antd, so those shells stay unthemed - Three files also carry open Tremor PRs; second to land rebases - CoordinationRedisTypeSelector has a flaky pre-existing test, untouched here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(azure_ai): strip non-spec thinking_blocks/provider_specific_fields before strict OpenAI-compatible backends
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #33961 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live e2e against a real strict OpenAI-compatible backend: an `azure_ai/*` deployment pointed at Fireworks (`glm-5.2`), which enforces `additionalProperties: false` and rejects unknown message fields. A multi-turn Anthropic `/v1/messages` request whose assistant turn carries a thinking block is routed through the `AnthropicAdapter`, which attaches `thinking_blocks` to the outbound OpenAI-format message. Request body (`repro_msg.json`) sends messages `[user, assistant(thinking + text), user]`. Before the fix (base `bd44c9e305`) ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @repro_msg.json HTTP 400 $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @repro_msg.json litellm.BadRequestError: Azure_aiException - {"error":{"object":"error","type":"invalid_request_error", "code":"invalid_request_error","message":"Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[1].thinking_blocks', value: [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': '2+2 is basic arithmetic equal to 4.', 'signature': 'fake-sig-abc123', 'cache_control': {}}]"}}. Received Model Group=fw-glm-5.2 ``` After the fix (`4e406e1cfe`) ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @repro_msg.json HTTP 200 ``` The same repro also confirms `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields` (the adapter attaches `thought_signature` there) is stripped, since `filter_value_from_dict` recurses. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AzureAIStudioConfig._transform_messages` now strips LiteLLM's output-only, non-spec fields from every message before the request leaves for the backend, matching what `fireworks_ai` and `mistral` already do. The stripped fields are `thinking_blocks`, `reasoning_content`, and `provider_specific_fields`. ```python NON_SPEC_MESSAGE_FIELDS = ("thinking_blocks", "provider_specific_fields", "reasoning_content") for message in messages: if isinstance(message, dict): for field in self.NON_SPEC_MESSAGE_FIELDS: filter_value_from_dict(message, field) # recurses -> also drops # tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields ... ``` `filter_value_from_dict` (existing helper in `prompt_templates/common_utils.py`) walks the message tree, so it removes both the message-level fields and the nested `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields` that the `AnthropicAdapter` sets for `thought_signature`. These fields are output-only artifacts LiteLLM attaches to assistant responses; replaying them on a follow-up turn to a backend with `additionalProperties: false` triggers the 400. Regression test added in `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure_ai/chat/test_azure_ai_transformation.py::test_transform_messages_strips_non_spec_thinking_and_provider_fields` asserting all three message-level fields and the nested tool-call field are removed while spec fields (content, tool call id/name) are preserved. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/abce2b25bdf646d88ad17ea03575b4b7

signal.title: fix(azure_ai): strip Anthropic-only fields that strict backends reject
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #33961 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a pure message-transformation bug (no upstream call needed to trigger it), so the reproduction below drives `AzureAIStudioConfig._transform_messages` with the assistant message an Anthropic-format client echoes back through the Anthropic-messages adapter (a thinking block, a nested tool-call thought signature, and cache_control) before, base at `1ebf2a78a9` ``` thinking_blocks present: True message provider_specific_fields: True message cache_control: True tool_calls fn provider_specific: True ``` after, this PR at `b29e9e5ad5` ``` thinking_blocks present: False message provider_specific_fields: False message cache_control: False tool_calls fn provider_specific: False tool_calls fn name preserved: read_file ``` Reproduction script: ```python from litellm.llms.azure_ai.chat.transformation import AzureAIStudioConfig messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read a file."}, { "role": "assistant", "content": "I can help.", "thinking_blocks": [{"type": "thinking", "thinking": "let me read it", "signature": "", "cache_control": {}}], "provider_specific_fields": {"foo": "bar"}, "tool_calls": [{"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{}", "provider_specific_fields": {"thought_signature": "abc"}}}], "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}, }, ] asst = AzureAIStudioConfig()._transform_messages(messages, model="azure_ai/fw-glm-5.2")[1] print("thinking_blocks" in asst, "provider_specific_fields" in asst, "cache_control" in asst, "provider_specific_fields" in asst["tool_calls"][0]["function"]) ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Anthropic-format clients such as Claude Code echo prior assistant turns that carry `thinking` blocks. For the `azure_ai` provider there is no native Anthropic-messages config, so the request routes through the Anthropic-messages adapter, which reattaches those onto the outbound OpenAI-format assistant message as a `thinking_blocks` field, a `provider_specific_fields` thought signature nested inside `tool_calls[].function`, and `cache_control` annotations. None of these are OpenAI chat-completions schema fields `AzureAIStudioConfig._transform_messages` previously only converted list content to a string, so those fields survived serialization and reached the Azure AI Foundry backend. Strict OpenAI-compatible upstreams there (for example Fireworks) set `additionalProperties: false`, so they reject the request with `Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[n].thinking_blocks'` (and, on tool-use turns, `messages[n].tool_calls[m].function.provider_specific_fields`), breaking multi-turn tool use `_transform_messages` now strips `thinking_blocks`, `provider_specific_fields`, and `cache_control` from each message with the existing recursive `filter_value_from_dict` helper, so the nested tool-call thought signature is removed too, not just the message-level fields. This mirrors what `fireworks_ai` (`_transform_messages_helper`) and `mistral` already do. Legitimate fields (content, tool-call name and arguments) are preserved. The new test in the mapped `test_azure_ai_transformation.py` asserts all four fields are stripped (it fails on the pre-fix code) and that the tool-call name and content survive

signal.title: [Bug]: Azure AI Foundry (`azure_ai`) forwards non-spec `thinking_blocks` to strict OpenAI-compatible backends
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? I point Claude Code at the LiteLLM proxy and route to a Fireworks model (fw-glm-5.2) deployed on Azure AI Foundry via the `azure_ai` provider. The first turn works. As soon as an assistant turn that contained a `thinking` block is echoed back as history (which Anthropic-format clients like Claude Code always do on multi-turn tool-use), the next request fails with HTTP 400 from the upstream: ```json {"error":{"object":"error","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_request_error","message":"Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[2].thinking_blocks', value: [{'type': 'thinking','thinking': 'The user wants me to read a file. Let me read it.','signature': '','cache_control': {}}]"}} ``` This happens on a simple "read a file" turn, i.e. the second message after a thinking-bearing assistant response. ### Root cause Claude Code talks to the proxy in Anthropic `/v1/messages` format. For the `azure_ai` provider there is no native Anthropic-messages config, so `anthropic_messages_handler` routes through `LiteLLMMessagesToCompletionTransformationHandler` -> `AnthropicAdapter.translate_completion_input_params_with_tool_mapping`. That adapter collects `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` content blocks and attaches them as a `thinking_blocks` field on the outbound OpenAI-format assistant message: `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py`, assistant-message branch: ```python assistant_message = ChatCompletionAssistantMessage( role="assistant", content=assistant_content, thinking_blocks=(thinking_blocks if len(thinking_blocks) > 0 else None), ) ... if len(thinking_blocks) > 0: assistant_message["thinking_blocks"] = thinking_blocks ``` `thinking_blocks` is not part of the OpenAI chat-completions message schema. The request then flows to `AzureAIStudioConfig.transform_request` -> `_transform_messages`, which only converts content lists to strings and passes images/audio through; it does **not** strip `thinking_blocks` nor the nested Anthropic thought signature the adapter attaches at `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields` (nor the Anthropic `cache_control` annotation). Those fields survive serialization and reach the Fireworks-via-Azure endpoint, whose chat-message schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, so it rejects them with `Extra inputs are not permitted`. By contrast, the direct `fireworks_ai` provider (`FireworksAIConfig._transform_messages_helper`) and the `mistral` provider (`MistralConfig._strip_output_only_fields`) already strip a subset of these fields. ### Related #32188 is the same symptom (`thinking_blocks` forwarded to a strict chat/completions upstream, breaking Claude Code multi-turn) but a different provider path: it covers the `openai` provider under the `LITELLM_USE_CHAT_COMPLETIONS_URL_FOR_ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES` opt-out flag (the Responses-API escape path, which today only routes `openai` through the Responses API). This issue covers the `azure_ai` (Azure AI Foundry) provider, which always routes through chat/completions and is unaffected by that flag. A fix for `AzureAIStudioConfig._transform_messages` is complementary and does not resolve #32188. #15758 was a Databricks-specific case, closed by the reporter. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Proxy config: an `azure_ai/<model>` deployment pointing at an Azure AI Foundry endpoint hosting a Fireworks model with strict request validation (e.g. fw-glm-5.2). 2. POST `/v1/messages` with an assistant turn carrying a thinking block (what an Anthropic client echoes back): ```json {"model": "<alias>", "max_tokens": 512, "stream": true, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024}, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read a file."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user wants me to read a file. Let me read it.", "signature": ""}, {"type": "text", "text": "I can help."}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "go ahead"}]} ``` 3. The upstream returns `400 Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[2].thinking_blocks'`. 4. A second, distinct 400 surfaces on multi-turn tool use once the thinking block is handled: the adapter attaches the thought signature at `tool_calls[].function.provider_specific_fields`, which Fireworks also rejects with `400 Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[n].tool_calls[m].function.provider_specific_fields'`. 5. End-to-end: point Claude Code at the proxy (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) and run any 2-turn tool-using task; it fails on the first turn after a thinking-bearing assistant message. ### Relevant log output ```shell {"error":{"object":"error","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_request_error","message":"Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[2].thinking_blocks', value: [{'type': 'thinking','thinking': 'The user wants me to read a file. Let me read it.','signature': '','cache_control': {}}]"}} ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.92.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: Chained proxy batch results: output_file_id from the second proxy is not fetchable through the first
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? In a chained proxy setup (proxy A has a `litellm_proxy/` deployment whose `api_base` points at proxy B), file upload and batch create/retrieve work end to end since #36240. But the `output_file_id` and `error_file_id` that proxy B mints on a completed batch pass through proxy A without being rewrapped into ids proxy A can route. Fetching the batch output content through proxy A fails with a routing error, so results are only retrievable by calling proxy B directly, which defeats the point of fronting it with proxy A Expected: after polling a completed batch through proxy A, fetching the output file content through proxy A returns the batch results, same as it does in a single-proxy managed files setup ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running batches through a front proxy that forwards to a second proxy cannot download their results from the front proxy 1. They send POST https://front-proxy/v1/files as multipart with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-5.6-batch`, and their JSONL file, and get 200 with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches with that `input_file_id` and get a batch id 3. GET https://front-proxy/v1/batches/{batch_id} eventually returns `status: completed` with an `output_file_id` 4. GET https://front-proxy/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns 400 `You passed in model=0ed8a2e0867ab6b8ec414ffc609f3bd1afa487f34713b18c423bcbcfd44f0267. There are no healthy deployments for this model` 5. The same GET against the second proxy directly returns the results, so they must hold credentials for a proxy they were never meant to talk to After a (hypothetical) fix: the same steps end with the results coming back from the front proxy 1. They send POST https://front-proxy/v1/files as multipart with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-5.6-batch`, and their JSONL file, and get 200 with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches with that `input_file_id` and get a batch id 3. GET https://front-proxy/v1/batches/{batch_id} eventually returns `status: completed` with an `output_file_id` 4. GET https://front-proxy/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns 200 with the JSONL batch results, and they never need the second proxy's URL or key ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: Proxy B (port 33417), real OpenAI key in env: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-batch litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.5 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-...b ``` Proxy A (port 25002), key redacted: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-batch litellm_params: model: litellm_proxy/gpt-5.6-batch api_base: http://localhost:33417 api_key: sk-...b general_settings: master_key: sk-...a ``` Both proxies ran with a Postgres `DATABASE_URL` set Version or commit: 76a2340685 (PR #36240 tip merged on litellm_internal_staging 852368d72f) Commands and their full output: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-...a" -F purpose="batch" -F target_model_names="gpt-5.6-batch" -F file=@batch.jsonl # 200: {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07dW5pZmll...","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} curl -s http://localhost:25002/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-...a" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id": "<id from upload>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h", "model": "gpt-5.6-batch"}' # 200, then polling GET /v1/batches/<batch id> reaches: # {"status": "completed", "request_counts": {"completed": 1, "failed": 0, "total": 1}, "model": "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23", "output_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29u..."} curl -s "http://localhost:25002/v1/files/<output_file_id>/content" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-...a" # {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=0ed8a2e0867ab6b8ec414ffc609f3bd1afa487f34713b18c423bcbcfd44f0267. There are no healthy deployments for this model. ...","code":"400"}} curl -s "http://localhost:33417/v1/files/<output_file_id>/content" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-...b" # 200: {"id": "batch_req_6a84c37218688190a8fd11c3102b7c4c", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, ... "content": "Hello" ...}} ``` ### What a fix PR should look like When proxy A's managed batch polling stores a completed batch, the `output_file_id` and `error_file_id` coming back from a `litellm_proxy/` deployment are proxy B unified ids. Proxy A should rewrap them into its own unified file ids bound to the same deployment (the way it wraps the input file at upload), so a later content fetch through proxy A decodes to proxy B's id and forwards the call to proxy B with the deployment's credentials. The batch retrieve path in the managed batches hook and the file content routing in the managed files hook are the places to touch; QA is the exact curl chain above ending in a 200 through proxy A ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 76a2340685 (post #36240) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
