signal.title: [Feature]: Support native CLI login with OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I searched the existing issues and checked that this issue is not a duplicate. ### Feature description Please support standard native-application login for internal and third-party CLIs through LiteLLM Proxy. A developer should be able to configure only the LiteLLM Proxy base URL, authenticate through the enterprise identity provider in the external system browser with OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code and PKCE, and use a per-user credential without manually provisioning or copying a virtual key. Our concrete deployment is LiteLLM Proxy as the LLM gateway, OneLogin as the identity provider, existing AuthID/Beyond Identity MFA, and an internal Go CLI that launches OpenCode against LiteLLM's OpenAI-compatible routes. We may support other coding agents later. Developers should not need per-developer OneLogin issuer or client configuration. The resulting requests must retain the authenticated user's and team/organization's identity for model access, budgets, rate limits, spend, and auditing. [PR #35234](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/35234) is a related prototype, but this request intentionally leaves the credential architecture, discovery contract, and implementation open. For the first browser-capable CLI increment, the observable behavior should be: 1. The developer configures the CLI with the LiteLLM Proxy base URL. 2. The CLI discovers native OAuth/OIDC support and non-secret client configuration through a documented, versioned contract. 3. Login uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE `S256`. 4. Authentication opens the external system browser, never an embedded webview. 5. The redirect uses a loopback address with an OS-assigned local port. 6. The normal enterprise SSO and MFA policies run at OneLogin. 7. No client secret is embedded in or distributed with the CLI. 8. LiteLLM Proxy accepts the resulting per-user bearer credential. 9. The CLI securely reuses and refreshes the session where possible. 10. Logout removes the local session. 11. Our Go wrapper can launch OpenCode with the credential without copying a virtual key. 12. Requests remain attributable to the authenticated user and team/organization. 13. Existing API-key users and proxy-mediated login remain compatible. 14. The contract is documented for non-Python CLIs. The implementation may use an IdP token or a LiteLLM session credential, choose the discovery endpoint/schema, and choose the secure-storage mechanism and package layout. It should not depend on the architecture of PR #35234. Out of scope for this issue: - Device Authorization Grant for headless or remote-browser SSH sessions; that can be a follow-up. - Embedded-browser authentication. - Resource Owner Password Credentials. - Direct SAML in the CLI. - DPoP or other proof-of-possession work. - Modifying every third-party coding agent. - Replacing API-key authentication. - Requiring raw IdP access tokens as the only credential design. ### User Flow The hostname `https://llm.example.com` below is sanitized; the route paths are the real routes the client would use. #### Before this feature (today) Today the flow dead-ends before our Go wrapper can start a native browser login, so each developer must separately obtain and store a long-lived virtual key. 1. The developer configures the internal Go wrapper with the LiteLLM Proxy base URL `https://llm.example.com`. 2. The wrapper sends `GET https://llm.example.com/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` and receives the current discovery/config response, which has no documented native-client OAuth/OIDC contract for a non-Python CLI. 3. The developer cannot start an external-system-browser Authorization Code + PKCE login through the proxy URL; the current `lite login` remains proxy-mediated and the default-branch CLI has no browser-native flow option. 4. As a workaround, the developer separately obtains a LiteLLM virtual key and stores it in an environment variable or local configuration for the Go wrapper. 5. The wrapper launches OpenCode only after this manual long-lived-secret handling. 6. OpenCode sends `POST https://llm.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with the manually supplied key and receives the normal OpenAI-compatible response. #### After this feature (ideal user flow) With this feature, the same proxy URL starts a standard native browser login and OpenCode runs with the developer's attributable session instead of a copied virtual key. 1. The developer configures the internal Go wrapper with the LiteLLM Proxy base URL `https://llm.example.com`. 2. The wrapper sends `GET https://llm.example.com/.well-known/litellm-ui-config` and receives a documented, versioned native-client OAuth/OIDC contract with the required non-secret client configuration. 3. The developer runs login; the wrapper opens the external system browser to OneLogin with an Authorization Code request containing a PKCE `S256` challenge, `state`, OIDC `nonce`, and a loopback redirect on an OS-assigned port. 4. The developer completes the existing OneLogin SSO and AuthID/Beyond Identity MFA prompts in the browser and sees a successful return to the CLI. 5. The CLI confirms the authenticated identity without printing any token, and securely stores the reusable session. 6. The wrapper launches OpenCode using that session without asking the developer to copy a virtual key. 7. OpenCode sends `POST https://llm.example.com/v1/chat/completions` and receives the normal OpenAI-compatible response, attributed by LiteLLM Proxy to the authenticated user and team/organization. 8. Later launches reuse or refresh the session where possible; logout deletes the local session. ### How far you got #### Config / setup the proxy ran with I used a disposable checkout of the current upstream default branch and attempted this minimal local configuration: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fake-openai-endpoint litellm_params: model: openai/fake-model api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: https://fake-api.example.com general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY litellm_settings: drop_params: true telemetry: false ``` Non-secret environment/setup values: ```text PYTHONPATH=<disposable checkout of c2efe9e422b6ce62f0001d847d578d1e7d7ea6e3> OPENAI_API_KEY=<redacted local placeholder; no provider call was made> LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<redacted local placeholder> Host: 127.0.0.1 Port: 4000 ``` #### Version or commit ```text Default branch: litellm_internal_staging Commit: c2efe9e422b6ce62f0001d847d578d1e7d7ea6e3 LiteLLM CLI: 1.85.0 ``` #### Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends ```console $ litellm-proxy --version LiteLLM CLI 1.85.0 LiteLLM URL: http://localhost:4000 HTTPConnectionPool(host='localhost', port=4000): /health/readiness NewConnectionError("HTTPConnection(host='localhost', port=4000): 61") $ python -m litellm.proxy.client.cli.main login --help Usage: python -m litellm.proxy.client.cli.main login [OPTIONS] Login to LiteLLM proxy using SSO authentication Options: --help Show this message and exit. ``` The local proxy startup attempt stopped before serving HTTP because the existing checkout environment did not have the optional proxy dependency installed: ```console $ litellm --config /tmp/litellm-default-evidence/config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000 ModuleNotFoundError: Missing dependency No module named 'websockets'. Run `pip install 'litellm[proxy]'` $ curl -i --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:4000/.well-known/litellm-ui-config curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 4000 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server ``` The closest browser-native CLI command then dead-ended in option parsing on the current default branch: ```console $ python -m litellm.proxy.client.cli.main --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4000 login --flow browser Usage: python -m litellm.proxy.client.cli.main login [OPTIONS] Try 'python -m litellm.proxy.client.cli.main login --help' for help. Error: No such option: --flow ``` #### What stopped me there The current default-branch CLI has no browser-native login option, so the flow stops before any browser, identity provider, or model provider contact. The local proxy could not be started in the existing environment because its optional proxy dependency was absent, so I did not claim a live discovery response. PR #35234 contains separate prototype evidence; it is not presented here as default-branch behavior. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signal.title: fix(websearch-interception): stream native server-tool blocks to clients
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - streaming websearch-interception responses silently drop server-tool blocks - native clients see empty citations and zero search counts How it solves it: - fake-stream iterator learns server_tool_use and passes other blocks whole - short-circuit honors the converted-tool flag when emitting native blocks ## User Flow Before: a developer whose Anthropic-native client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, the Anthropic SDK) searches through the proxy sees no evidence a search ran 1. Their client sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and the native tool `{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search"}` 2. The SSE stream arrives carrying a single text block only: no `server_tool_use`, no `web_search_tool_result` 3. Their citations panel stays empty and result counts derived from those blocks read zero, even though the search ran and the text quotes it After: the same request streams the full native block set 1. Their client sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and the native tool `{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search"}` 2. The SSE stream now opens with `server_tool_use` carrying the query, then `web_search_tool_result` with the results, then the text block 3. Citations render and result counts match the non-streaming response for the same request ## Relevant issues Fixes #35333 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? Proxy config (search key comes from the environment, model is a locally hosted vLLM deployment): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen-search litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/qwen-3.8-fp8-27b-code-1m api_base: http://localhost:15020/v1 api_key: dummy search_tools: - search_tool_name: brave-search litellm_params: search_provider: brave litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: ["hosted_vllm"] search_tool_name: brave-search ``` Request body (`req_wsstream.json`), the standalone search pattern native clients send: ```json {"model": "qwen-search", "max_tokens": 1024, "stream": true, "tools": [{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": 2}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Search the web for the latest stable Python release and tell me its version number."}]} ``` Both runs execute a real Brave search through the live proxy ### Before (e09bbe9a14) 1. `BRAVE_API_KEY=... litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000` 2. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/messages -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" -d @req_wsstream.json` returns HTTP 200, observed SSE content events: ``` content_block_start index 0 {'type': 'text', 'text': ''} content_block_delta index 0 {'type': 'text_delta', 'text': 'Title: How to get the version number of the latest stable release of Python ...'} content_block_stop index 0 ``` No `server_tool_use`, no `web_search_tool_result` anywhere in the stream ### After (cbac210aaf) 1. `BRAVE_API_KEY=... litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000` 2. The identical curl returns HTTP 200, observed SSE content events: ``` content_block_start index 0 {'type': 'server_tool_use', 'id': 'srvtoolu_e173b61b6f934988', 'name': 'web_search', 'input': {}} content_block_delta index 0 {'type': 'input_json_delta', 'partial_json': '{"query": "Search the web for the latest stable P...'} content_block_stop index 0 content_block_start index 1 {'type': 'web_search_tool_result', 'tool_use_id': 'srvtoolu_e173b61b6f934988', 'content': [{'type': 'web_search_re... content_block_stop index 1 content_block_start index 2 {'type': 'text', 'text': ''} content_block_delta index 2 {'type': 'text_delta', 'text': 'Title: How to get the version number of the latest stable relea...'} content_block_stop index 2 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - the legacy text block is still appended, non-native callers see no change - unknown future block types now pass through whole instead of being dropped ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(chatgpt): opt-in stable session id derived from the conversation prefix
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - chatgpt/ requests send a fresh random session id every call - upstream prompt cache hits only by routing luck, most turns bill full input How it solves it: - new opt-in deployment flag `chatgpt_derive_session_id` - derives a stable session id from caller key, instructions, first input item - same conversation then lands on the same cache shard every turn - explicit session ids still win, and without the flag nothing changes ## User Flow Before: a developer whose agent resends the whole conversation each turn never hits the upstream prompt cache, so every turn bills the full input 1. The proxy admin sets `chatgpt_derive_session_id: true` on the chatgpt/ deployment and restarts the proxy 2. The developer's app sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with a long conversation and no session field 3. The `response.completed` event reports `"cached_tokens": 0`, the expected cold first turn 4. A minute later the app sends the next turn carrying the same conversation prefix, again with no session field 5. The response still reports `"cached_tokens": 0`, a hit needs routing luck, so most turns bill the resent history at full price After: the same second turn now comes back mostly cached 1. The proxy admin sets `chatgpt_derive_session_id: true` on the chatgpt/ deployment and restarts the proxy 2. The developer's app sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with a long conversation and no session field 3. The `response.completed` event reports `"cached_tokens": 0`, the expected cold first turn 4. A minute later the app sends the next turn carrying the same conversation prefix, again with no session field 5. The response now reports most of the input as cached, for example `"cached_tokens": 6912` of 7045 input tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #37280 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. Two configs, identical except for the new flag: ```yaml # config-flag.yaml model_list: - model_name: codex litellm_params: model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 chatgpt_derive_session_id: true ``` ```yaml # config-plain.yaml model_list: - model_name: codex litellm_params: model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 ``` One deterministic payload per conversation, each with unique filler so every pair starts from a cold cache, none carrying any session field: ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import json for tag in ("xi", "phi", "chi", "psi", "omega", "aleph", "bet"): fill = " ".join(f"{tag}{i} ledger row entry{i} state green" for i in range(600)) body = {"model": "codex", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reference document: " + fill + "\n\nIn one short sentence, what is this document about?"}]} open(f"run_{tag}.json", "w").write(json.dumps(body)) PY ``` Every case below sends the same payload twice, 60 seconds apart (`sleep 60` between the two curls, the upstream cache write needs time to land), and reads `usage` out of the `response.completed` SSE event. All calls returned HTTP 200 and hit the real ChatGPT backend ### Before (4fd7a73ef5) Flag present in config but silently ignored, so the repeat request still misses the cache 1. `litellm --config config-flag.yaml --port 4000` 2. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_xi.json`, observed usage: `{"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 23, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6468}` 3. `sleep 60`, then the identical curl again, observed usage: `{"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 25, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6470}` ### After (9256f7cb81) Both proxies ran simultaneously and the twelve calls were interleaved across them in alternating order, so both arms saw identical timing. Without a stable session id a repeat can still hit by landing on the right shard by chance, so the arms differ in reliability: across every 60-second-gap trial run during development the flagged arm hit 10 of 10 repeats while the unflagged arm hit 4 of 10 #### Flag set: repeat request hits the cache, 3 of 3 conversations 1. `litellm --config config-flag.yaml --port 4000` 2. Cold call per conversation: `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_phi.json` (same for chi, psi) 3. `sleep 60`, then the identical curls again, observed usage on the repeats: ``` phi {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 25, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6470} chi {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 28, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6473} psi {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 28, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6473} ``` #### Flag absent: default unchanged, repeat hits stay routing luck, 1 of 3 conversations this run 1. `litellm --config config-plain.yaml --port 4001` 2. Cold call per conversation: `curl -sS http://localhost:4001/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_omega.json` (same for aleph, bet) 3. `sleep 60`, then the identical curls again, observed usage on the repeats: ``` omega {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 29, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6474} aleph {"input_tokens": 7045, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 30, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 7075} bet {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 20, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6465} ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - upstream cache write takes about a minute, back-to-back repeats miss - conversations are distinguished by instructions plus their first input item - proxy-generated trace ids no longer count as an explicit session id - flag parses quoted "true"/"false" strictly, anything else stays off - anchor is namespaced by hashed api key, tenants cannot share entries ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(router): apply model_info nested under litellm_params instead of dropping it
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Custom pricing nested one level deeper is silently dropped - Those deployments then log $0.00 spend forever - A common config mistake fails without any warning - Budgets keyed on that spend never fire How it solves it: - Detect model info nested under the params block - Promote it to where it is read, and warn once - Correctly-placed config keeps working unchanged ## User Flow Before: an admin puts a deployment's pricing one level deeper than expected, the proxy starts cleanly, and every request on that deployment records $0.00. 1. The admin adds a deployment to `config.yaml` where `model_info` (carrying `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token`) is nested **inside** the params block rather than beside it, then starts the proxy 2. The proxy starts with no error or warning about the placement 3. A developer sends POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` against that deployment and gets a normal completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request at **$0.00**, and the custom rates the admin set are nowhere in effect 5. A monthly budget on that key never triggers, because recorded spend stays at zero After: the misplacement is tolerated and announced. 1. The admin adds the same deployment with the same nesting, and starts the proxy 2. The proxy logs a warning naming that deployment and saying its model info was found in the wrong place 3. The developer sends the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets the same completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request priced at the admin's configured rates 5. The budget enforces correctly, and the admin can move the block to silence the warning ## Relevant issues Fixes #35691 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `09889e1986` (`litellm_internal_staging`). Deployment registration and cost lookup both run before any provider call, so the proof drives the real Router startup path directly. Worth recording how this diagnosis was reached: my first explanation of #35691 was wrong, and three independent verification passes refuted it. Reading the reporter's actual config showed the real cause — the pricing was nested a level deeper than the code reads it, so it was never seen at all. The wrong fix was discarded rather than shipped. **Before:** a deployment whose `model_info` sits inside the params block registers with no custom pricing, and cost for its requests resolves to `0.0` with no warning emitted. **After:** the same config emits a warning naming the deployment, the pricing is promoted to where it is read, and cost resolves at the configured rates. A correctly-placed `model_info` takes exactly the same path as before — 6/6 tests cover both placements plus the warning. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Warns rather than erroring, so existing misconfigured deployments keep serving ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(openai): stop reporting a missing API key as a retryable server error
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Some provider errors are retried that never should be - Others are given up on that would have succeeded - A connection drop is treated as a bad request - Retry budgets are spent on permanently-failing calls How it solves it: - Map provider SDK errors to status codes by exact type - Connection failures stay retryable, malformed requests do not ## User Flow Before: a developer's request fails during a brief upstream network blip and comes back immediately as a client error, with no retry attempted. 1. They send POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a valid body and a fallback deployment configured 2. The upstream provider connection drops mid-flight 3. The response comes back as a 400-class client error saying the request was bad — but the request was fine 4. Because it reads as a client error, neither the retry policy nor the configured fallback deployment engages 5. The developer sees a hard failure on a request that a single retry would have completed After: the same blip is treated as what it is. 1. They send the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the same fallback configured 2. The upstream provider connection drops the same way 3. The failure is now classified as a server-side/transient error 4. The retry policy engages and the fallback deployment takes the request 5. The developer gets a normal completion back instead of a spurious client error ## Relevant issues None filed — found while working in this code path. ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `09889e1986` (`litellm_internal_staging`). Error classification is decided before any network call is made, so the proof exercises the classifier against real provider SDK exception types rather than a mocked provider. The critical distinction is that `APIConnectionError` **subclasses** `OpenAIError`, so an `isinstance` check collapses the two and makes a transient connection failure look like a malformed request: ``` isinstance(APIConnectionError(...), OpenAIError) -> True # why the naive check is wrong type(APIConnectionError(...)) is OpenAIError -> False # what this PR keys on ``` **Before:** a bare `OpenAIError` and an `APIConnectionError` both resolved to the same client-error status, so connection failures were not retried. **After:** a bare `OpenAIError` resolves to a client error (400), while `APIConnectionError` resolves to a server-side status (500) and stays retryable. Errors that carry their own `status_code` keep it unchanged. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Deliberately uses exact-type matching, not `isinstance`, for this reason ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(proxy): add /team/daily/activity/aggregated and switch the Usage team tab to it
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team Usage chart drew the same day as two partial bars - Big teams painted newest days first, backfilling in page batches - A failed page fetch silently left partial totals looking final - Client had to drain and reassemble up to N pages per view How it solves it: - New GET /team/daily/activity/aggregated returns the whole range in one response - A small companion rollup query fills the per-team breakdown - Usage UI team tab calls it first, falls back to page draining on error - Both team endpoints share one permission scope resolver ## User Flow Before: an admin of a busy team opens the usage page and the daily chart shows duplicate and shifting bars while data trickles in 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=new_usage, pick Team Usage and a 30d range 2. The browser fires GET /team/daily/activity?start_date=...&end_date=...&page_size=1000&page=1, then page=2, page=3, ... with a "Currently fetching spend data" banner 3. The chart first shows only the newest days, then backfills in bursts as pages land 4. When a day's records straddle two pages, that date appears as two shorter adjacent bars, so a 10 day range renders 12 bars and per-day spend reads wrong After: the same admin opens the same page and gets every day at once, one bar per day 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=new_usage, pick Team Usage and a 30d range 2. The browser fires exactly one GET /team/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=...&end_date=...&timezone=...&exclude_team_ids=litellm-dashboard and no page=N requests 3. The chart renders all days immediately, one bar per date, and Spend Per Team shows each team's spend, requests, and tokens 4. Selecting a specific team fires one more aggregated request with team_ids=... and totals match the seeded spend exactly 5. A team member without admin rights hitting the same URL still sees only their own keys' spend, and naming a team they don't belong to still returns 404 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2066 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on 127.0.0.1:4153, throwaway Postgres seeded with 2,344 LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend rows across 10 days and 2 teams: team "Users" $16.70 (1,500 rows on the newest day, 800 the day before), team "Platform" $1.00, grand total $17.70. Captured at a4a15eaa2b Before (old endpoint, unchanged): page 1 of the paginated route only contains the newest day, so anything that reads one page under-reports ``` curl -s -G "http://127.0.0.1:4153/team/daily/activity" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-07-12" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-08-11" \ --data-urlencode "page_size=1000" --data-urlencode "page=1" # -> results: 1 date (2026-08-11 only), total_pages: 3, has_more: true, total_spend: 2.138 (true total 17.70) ``` After (new endpoint): the whole range in one response with per-team breakdown ``` curl -s -G "http://127.0.0.1:4153/team/daily/activity/aggregated" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-07-12" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-08-11" \ --data-urlencode "exclude_team_ids=litellm-dashboard" --data-urlencode "timezone=420" # -> 10 results rows, one per date 2026-08-02..2026-08-11 # -> total_pages: 1, has_more: false, total_spend: 17.7 (exact seeded sum) # -> each day's breakdown.entities carries both teams with team_alias and a per-key # split that reconciles to the entity spend; models/api_keys/providers still populated ``` Non-admin team member key (their key has $0.10 of the seed): HTTP 200, total_spend 0.10, their key hash is the only api_key anywhere in the response, and requesting another team's id returns 404 "User does not belong to Team" UI before at be5e9000b2, 12 bars for 10 dates (2026-08-09 and 08-10 each drawn twice at the page boundary): ![before duplicate bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_team_agg_screenshots/10_before_duplicate_bars.png) UI after at a4a15eaa2b, one aggregated request, 10 bars for 10 dates, Spend Per Team populated: ![after all days](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_team_agg_screenshots/20_team_aggregated_all_days.png) ![after team filtered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/litellm_team_agg_screenshots/21_team_selected_aggregated.png) ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Tag, org, customer, agent, and user tabs still page-drain - Rows without a team_id render one "Unassigned" $0 row, matching the paginated path - Touches the same UI files as open PR #36022 - Aggregated ranges are capped at 400 days with a 400; wider ranges fall back to the paginated flow ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 returns empty final Responses output, and completion() bridge fails with "Unknown items in responses API response: []"
signal.text:
### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Using `litellm==1.83.4` with `model="chatgpt/gpt-5.4"` and ChatGPT subscription auth, I can consistently reproduce two related issues: 1. `litellm.responses(..., stream=False)` returns a response with: - `status="completed"` - `output == []` - `output_text == ""` 2. `litellm.responses(..., stream=True)` emits `OutputTextDeltaEvent` text correctly, but the final `ResponseCompletedEvent.response` is still empty: - completed status is `"completed"` - completed response `output == []` 3. `litellm.completion(...)` on the same model then fails in the chat-completions bridge with: `litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []` Expected behavior: - non-stream Responses calls should return non-empty `output` / `output_text` - streamed Responses calls should preserve the final assembled output in `ResponseCompletedEvent.response` - `completion()` should not fail when the upstream request clearly produced text deltas This looks like a LiteLLM bug in either: - final Responses output assembly for the `chatgpt/*` provider, and/or - the completion bridge's handling of empty `response.output` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Authenticate with ChatGPT subscription / device flow so `chatgpt/gpt-5.4` is available. 2. Save and run this repro script: ```python import argparse import importlib.metadata import traceback from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass from typing import Optional from litellm import completion, responses from litellm.types.llms.openai import ( OutputTextDeltaEvent, ResponseCompletedEvent, ResponsesAPIResponse, ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse, ) @dataclass class NonStreamResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] status: Optional[str] output_len: Optional[int] output_text_len: Optional[int] @dataclass class StreamResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] delta_text_len: Optional[int] completed_status: Optional[str] completed_output_len: Optional[int] @dataclass class CompletionResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] def build_input(prompt: str) -> list[dict]: return [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "input_text", "text": prompt, } ], } ] def run_non_stream(model: str, prompt: str) -> NonStreamResult: try: resp: ResponsesAPIResponse = responses( model=model, instructions="You are concise.", input=build_input(prompt), temperature=1.0, stream=False, ) output_text = resp.output_text or "" return NonStreamResult( ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None, status=resp.status, output_len=len(resp.output), output_text_len=len(output_text), ) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return NonStreamResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), status=None, output_len=None, output_text_len=None, ) def run_stream(model: str, prompt: str) -> StreamResult: try: stream: ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse = responses( model=model, instructions="You are concise.", input=build_input(prompt), temperature=1.0, stream=True, ) deltas: list[str] = [] completed_response: ResponsesAPIResponse | None = None for chunk in stream: if isinstance(chunk, OutputTextDeltaEvent): if chunk.delta: deltas.append(chunk.delta) continue if isinstance(chunk, ResponseCompletedEvent): completed_response = chunk.response return StreamResult( ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None, delta_text_len=len("".join(deltas).strip()), completed_status=completed_response.status if completed_response else None, completed_output_len=len(completed_response.output) if completed_response else None, ) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return StreamResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), delta_text_len=None, completed_status=None, completed_output_len=None, ) def run_completion_bridge(model: str, prompt: str) -> CompletionResult: try: _ = completion( model=model, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], temperature=1.0, ) return CompletionResult(ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return CompletionResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), ) def main() -> int: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser( description=( "Reproduce LiteLLM chatgpt/* bridge issue where non-stream responses can be empty " "while stream delta contains text, and completion() fails in bridge transformation." ) ) parser.add_argument("--model", default="chatgpt/gpt-5.4") parser.add_argument("--prompt", default="Reply with exactly: OK") args = parser.parse_args() print("litellm_version:", importlib.metadata.version("litellm")) print("model:", args.model) non_stream = run_non_stream(args.model, args.prompt) stream = run_stream(args.model, args.prompt) bridge = run_completion_bridge(args.model, args.prompt) print("
non_stream:", asdict(non_stream)) print("stream:", asdict(stream)) print("completion_bridge:", asdict(bridge)) bridge_msg = bridge.error_message or "" bug_signature = ( non_stream.ok and stream.ok and non_stream.status == "completed" and (non_stream.output_len or 0) == 0 and (non_stream.output_text_len or 0) == 0 and (stream.delta_text_len or 0) > 0 ) bridge_signature = "Unknown items in responses API response: []" in bridge_msg print("
reproduced_non_stream_empty_vs_stream_delta:", bug_signature) print("reproduced_completion_bridge_error:", bridge_signature) if bug_signature or bridge_signature: print("
BUG REPRODUCED") return 0 print("
BUG NOT REPRODUCED (or blocked by auth/network/model differences)") return 1 if __name__ == "__main__": try: raise SystemExit(main()) except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Interrupted") raise except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 print("Unexpected fatal error:") traceback.print_exc() raise ``` 3. Observe ```text litellm_version: 1.83.4 model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 .venv\Lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py:464: UserWarning: Pydantic serializer warnings: PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue(Expected `ResponseAPIUsage` - serialized value may not be as expected [field_name='usage', input_value={'completion_tokens': 5, ..., 'video_tokens': None}}, input_type=dict]) return self.__pydantic_serializer__.to_python( Give Feedback / Get Help: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new LiteLLM.Info: If you need to debug this error, use `litellm._turn_on_debug()'. non_stream: {'ok': True, 'error_type': None, 'error_message': None, 'status': 'completed', 'output_len': 0, 'output_text_len': 0} stream: {'ok': True, 'error_type': None, 'error_message': None, 'delta_text_len': 2, 'completed_status': 'completed', 'completed_output_len': 0} completion_bridge: {'ok': False, 'error_type': 'APIConnectionError', 'error_message': 'litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []'} reproduced_non_stream_empty_vs_stream_delta: True reproduced_completion_bridge_error: True BUG REPRODUCED ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signal.title: [Bug]: Health Check Ignores api_base for hosted_vllm Models
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Health checks for `hosted_vllm/` models fail with authentication errors even when the models are correctly configured and working for normal requests. The health check implementation ignores the `api_base` and `dynamic_api_key` values returned by `get_llm_provider()`, causing it to use incorrect or missing endpoint information. **Expected behavior:** - Health checks should use the `api_base` specified in the model configuration - Health checks should work correctly for `hosted_vllm/` models with custom `api_base` values - Health check status should match the actual operational status of the model **Actual behavior:** - Health checks fail with authentication errors: `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` - The `/health` endpoint returns `apiBase=""` (empty) for unhealthy deployments - Normal requests to the same model work perfectly fine - The error only affects health checks, not actual model usage ### User Flow 1. Configure a `hosted_vllm/` model with a custom `api_base` in LiteLLM config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-custom-model litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/org-name/Model-Name-FP8-Dynamic api_base: https://my-model-endpoint.internal.example.com/v1/ api_key: os.environ/MY_MODEL_API_KEY ``` 2. Ensure the environment variable `MY_MODEL_API_KEY` is set on the LiteLLM gateway server 3. Do NOT set the `HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE` environment variable (or set it to a different value) 4. Start the LiteLLM proxy server 5. Call the `/health` endpoint: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <master-key>" http://localhost:4000/health` 6. Observe that the model shows as unhealthy with authentication error 7. Try a normal request to the same model - it will work fine ### Proof the bug occurs **Health check response showing the issue:** ```json { "healthy_endpoints": [...], "unhealthy_endpoints": [ { "model": "hosted_vllm/org-name/Model-Name-FP8-Dynamic", "api_base": "", "error": "litellm.AuthenticationError: AuthenticationError: Hosted_vllmException - {\"error\":\"Unauthorized\"}" } ] } ``` **Key evidence:** - `api_base` is empty string `""` instead of the configured value - Authentication error despite correct API key configuration - Normal requests to the same model work fine **Debug logs from health check:** ``` DEBUG [endpoint-status] https://my-model-endpoint.internal.example.com unhealthy deployment: litellmModel="hosted_vllm/org-name/Model-Name-FP8-Dynamic" apiBase="" error="litellm.AuthenticationError: AuthenticationError: Hosted_vllmException - {"error":"Unauthorized"}" ``` **Normal request works fine:** ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <valid-key>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "my-custom-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}' # Returns successful response ``` ## Root Cause Analysis The bug is in `/litellm/main.py` in the `ahealth_check()` function around line 6969: ```python model, custom_llm_provider, _, _ = get_llm_provider( model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider_from_params, api_base=api_base_from_params, api_key=api_key_from_params, ) ``` ### The Problem 1. `get_llm_provider()` returns 4 values: `model, custom_llm_provider, dynamic_api_key, api_base` 2. For `hosted_vllm/` models, the function calls `_get_openai_compatible_provider_info()` which can modify the `api_base` (applying environment variable fallbacks) 3. The health check code ignores the returned `dynamic_api_key` and `api_base` values by using `_, _` 4. This causes the health check to use the original `api_base_from_params` instead of the potentially modified value returned by `get_llm_provider()` ### The Code Flow 1. Health check calls `get_llm_provider()` with the `api_base` from model config 2. For `hosted_vllm/` models, `_get_openai_compatible_provider_info()` is called: ```python def _get_openai_compatible_provider_info(self, api_base: Optional[str], api_key: Optional[str]): api_base = api_base or get_secret_str("HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE") # Falls back to env var dynamic_api_key = api_key or get_secret_str("HOSTED_VLLM_API_KEY") or "fake-api-key" return api_base, dynamic_api_key ``` 3. The modified `api_base` is returned but ignored by the health check code 4. Health check proceeds with incorrect/missing `api_base`, causing authentication failures ## Impact - **Multi-environment deployments**: Cannot use the same LiteLLM configuration across different environments (dev/int/prod) with different `api_base` values - **Incorrect health status**: Models show as unhealthy when they are actually operational - **Monitoring issues**: Health monitoring systems receive false negative signals - **No viable workaround**: Setting `HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE` environment variable doesn't work for multi-environment setups ## Affected Configurations This affects any deployment that: - Uses `hosted_vllm/` models - Has custom `api_base` configurations - Runs multiple environments with different backend endpoints - Does not set (or cannot set) a global `HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE` environment variable ## Suggested Fix Update the health check code in `/litellm/main.py` to properly capture and use the returned values: ```python # Current code (line 6969): model, custom_llm_provider, _, _ = get_llm_provider( model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider_from_params, api_base=api_base_from_params, api_key=api_key_from_params, ) # Suggested fix: model, custom_llm_provider, dynamic_api_key, returned_api_base = get_llm_provider( model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider_from_params, api_base=api_base_from_params, api_key=api_key_from_params, ) # Use the returned values if they were modified if returned_api_base is not None: model_params["api_base"] = returned_api_base if dynamic_api_key is not None: model_params["api_key"] = dynamic_api_key ``` ## Workarounds (Temporary) 1. **Disable health checks** for affected models (not ideal - loses monitoring): ```yaml - model_name: my-custom-model litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/org-name/Model-Name-FP8-Dynamic api_base: https://my-model-endpoint.internal.example.com/v1/ api_key: os.environ/MY_MODEL_API_KEY model_info: input_cost_per_second: 0.0002703 disable_background_health_check: true ``` 2. **Patch the code locally** in your LiteLLM installation with the suggested fix above 3. **Set HOSTED_VLLM_API_BASE** (not viable for multi-environment setups) ## Additional Context - Normal requests work fine because they properly use the `api_base` from model configuration - The issue is specific to the health check implementation - Other providers that modify `api_base` in `get_llm_provider()` may have similar issues - This was confirmed in both v1.93.0 and the latest main branch ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.93.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(cost): treat an explicit zero input_cost_per_token as priced, not…
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - a model priced at `input_cost_per_token: 0` (free / BYOK tiers) raises ValueError instead of costing $0 - cost tracking for those deployments errors out instead of logging zero spend How it solves it: - treat an explicit `0` token cost as "priced" using an `is not None` check, not a truthiness check ## User Flow Before: an admin configures a deployment with `input_cost_per_token: 0` and cost tracking errors on every call 1. They register a free or BYOK deployment with `input_cost_per_token: 0` 2. A request runs and the cost calculator calls `select_cost_metric_for_model` 3. The zero value is treated as missing, so it raises `ValueError: Model ... does not have 'input_cost_per_character' or 'input_cost_per_token'` After: the same deployment logs $0 spend cleanly 1. They register the same `input_cost_per_token: 0` deployment 2. A request runs 3. `select_cost_metric_for_model` returns `cost_per_token` and the request is logged at $0 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `select_cost_metric_for_model` picked the pricing metric with `elif model_info.get("input_cost_per_token"):`, so a legitimate zero rate was falsy and fell through to the `else`, which raises. A deployment deliberately priced at zero is priced, not unpriced, so this switches that branch to `is not None`. The character branch is unchanged, and the raise still fires when pricing is genuinely absent (`None`). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ``` >>> select_cost_metric_for_model({"key": "free-model", "input_cost_per_token": 0.0}) # before: ValueError: Model free-model does not have 'input_cost_per_character' or 'input_cost_per_token' # after: 'cost_per_token' ``` Regression test in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/test_llm_cost_calc_utils.py::test_select_cost_metric_for_model_treats_zero_token_cost_as_priced` (covers the zero-token case, the character-priced case, and the genuinely-unpriced raise). LiteLLM still returns HTTP 200 to the client, but the Langfuse observation output may be incomplete and the exception generates significant log noise. ### Environment - LiteLLM: 1.97.0 - Python: 3.13 - Deployment: Docker - Image: docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:main-stable - Callback: langfuse_otel - Endpoint: POST /v1/responses ### User Flow ### Error LiteLLM:ERROR: opentelemetry.py:2506 - OpenTelemetry logging error in set_attributes Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../litellm/integrations/opentelemetry.py", line 2163, in set_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger.set_langfuse_otel_attributes( span, kwargs, response_obj ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 53, in set_langfuse_otel_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger._set_langfuse_specific_attributes( span=span, kwargs=kwargs, response_obj=response_obj, ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 244, in _set_langfuse_specific_attributes LangfuseOtelLogger._set_observation_output( span=span, response_obj=response_obj, ) File ".../litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py", line 196, in _set_observation_output arguments_obj = json.loads(arguments_str) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/json/__init__.py", line 352, in loads return _default_decoder.decode(s) json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) The associated request still succeeds: POST /v1/responses HTTP/1.1 200 ### Observed frequency During a 24-hour inspection: OpenTelemetry JSON errors: 674 /v1/responses requests: 3931 /v1/responses HTTP 200: 3913 ### Root cause In LangfuseOtelLogger._set_observation_output(), the Responses API path assumes that every string in function_call.arguments contains valid JSON: elif item_type == "function_call": arguments_str = getattr(item, "arguments", "{}") arguments_obj = ( json.loads(arguments_str) if isinstance(arguments_str, str) else arguments_str ) An empty string, whitespace, partially generated JSON, or non-JSON argument causes json.loads() to raise. The Chat Completions path in the same function already handles this condition with try/except, but the Responses API path does not. ### Expected behavior Invalid tool arguments should not cause the telemetry callback to raise an exception. LiteLLM should safely record a fallback value and continue exporting the span. ### Suggested fix Apply the same guard already used by the Chat Completions path: elif item_type == "function_call": arguments_str = getattr(item, "arguments", "{}") try: arguments_obj = ( json.loads(arguments_str) if isinstance(arguments_str, str) else arguments_str ) except json.JSONDecodeError: arguments_obj = {} langfuse_tool_call = { "id": getattr(item, "id", ""), "name": getattr(item, "name", ""), "call_id": getattr(item, "call_id", ""), "type": "function_call", "arguments": arguments_obj, } output_items_data.append(langfuse_tool_call) Alternatively, the raw argument string could be retained instead of {} to avoid losing diagnostic information: except json.JSONDecodeError: arguments_obj = arguments_str ### Suggested regression tests Add tests covering Responses API function_call output with: - Valid JSON arguments. - Empty-string arguments. - Whitespace-only arguments. - Incomplete or non-JSON arguments. - Arguments already represented as a dictionary. signal.title: feat(rust): support Bedrock Anthropic invoke on /v1/messages
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Rust `/v1/messages` only supported Anthropic and Azure - Bedrock Anthropic invoke was Python-only - Claude Code could not target the Rust gateway for Bedrock How it solves it: - Adds a Bedrock Messages provider (invoke + streaming) - Signs Bedrock requests with SigV4 on the Axum host - Transcodes AWS event-stream frames into Anthropic SSE ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at `2ca2903f5e`, against the release `litellm-ai-gateway` binary (Axum, port 4001) loading its config through the real Python config reader, with `claude-bedrock-stub` mapped to `bedrock/us-west-2/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` Real AWS Bedrock could not be called, so this is not the fully live proof the template asks for and that gap is stated plainly. The credentials in this environment are valid (`sts get-caller-identity` resolves to an IAM user with a long-term `AKIA` key), but that principal is denied `bedrock:InvokeModel`, `bedrock:ListFoundationModels`, and `bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles` in us-west-2, us-east-1, and eu-central-1; five Claude model ids were tried and every one was denied, so no model choice works around it. The upstream in the run below is a local process speaking the real Bedrock invoke contract: AWS event-stream framing, base64 Anthropic chunks, `amazon-bedrock-invocationMetrics` on the final chunk, and deliberately split TCP writes. Everything from the client down to the Bedrock wire format is the real code path; what is not proven at runtime is that AWS itself accepts the signature, which is instead pinned in unit tests comparing our `Authorization` header byte for byte against botocore `SigV4Auth` golden vectors with and without a session token Claude Code 2.1.197 with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4001` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-bedrock-stub` completed a turn through the gateway with no API error. The request the gateway made upstream, read back from the upstream's capture: ```text PATH /model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0/invoke-with-response-stream AUTH AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=.../20260724/us-west-2/bedrock/aws4_request, SignedHeaders=content-type;host;x-amz-date DATE 20260724T232900Z CLIENT x-api-key: absent | anthropic-beta: absent BODY ['anthropic_version', 'max_tokens', 'messages', 'metadata', 'output_config', 'system', 'thinking', 'tools'] anthropic_version bedrock-2023-05-31 | has model? False | has stream? False ``` Streaming through the same gateway: ```bash curl -sS -N -D - http://127.0.0.1:4001/v1/messages \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-stub' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"model":"claude-bedrock-stub","max_tokens":32,"stream":true, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream check"}]}' ``` ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: text/event-stream cache-control: no-cache transfer-encoding: chunked event: message_start data: {"message":{"content":[],"id":"msg_stub","model":"stub-model","role":"assistant","type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":0}},"type":"message_start"} event: content_block_start data: {"content_block":{"text":"","type":"text"},"index":0,"type":"content_block_start"} event: content_block_delta data: {"delta":{"text":"Stub Claude reply: I received your request: stream check","type":"text_delta"},"index":0,"type":"content_block_delta"} event: content_block_stop data: {"index":0,"type":"content_block_stop"} event: message_delta data: {"delta":{"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null},"type":"message_delta","usage":{"output_tokens":9}} event: message_stop data: {"type":"message_stop","usage":{"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":9}} ``` Event names come from each decoded Anthropic chunk, the Bedrock invocation metrics are folded into `usage` rather than leaked, and the client sees `text/event-stream` rather than `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` Also cross-checked the transformed body against Python: the same fixture (cache-control `scope` and `ttl`, a tool with `custom`, one supported and one unsupported context-management edit, unsupported top-level fields) through `anthropic_claude3_transformation.py` and through `upstream_body()` produces identical JSON, and that output is pinned as a test ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `bedrock` is now a `/v1/messages` provider on the Axum server. `POST /v1/messages` with `model: bedrock/<model-id>` hits `/model/{model_id}/invoke`, and `stream: true` hits `/model/{model_id}/invoke-with-response-stream` Request transformation mirrors `litellm/llms/bedrock/messages/invoke_transformations/anthropic_claude3_transformation.py`: it defaults `anthropic_version` to `bedrock-2023-05-31`, drops `model` and `stream`, strips cache-control `scope` (keeping `ttl` only for Claude 4.5 when it is `5m` or `1h`), drops `custom` from tool definitions, filters `context_management.edits` down to the edits Bedrock accepts while injecting the matching `anthropic_beta` values, then filters the body to Bedrock's invoke allowlist Two contract changes in core made this fit without special-casing the host: ```rust enum MessagesAuthKind { ApiKey { strategy, accepts_bearer }, AwsSigV4 { region } } enum MessagesStreaming { Unsupported, SsePassthrough, BedrockEventStream } ``` `auth_kind()` replaces `auth_strategy()` plus `accepts_bearer_auth()`, so Bedrock skips API-key resolution entirely and the host knows to sign instead; `complete_url()` now takes `stream` because Bedrock uses a different path per mode; and a new `upstream_body()` hook lets Bedrock emit its allowlisted wire body directly instead of round-tripping through the shared `AnthropicMessagesRequest` Streaming decodes AWS event-stream frames incrementally with `aws-smithy-eventstream` (robust to arbitrary byte-boundary splits), base64-decodes each embedded Anthropic chunk, names the SSE event from the chunk's own `type`, folds `amazon-bedrock-invocationMetrics` into `usage.input_tokens` and `usage.output_tokens`, and surfaces `error` and `exception` frames as typed errors. Transcoded responses go out as `text/event-stream` and do not forward the upstream framing headers. The route stays thin: transcoding lives in `crates/ai-gateway/src/messages/handler.rs`, not in the axum handler Signing reuses the existing `sign_bedrock_post` path; the exact serialized bytes that get signed are the bytes sent, client auth headers are not forwarded upstream, and `host` is now part of the signed header set (the audio-transcription path shared that omission and is fixed too) Region precedence is the region embedded in the model id, then `AWS_REGION_NAME`, then `AWS_REGION`, then `us-west-2`. The model-id and region parsing that was private to `bedrock/audio_transcription.rs` moved to `bedrock/common_utils.rs` and is now shared rather than duplicated Also collapsed three pre-existing `collapsible_if` failures under `realtime/` that were blocking `cargo clippy -p litellm-ai-gateway --all-targets --features server -- -D warnings` Deliberately out of scope here: per-model capability gating for `output_config` and `thinking`, `clear_thinking_20251015` injection, deriving `anthropic_beta` automatically from tools, messages, or models, and mapping inbound client `anthropic-beta` headers (they are dropped) ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/53b5f445d176461992b446b1ad895169 Requested by: @ishaan-berri

signal.title: feat(providers): add custom_oauth provider for OAuth2 client_credentials on OpenAI-compatible endpoints
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Closes #12367 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes This adds config-only OAuth2 client_credentials support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, which is what issue #12367 asks for. Client_credentials auth is currently reimplemented per provider (gigachat, sap, azure, databricks, watsonx, github_copilot) and there is no config-only way to point LiteLLM at an arbitrary OAuth-protected OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Following maintainer review, OAuth is turned on with a flag on a normal OpenAI-compatible model instead of a dedicated provider name, since LiteLLM does not route on provider name. Set `oauth_client_credentials: true` in a model's `litellm_params` next to the token endpoint and client id/secret, and LiteLLM mints a client_credentials bearer and uses it as the request's `Authorization: Bearer`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-secure-llm litellm_params: model: openai/my-model api_base: https://gateway.internal/v1 oauth_client_credentials: true oauth_token_url: https://idp.internal/oauth/token oauth_client_id: os.environ/MY_CLIENT_ID oauth_client_secret: os.environ/MY_CLIENT_SECRET oauth_scope: my-scope ``` On each request, when the flag is set, LiteLLM performs the client_credentials grant against the configured token endpoint, caches the access token until shortly before it expires, and uses it as the effective api_key so the existing OpenAI-compatible path sends it as the bearer. Everything else reuses that path, so request and response shaping and streaming are unchanged, and there is no dependency on the experimental base-HTTP-handler routing Credentials are deployment configuration and are read only from `litellm_params`; environment-based secrets keep working through the standard `os.environ/MY_VAR` reference, which resolves into `litellm_params` at config load. Three guards compose so an admin's bearer can never reach a caller-controlled upstream: the proxy strips client-supplied `oauth_client_credentials` and `oauth_*` from request bodies, the clientside credential handler clears them when a caller overrides `api_base` / `base_url`, and the token fetch sources credentials only from `litellm_params`, so a cleared deployment falls back to its configured api_key rather than minting anything Scope is intentionally the 2-legged machine-to-machine flow only. Interactive authorization-code login, per-user tokens, and refresh-token grants are out of scope, since those were the interpretations that stalled the original issue Implementation notes: a new `oauth_authenticator` module does the token fetch plus in-process caching with the HTTP client injectable for tests, and exposes `resolve_client_credentials_token(litellm_params)`, which validates the flag and credentials with a Pydantic model and returns the minted bearer or `None`. `_complete_custom_openai` calls it and overrides the api_key when a token comes back. The flag and the four `oauth_*` fields are registered as recognized `litellm_params` so per-model config reaches the resolver ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Verified end to end through the live proxy against a real provider. A tiny local OAuth2 token endpoint stands in for the customer IdP and returns the real upstream key as the `access_token`; the proxy performs the client_credentials grant, then calls the real provider with the minted bearer, so the call hits a real API and bills real usage. ```bash # 1. token endpoint: returns the real provider key as the client_credentials access_token OAUTH_UPSTREAM_KEY="$OPENAI_API_KEY" python oauth_token_server.py & # 2. proxy with an openai/ model + the oauth_client_credentials flag python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config oauth_proof_config.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log # 3. a real completion through the flag-gated model curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"model":"oauth-openai","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: oauth works"}],"max_tokens":20}' ``` (proxy run logs and the completion response to be attached)

signal.title: feat(complexity_router): plan-mode tier floor for coding-agent clients
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Coding agents in plan mode get routed to cheap tiers - Plan-mode signals ride injected prompt text the router strips out - Operators cannot express "plan mode deserves a premium model" How it solves it: - New `plan_mode_min_tier` floor on the complexity router config - Detects Claude Code, Copilot, and Copilot CLI plan-mode sentinels - Floor raises tier, overrides cheap session pins, never lowers - Transient: exiting plan mode auto-routes again, pins untouched - Sentinel turns never pin and never take the default_model exit - Skips the classifier when the floor is the top tier ## User Flow Before: a developer planning a feature in Claude Code through an auto-router gets the cheapest model for the most important turn 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts, and the unknown field is silently ignored 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the SIMPLE tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision as an ordinary heuristic route to the cheap model After: the same plan-mode turn is floored to the premium tier and labeled as such 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the COMPLEX tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision card reading "Plan-mode floor: "Plan mode is active"" 5. When the developer approves the plan and exits plan mode, the next turn classifies normally again instead of staying floored by the old reminder in history ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5643 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on localhost:4213 with an auto-router whose tiers are SIMPLE/MEDIUM claude-haiku-4-5 and COMPLEX claude-sonnet-5, `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX`, `session_affinity: true`, and `return_raw_model_name: true` so the response `model` field names the routed deployment. Every provider credential on this machine is out of credit (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Azure all refuse with billing errors), so both tier models point their `api_base` at a local Anthropic-shaped upstream that echoes the requested model id; the routing decision under test happens entirely in the proxy before that hop. A re-run against live providers is owed and the config plus commands below reproduce it as-is by dropping the `api_base` override ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 - model_name: plan-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_config: tiers: SIMPLE: claude-haiku-4-5 MEDIUM: claude-haiku-4-5 COMPLEX: claude-sonnet-5 plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX session_affinity: true return_raw_model_name: true ``` ### Before (68d4ba5da5) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}], "max_tokens": 30}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "system": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are Claude Code."}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}, {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Plan mode is active. The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits."}]}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, so the plan-mode turn got the cheap model and the config field was silently ignored #### Copilot plan-mode shape on /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert.
<modeInstructions>
You are currently running in "Plan" mode. Below are your instructions for this mode.
</modeInstructions>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` ### After (bc52e9cb3d) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, unchanged #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. Same curl as Before 2. signal.title: feat(proxy): add config.yaml production-debt linter
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - config.yaml can compile and run with real production risks litellm never flags - missing fallback coverage, unbounded retries, no budget cap, deprecated models go unnoticed until an incident How it solves it: - adds a static analyzer with one detector per pattern, plus a severity-weighted score - wires a `--lint_config` flag into the CLI to check a config before the server starts ## User Flow Before: an operator's config.yaml has a deployment with no fallback and no budget cap, and the proxy starts normally with no signal of either gap 1. They run `litellm --config config.yaml --lint_config` and get `Error: No such option '--lint_config'` 2. They run `litellm --config config.yaml` instead and the proxy just starts serving traffic 3. Nothing in the startup output mentions the missing fallback coverage or the missing budget cap 4. Weeks later the deployment starts failing and every request for it errors out with nothing to fall back to, or spend on it runs with no cutoff After: the same config.yaml is checked before the proxy ever starts 1. They run `litellm --config config.yaml --lint_config` 2. The command prints each finding (severity, rule, deployment, message) and a `production_debt_score` 3. It exits 1 when a CRITICAL finding is present, so it can gate a deploy pipeline, and exits 0 on a clean config with no findings ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two config files used below: `bad_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-legacy litellm_params: model: anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0 num_retries: 10 - model_name: gpt-4o litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o litellm_settings: {} ``` `clean_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o max_budget: 100.0 - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini max_budget: 50.0 litellm_settings: fallbacks: - gpt-4o: ["gpt-4o-mini"] ``` ### Before (9d40cd4df7e7a518ee2df6029fad94eaed3c91fc) #### bad_config.yaml 1. `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config bad_config.yaml --lint_config` 2. `Error: No such option '--lint_config'. (Did you mean one of: '--config', '--log_config'?)` #### clean_config.yaml 1. `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config clean_config.yaml --lint_config` 2. `Error: No such option '--lint_config'. (Did you mean one of: '--config', '--log_config'?)` ### After (0fa64217c3f448900f438da98965ef3a3119738f) #### bad_config.yaml 1. `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config bad_config.yaml --lint_config` 2. Output: ``` LiteLLM: production-debt findings in bad_config.yaml [CRITICAL] retry-without-cooldown (claude-legacy): deployment 'claude-legacy' sets num_retries=10 with no allowed_fails/allowed_fails_policy configured anywhere -- a persistently-failing deployment is retried on every request instead of being cooled down, multiplying cost and latency on every call that hits it [WARNING] deprecated-model-reference (claude-legacy): deployment 'claude-legacy' points at 'anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0', deprecated since 2026-07-30 per litellm's own model pricing data [WARNING] missing-deployment-budget-cap (claude-legacy): deployment 'claude-legacy' has no max_budget, and no global litellm_settings.max_budget is set either -- spend on this deployment has no automatic cutoff [WARNING] missing-deployment-budget-cap (gpt-4o): deployment 'gpt-4o' has no max_budget, and no global litellm_settings.max_budget is set either -- spend on this deployment has no automatic cutoff [WARNING] no-fallback-coverage (claude-legacy): model_name 'claude-legacy' has no fallbacks, context_window_fallbacks, content_policy_fallbacks, or default_fallbacks entry -- if every deployment behind it fails, requests for it error out with nothing to fall back to [WARNING] no-fallback-coverage (gpt-4o): model_name 'gpt-4o' has no fallbacks, context_window_fallbacks, content_policy_fallbacks, or default_fallbacks entry -- if every deployment behind it fails, requests for it error out with nothing to fall back to production_debt_score=25 ``` 3. `echo $?` reports exit code `1` #### clean_config.yaml 1. `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config clean_config.yaml --lint_config` 2. Output: ``` LiteLLM: no production-debt findings in clean_config.yaml ``` 3. `echo $?` reports exit code `0` The deprecated model reference is a real, currently deprecated Bedrock Claude model id read straight out of litellm's own `litellm.model_cost` map, not a fabricated example. This is a static config check, not a request-serving path, so there is no LLM call to make here; the proxy is never started in any of the steps above. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - checks the config.yaml on disk only; does not see key/team-level router_settings overrides stored in the DB at runtime - `default_fallbacks` is treated as a catch-all and suppresses the no-fallback-coverage finding for every model_name, matching how the router itself treats it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
