signal.title: fix(guardrails): merge model-level guardrails into litellm_metadata for /v1/messages
signal.text: ## Summary - `_merge_guardrails_with_existing` always wrote guardrails to `data["metadata"]`, but routes like `/v1/messages`, `batches`, `files`, and `responses` store proxy-internal state in `data["litellm_metadata"]` while `data["metadata"]` is the provider-facing field (Anthropic expects `metadata.user_id`, etc.). - This caused litellm-internal guardrail names to leak into the Anthropic provider-facing metadata, and when key/team guardrails were already in `litellm_metadata` (written by `move_guardrails_to_metadata`), the model-level guardrails landed in a different bucket: `get_guardrail_from_metadata` checks `metadata` first and returns early, silently shadowing the key/team guardrails in `litellm_metadata`. - Fix: use `get_metadata_variable_name_from_kwargs` to pick the correct bucket. When `litellm_metadata` is present, guardrails are merged there; otherwise behaviour is unchanged for legacy endpoints. - Also read `model_info` from `litellm_metadata` in `_check_and_merge_model_level_guardrails` so the post_call path (`trust_client_model_info=True`) resolves `model_info.id` on `/v1/messages` where the router writes it to `litellm_metadata`. ### Security fix: caller metadata shadowing (veria-ai HIGH on #36085) `get_guardrail_from_metadata` checks `data["metadata"]` before `data["litellm_metadata"]`. On `/v1/messages`, `metadata` is the caller-supplied Anthropic provider-facing field. A caller sending `metadata: {"guardrails": []}` could shadow the admin-authoritative guardrails merged into `litellm_metadata`, silently bypassing all model-level and key/team guardrails. Fix: add `guardrails` and `guardrail_config` to `_UNTRUSTED_METADATA_CONTROL_FIELDS` so they are stripped from both caller-supplied metadata dicts in `add_litellm_data_to_request` before `move_guardrails_to_metadata` and `_check_and_merge_model_level_guardrails` write admin-authoritative values. The top-level `data["guardrails"]` feature (popped by `move_guardrails_to_metadata`) is unaffected: the strip only removes keys from the `metadata`/`litellm_metadata` sub-dicts. Fixes #36085 #### Test plan - [x] 23 existing guardrail merge tests pass (`test_guardrail_merge.py`) - [x] 6 tests covering `/v1/messages` scenario (`test_guardrail_merge_v1_messages.py`): - guardrails merged into `litellm_metadata` when present - guardrails findable by `get_guardrail_from_metadata` after merge - provider-facing `metadata` not modified - existing `litellm_metadata` guardrails preserved and unioned - caller `metadata.guardrails` does not shadow `litellm_metadata` guardrails - caller cannot empty-list bypass guardrails - [x] New strip test in `test_litellm_pre_call_utils.py`: caller-supplied `guardrails` and `guardrail_config` stripped from both `metadata` and `litellm_metadata` - [x] 102 pre-call utils tests pass (guardrail, metadata, strip) - [x] 7 common_request_processing guardrail tests pass

signal.title: feat(spend): add filter_time_by parameter to /spend/logs/v2 for endTime filtering
signal.text: ## TLDR **Problem this solves:** - `/spend/logs/v2` only filters by `startTime`, making long-running requests invisible for billing when scanned by completion time windows - Requests that start at 14:30 and end at 14:34 are lost because they appear with `startTime=14:30` but are scanned at 14:34-14:36 **How it solves it:** - Adds `filter_time_by` parameter with values `startTime` (default) or `endTime` - Existing `start_date`/`end_date` filters apply to the chosen field --- ## User Flow **Before this feature (today):** The billing team tries to collect all completed requests from the last 2 minutes for automated synchronization, but filtering by `startTime` prevents them from finding requests that started earlier and finished in the target window. 1. Every 2 minutes, the system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:30:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:32:00&page=1&page_size=100` 2. It receives `200 OK` with an empty `data` array and `total_count=0`, because the request sent at 14:30 hasn't completed yet and hasn't appeared in logs 3. At 14:32, the system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:32:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:34:00&page=1&page_size=100` 4. It receives `200 OK` with an empty `data` array and `total_count=0`, because the request is still running 5. At 14:34, the request completes. A log entry appears with `startTime=14:30:00` and `endTime=14:34:30`. The system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:34:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:36:00&page=1&page_size=100` 6. It receives `200 OK` with an empty `data` array and `total_count=0` — the request is **NOT FOUND**, because the filter looks for records with `startTime` between 14:34 and 14:36, but this request has `startTime=14:30:00` 7. At 14:36, the system continues scanning, but the request is now lost forever — it never fell into any scanned window 8. 🔧 **Workaround:** The system is forced to scan large ranges, e.g., `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:00:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2015:00:00&page=1&page_size=1000`, fetch thousands of records, and filter by `endTime` locally. This takes minutes, consumes memory, and is unsuitable for automated synchronization **After this feature (ideal user flow):** The billing team can filter requests by their completion time, and all completed requests correctly fall into the right window. 1. Every 2 minutes, the system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:30:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:32:00&filter_time_by=endTime&page=1&page_size=100` 2. It receives `200 OK` with an empty `data` array and `total_count=0`, because the request sent at 14:30 hasn't completed yet 3. At 14:32, the system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:32:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:34:00&filter_time_by=endTime&page=1&page_size=100` 4. It receives `200 OK` with an empty `data` array and `total_count=0`, because the request is still running 5. At 14:34, the request completes. A log entry appears with `startTime=14:30:00` and `endTime=14:34:30`. The system sends `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/v2?start_date=2026-08-12%2014:34:00&end_date=2026-08-12%2014:36:00&filter_time_by=endTime&page=1&page_size=100` 6. It receives `200 OK` with `data` containing the log entry where `endTime=14:34:30` — the request is **FOUND**, because the filter looks for records with `endTime` between 14:34 and 14:36 7. At 14:36, the system continues scanning, and all requests are correctly accounted for in billing regardless of their duration 8. ✅ Automated synchronization runs fast and reliably, financial reports are accurate, and no manual workarounds are needed --- ## Relevant issues Closes #36666 ## Linear ticket *No response* ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Test results ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) *No response* ## QA runbook *No response* ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(vertex): stop re-listing cachedContents on every cache hit
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every cached request re-lists `cachedContents` before generating - That round trip lands on cache hits, the fast path - Reporter measured +1.55s p50, +3.9s p99 over 112 reads How it solves it: - Remembers the resolved cache name per deployment - Trusts it only until Google's own `expireTime` - Falls back to listing whenever the entry cannot be trusted ## User Flow ### Before A developer using Gemini explicit context caching pays a full discovery round trip on every request, including the ones that hit the cache, so caching is slower than it should be exactly when it works. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, marking a large stable prefix with `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` 2. The first response comes back after the proxy creates the cache 3. They send the identical request again 4. The response is correct, but noticeably slower than the cached content should allow — roughly 1.55s slower at p50 and 3.9s at p99 across 112 cache reads 5. Every subsequent identical request pays that same delay, so the cache never delivers its full benefit ### After The same repeated requests return without the extra delay, because a cache the proxy already resolved is not looked up again. 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the same `cache_control` prefix 2. The first response comes back after the proxy creates the cache, as before 3. They send the identical request again 4. The response comes back without the extra discovery delay 5. signal.title: [Feature]: Support GPT-5.6 (Sol / Terra / Luna) via Amazon Bedrock Runtime
signal.text: ### Overview AWS [announced on 2026-08-17](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/amazon-bedrock-cross-region-openai-v2/) that the GPT-5.6 family — Sol, Terra, and Luna — is now available through the **Bedrock Runtime** data plane, distinct from the existing Bedrock Mantle path. LiteLLM currently only has entries for these models under `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}`. There is no equivalent under a `bedrock/` prefix to reach them via Runtime. ### Why this matters Bedrock Runtime introduces two routing modes not available through Mantle: - **Geo (US CRIS)** — routes within a predefined US geography - **Global** — routes across any commercial AWS Region where the model is available, at lower per-token cost and with the highest throughput during demand spikes This addresses a practical capacity limitation with the current Mantle setup: as of 2026-07 GPT-5.6 is only available in us-east-1 / us-east-2, whereas global inference via Runtime removes that constraint. ### Problem Attempting to call these models via the Runtime path today fails. There are no model cost/metadata entries for them under a `bedrock` (non-Mantle) provider, and manually registering a model using the `openai.gpt-5.6-*` IDs produces: ``` BedrockException - {"message":"{\"error\":{\"code\":\"unsupported_parameter\",\"message\":\"Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model.\",\"param\":\"max_tokens\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}"} ``` ### Expected behavior LiteLLM should support invoking `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, and `openai.gpt-5.6-luna` via Amazon Bedrock Runtime, including support for the cross-region global inference endpoints, with correct parameter mapping for these models.

signal.title: [Feature]: Add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search as a native search provider (search_tools / websearch_interception backend)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature ### The Feature Add `bedrock_agentcore` (web search connector) as a first-class LiteLLM **search provider**, so it can be used: - directly via `litellm.search()` / the `/search` endpoint, and - as a backend for the v1.81 **websearch_interception** feature (native `web_search` tool on Bedrock/Azure/Vertex Claude Code & Cowork). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search is a fully managed, MCP-compatible web search connector (GA June 2026). It returns snippets, source URLs, titles, and publication dates — exactly the shape LiteLLM's `SearchResponse` expects. Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-connector-web-search-tool.html ### Motivation, pitch ### Motivation / Pitch Today every LiteLLM search provider (Perplexity, Tavily, Exa, Google PSE, SearXNG, …) is a third-party HTTP API requiring an external API key, and for AWS-hosted users it means search traffic and keys leave AWS. For teams running LiteLLM in front of **Bedrock**, AgentCore Web Search is the natural AWS-native option: - No third-party key — auth is AWS SigV4 via the AgentCore Gateway (IAM). - Search traffic stays within AWS / the account's trust boundary. - Completes the "web search across all providers" story: Claude Code / Claude Desktop (Cowork) on Bedrock could get the native `web_search` interception UX **without** onboarding an external search vendor. There is currently no way to do this via config, because search providers are gated by the hardcoded `SearchProviders` enum + `ProviderConfigManager`. This needs a small core addition. ### Current state (what already exists in the repo) - `litellm/search/main.py` — `search()` / `asearch()` dispatch. - `litellm/llms/base_llm/search/transformation.py` — `BaseSearchConfig` + `SearchResponse{results:[{title,url,snippet,date}]}`. - Example HTTP provider: `litellm/llms/tavily/search/transformation.py`. - Registration points: `SearchProviders` enum (`litellm/types/utils.py`) and `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_search_config` (`litellm/utils.py`). - Interception hook: `litellm/integrations/websearch_interception/handler.py` (already calls `litellm.asearch()` with the configured provider — no change needed if the new provider registers cleanly). - Existing SigV4/MCP machinery to reuse: the AgentCore-hosted MCP SigV4 auth path (`docs/mcp_aws_sigv4`) and Bedrock's SigV4 signer. Note: the existing `bedrock/agentcore/<ARN>` provider is **agent runtimes (InvokeAgentRuntime) / A2A only** — unrelated to the web search connector. ### Proposed implementation The wrinkle vs. other providers: AgentCore Web Search is reached over **MCP (tools/call)** with **SigV4**, not a single plain HTTP POST. Two viable approaches: **Option A — self-contained provider (preferred).** New `litellm/llms/bedrock_agentcore/search/transformation.py` implementing `BaseSearchConfig`, that: - signs a SigV4 request (reuse the existing Bedrock signer + AWS credential chain), - performs the MCP `tools/call` for `WebSearch` against the configured AgentCore Gateway URL, - maps the connector result → `SearchResponse`. Register in `SearchProviders` + `ProviderConfigManager`; add cost-map + `provider_endpoints_support` metadata so it appears in the Search Tools UI. **Option B — bridge to the existing MCP server manager.** Special-case dispatch in `search/main.py` to invoke the WebSearch tool through LiteLLM's MCP client (which already does AgentCore SigV4), then map to `SearchResponse`. Less new protocol code, but more coupling in the core search path. Proposed config UX: search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-search litellm_params: search_provider: bedrock_agentcore gateway_url: https://<gateway-id>.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/mcp aws_region_name: us-east-1 # credentials via standard chain / aws_role_name, mirroring the bedrock provider litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: [bedrock] search_tool_name: agentcore-search ### Are you willing to contribute a PR? Yes — I'd like to author the PR (Option A) and would appreciate a maintainer sanity-check on the preferred approach (A vs B) and the SigV4/MCP helpers to reuse. ### Related - #14011 (web_search tool support, Responses API) - #30822 (websearch_interception tool_choice on Bedrock) - #25191 (interception agentic loop not triggered for Bedrock via /chat/completions) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(streaming): preserve OpenAI SDK usage details in stream chunk builder
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed usage chunks built from raw OpenAI SDK `CompletionUsage` objects silently lose `prompt_tokens_details` and `completion_tokens_details` - Cache-read tokens then fall back to fresh-input pricing and reasoning tokens disappear from usage accounting How it solves it: - Convert raw pydantic usage models to litellm `Usage` at the stream chunk extraction boundary - Add a regression test using the raw `openai.CompletionUsage` shape ## User Flow Before: a developer streams chat completions through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and their cost dashboard never sees cached-token or reasoning-token detail. 1. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true` and `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` 2. The final SSE chunk arrives with `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`, but `prompt_tokens_details` is missing 3. Their cost dashboard bills the full input at the uncached input rate and shows no reasoning-token breakdown After: the same request keeps the provider-reported usage details. 1. They send the same `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true` and `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` 2. The final SSE chunk now carries `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` 3. Their cost dashboard bills cached tokens at the cache-read rate and shows the reasoning-token breakdown ## Relevant issues Related: #34801 (upstream #34812 fixed the generic stream-reassembly path; this covers raw OpenAI SDK pydantic usage shapes that still lost the details). ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix E2E proof against the real DeepSeek API through a litellm proxy, streamed chat completions with `stream_options.include_usage`. Before (v1.97.0-rc.1 without this patch, second call with a shared prefix): ```text call 1: usage=CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=1, prompt_tokens=1462, total_tokens=1463, completion_tokens_details=..., prompt_tokens_details=None) ``` After (same proxy image plus this patch; original capture at commit `96af89842c`, rebased onto `litellm_internal_staging` as `cc845663` with no production code changes): ```text call 0: usage=CompletionUsage(..., completion_tokens_details=..., reasoning_tokens=12, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetails(..., cached_tokens=1664)) call 1: usage=CompletionUsage(..., completion_tokens_details=..., reasoning_tokens=8, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetails(..., cached_tokens=1664)) ``` The regression test also fails on unpatched `litellm_internal_staging`: ```text > assert usage.prompt_tokens == 1714 E assert 0 == 1714 E + where 0 = Usage(..., prompt_tokens_details=None, ...).prompt_tokens ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: in `_extract_usage_chunk()`, convert raw pydantic usage objects (e.g. OpenAI SDK `CompletionUsage`) to litellm `Usage` via `model_dump()` before the chunk builder reads them. - `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: add a regression test using a raw `openai.CompletionUsage` on a stream chunk, asserting `cached_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` survive `calculate_usage()`. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix: include cache_write_tokens in cost calculation for cached-input requests
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #33772 OpenAI models that report **cache-write** tokens (`cache_write_tokens`) were being mis-priced because LiteLLM's cost path only recognized Anthropic's field name (`cache_creation_tokens`). This caused `response_cost` to be **understated** for any request that writes to the prompt cache -- cache-write tokens were billed at the plain input rate (or zero) instead of the correct 1.25x cache-creation rate. The error compounded across **three separate places** in the cost path, all of which are fixed here. ## Root Cause Analysis ### Pricing Model Background OpenAI's prompt caching has two distinct token categories: - **Cache-read tokens** (`cached_tokens`): tokens served from an existing cache entry, priced at a discount (e.g., 0.1x input) - **Cache-write tokens** (`cache_write_tokens`): tokens written to the cache for the first time, priced at a premium (e.g., 1.25x input) Anthropic uses the field name `cache_creation_tokens` for the same concept as OpenAI's `cache_write_tokens`. LiteLLM's cost engine was only reading the Anthropic field name, so OpenAI cache-write tokens were invisible to the pricing logic. ### Place 1: `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` drops `cache_write_tokens` **File:** `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` The function `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` only read `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic's field) from `usage.prompt_tokens_details`. OpenAI reports cache writes under `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (chat completions) / `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (responses API), so the cache-write token count arrived as `0` and those tokens were billed at the plain input rate instead of the 1.25x cache-write rate. ### Place 2: Tiered cache-creation cost keys not registered **Files:** `litellm/utils.py`, `litellm/types/utils.py` `get_model_info` copies a fixed set of cost keys onto `ModelInfoBase`, but omitted: - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_priority` - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_flex` - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_272k_tokens` Even when these keys were defined in the model config, they were silently discarded. The `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict and `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` tuple also lacked these fields. This meant cache-write cost could not vary by service tier (priority/flex) or long-context (>272k) tier. ### Place 3: Responses API usage translation drops the cache-write split **File:** `litellm/responses/utils.py` `ResponseAPILoggingUtils._transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage` builds a `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper` from the Responses API usage but did not map `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` onto the chat-shaped `cache_creation_tokens`. So even after fixing Place 1, requests routed through the Responses API (`/v1/responses`) still lost their cache-write tokens before cost was computed. ## Fix ### Fix 1: Read `cache_write_tokens` with fallback to `cache_creation_tokens` In `_parse_prompt_tokens_details`, the code now reads `cache_write_tokens` first (OpenAI's field), falling back to `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic's field). This ensures cache-write tokens are recognized regardless of which provider reports them. ### Fix 2: Register tiered cache-creation cost keys - Added `cache_creation_input_token_cost_priority`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost_flex`, and `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_272k_tokens` to: - `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` tuple in `litellm/utils.py` - The `ModelInfoBase` constructor call in `get_model_info` - The `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict in `litellm/types/utils.py` This mirrors the existing tiered `cache_read_input_token_cost_*` keys and allows cache-write pricing to vary by service tier and context-length threshold. ### Fix 3: Carry `cache_write_tokens` through Responses API transform In `_transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage`: - **Dict branch**: Maps `cache_write_tokens` -> `cache_creation_tokens` before constructing `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper` - **Object branch**: Reads `cache_write_tokens` via `getattr` and passes it as `cache_creation_tokens` This ensures cost is computed identically regardless of whether a request went through `/chat/completions` or `/responses`. ## Files Changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` | Read `cache_write_tokens` with fallback to `cache_creation_tokens` in `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` | | `litellm/utils.py` | Add tiered cache-creation keys to `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` and `get_model_info` | | `litellm/types/utils.py` | Add tiered cache-creation fields to `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict | | `litellm/responses/utils.py` | Map `cache_write_tokens` -> `cache_creation_tokens` in Responses API usage transform | ## Verification - Existing `cache_read_tokens` pricing is unchanged (the fix only adds a new field read with fallback) - Existing `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic) path is preserved as the fallback - Edge cases handled: if `cache_write_tokens` is `0`, `None`, or missing, the code gracefully falls back to `cache_creation_tokens` or defaults to `0` - The tiered key registration mirrors the existing pattern for `cache_read_input_token_cost_priority` / `_flex` / `_above_272k_tokens` - Both dict and object branches of the Responses API transform are covered ## Impact After this fix, `response_cost` for OpenAI models with prompt caching enabled will correctly reflect: - Cache-write tokens priced at the model's `cache_creation_input_token_cost` rate (typically 1.25x input) - Tiered pricing for priority/flex service tiers and >272k context windows - Consistent pricing across both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` API paths

signal.title: [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment
signal.text: # [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related: #37117 (same root cause in `savings.py`, but scoped there to *multiple deployments per `model_name` + `cost-based-routing`*). Filing separately because the trigger is much broader — a **single deployment with default routing** is enough — and because there is an additional key-shadowing behaviour that constrains the fix. Also related: #35693 (same `shared_backend_model_info()` stripping, surfaced as an unsuppressible cache-cost warning). ## What happened? The Cost Optimization dashboard reports **"$0.00" next to a perfectly correct non-zero "N tokens compressed"**. In our case: `2,642,007 tokens compressed`, `compression_savings_spend = $0.00`, while real `spend` for the same rollup row was `$11.71`. The trigger is not multi-deployment routing. It is simply: > the deployment carries operator-supplied custom pricing **and** the model is not in LiteLLM's built-in cost map — i.e. **any self-hosted / custom model**. Chain of events for a single deployment: 1. `Router._create_deployment()` registers the deployment's pricing under **two** keys: - the deployment UUID -> full pricing retained - `{provider}/{model}` -> passed through `shared_backend_model_info()`, which **strips every pricing field** 2. The **public `model_name`** — the value the spend log records, and therefore the only thing `compute_savings_spend()` receives — is **never registered with pricing at all**. 3. `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` calls `litellm.get_model_info(model=<public name>, custom_llm_provider=...)`, which raises `"This model isn't mapped yet"` for a custom model. 4. That raise is caught and the helper "falls open" to `(0.0, 0.0)`. 5. `compression = saved_tokens * 0.0 == 0.0`. Billing (`spend`) is unaffected, because response-cost calculation reads the deployment object directly instead of going through `litellm.model_cost`. Only the savings columns break, which is why the token count and the dollar figure disagree. ## Relevant log output ``` get_model_info('muse-glimmer-30b','openai') -> Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=muse-glimmer-30b, custom_llm_provider=openai _input_and_cache_read_cost('muse-glimmer-30b','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) ``` DB rollup row (`LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend`) showing the contradiction: ``` date=2026-08-18 model=muse-glimmer-30b custom_llm_provider=openai prompt_tokens = 31,274,060 spend = 11.7122 <-- billing works compression_saved_tokens = 2,642,007 <-- correct compression_savings_spend = 0.0 <-- should be ~$0.9247 api_requests = 2,287 ``` The per-request guardrail metadata is recorded correctly, so nothing is wrong upstream of pricing: ```json {"guardrail_name": "headroom-compression", "guardrail_provider": "headroom", "guardrail_status": "success", "guardrail_response": {"tokens_before": 49323, "tokens_after": 49206, "tokens_saved": 117}} ``` ## Steps to Reproduce Minimal config — **one** deployment, no `router_settings`, no `cost-based-routing`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: muse-glimmer-30b litellm_params: model: muse-glimmer-30b custom_llm_provider: openai api_base: https://your-self-hosted-endpoint/v1 api_key: os.environ/MY_TOKEN input_cost_per_token: 3.5e-07 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-06 guardrails: - guardrail_name: headroom-compression litellm_params: guardrail: headroom mode: pre_call api_base: http://headroom-proxy:8787 default_on: true ``` Send traffic through it, then read `/user/daily/activity` (or the Cost Optimization tile): `total_compression_saved_tokens` climbs, `total_compression_savings_spend` stays `0.0`. Reproduced directly in the running container, replaying what `Router` does for that single deployment: ```python import litellm from litellm.router import shared_backend_model_info from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import _input_and_cache_read_cost PRICE = {"input_cost_per_token": 3.5e-07, "output_cost_per_token": 1.5e-06, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 3.5e-07} full = dict(PRICE, id="dep-solo") litellm.register_model(model_cost={"dep-solo": full}) litellm.register_model(model_cost={"openai/solo-model": shared_backend_model_info(full)}) print(litellm.model_cost["dep-solo"]["input_cost_per_token"]) # 3.5e-07 print(litellm.model_cost["openai/solo-model"]["input_cost_per_token"]) # None print(litellm.model_cost.get("solo-model")) # None print(_input_and_cache_read_cost("solo-model", "openai")) # (0.0, 0.0) ``` Output: ``` model_cost['dep-solo'].input = 3.5e-07 model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input = None model_cost['solo-model'] = None LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) ``` ### Second finding: the provider-prefixed key shadows the public name Important for whichever fix is chosen. `get_model_info()` prefers the combined `{provider}/{model}` key, and `Router` has already created that key *without* pricing. So registering pricing under the bare public name is **not** sufficient: ``` after pricing bare 'solo-model': model_cost['solo-model'].input = 3.5e-07 model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input = None LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (0.0, 0.0) <-- STILL ZERO after also pricing 'openai/solo-model': LOOKUP('solo-model','openai') = (3.5e-07, 3.5e-07) <-- fixed ``` ## What did you expect to happen? `compression_savings_spend` / `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should price saved tokens at the deployment's configured input rate whenever that rate is known — which it demonstrably is, since ordinary `spend` is calculated correctly from the same deployment. Expected for the row above: `2,642,007 x 3.5e-07 = $0.9247`. At minimum, savings should never silently render `$0.00` beside a non-zero token count; that reads as "compression achieved nothing" rather than "pricing lookup failed". ## Suggested fix Preferred: make the savings path deployment-aware rather than name-aware, so key shadowing is irrelevant. **Option C** (in addition to Options A/B in #37117): have `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` consult `Router.get_deployment_model_info(model_id, model)` before falling back to `get_model_info()`. `savings.py` already imports `Router` for the autorouter baseline and `_effective_model_info()` already performs deployment-aware resolution, so most of the plumbing exists. Two smaller points regardless of approach: 1. Any cost-map-repair fix must also write the `{provider}/{model}` key, or stop `shared_backend_model_info()` from stripping pricing when a single deployment owns that key (cf. #35693). 2. Consider distinguishing "priced at zero" from "price unknown". The current fall-open to `(0.0, 0.0)` turns a lookup failure into a confident `$0.00`; a debug log exists but nothing surfaces to the operator. `compression_savings_spend` is written with `increment`, so historical rows will remain `$0.00` after a fix and need a separate backfill. ## Workaround A `CustomLogger` registered via `litellm_settings.callbacks` that mirrors each deployment's pricing (read back from `litellm.model_cost[<deployment id>]`) onto both the public `model_name` and the `{provider}/{model}` key, re-synced on an interval to catch DB/UI-added deployments. It invents no prices: deployments without custom pricing are skipped, so nothing is over-reported. Verified end-to-end against the live proxy after deploying it: ``` delta saved_tokens = 734 delta saved_usd = 0.000256900 expected (734 x 3.5e-07) = 0.000256900 MATCH /user/daily/activity -> total_compression_savings_spend = 0.00113715 (was 0.0) ``` Also confirmed to survive a pod restart (860 saved tokens -> $0.000301, exact match). ## Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.2 (also verified present in v1.97.0) ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: compression_savings_spend and prompt_caching_savings_spend always $0 with cost-based-routing and multiple deployments per model_name
signal.text: # [Bug]: `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` always $0 when using `cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments per model_name ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? When using `routing_strategy: cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments sharing the same `model_name` (each at a different provider/price point), the daily spend rollup fields `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` are always recorded as `$0.00`, even though compression is actively removing tokens from requests. The root cause is that `compute_savings_spend()` in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/savings.py` calls `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` which uses `litellm.get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider)` to look up the model's pricing. But for multi-deployment setups the backend model name (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider="openrouter"`) is **not** in `litellm.model_cost` — because `shared_backend_model_info()` in `litellm/types/utils.py` explicitly strips all pricing fields from the shared backend key: ```python SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS = frozenset( ModelInfoBase.__required_keys__ | ModelInfoBase.__optional_keys__ ) - frozenset(CustomPricingLiteLLMParams.model_fields) # <-- removes ALL cost fields def shared_backend_model_info(model_info: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]: return {k: v for k, v in model_info.items() if k in SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS} ``` So when `_create_deployment()` registers the shared backend key: ```python _backend_alias_cost = {_model_name: _shared_model_info} litellm.register_model(model_cost=_backend_alias_cost) ``` The registered entry contains only `{"litellm_provider": "openrouter", "mode": "chat"}` — no pricing. Subsequent `get_model_info()` calls for that model+provider combination fail with "This model isn't mapped yet", and `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` gracefully returns `(0.0, 0.0)`. The per-deployment pricing IS correctly stored under the deployment's unique `model_info.id` hash, but `compute_savings_spend()` never looks it up by that ID — it only has `model` and `custom_llm_provider` available from the spend log payload. ## What did you expect to happen? `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should reflect the actual dollar savings using the deployment's configured pricing, even when multiple deployments share a `model_name` with different prices. ## Steps to Reproduce **Config (minimal):** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.0000004225 output_cost_per_token: 0.000000845 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000035 - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openai/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/ZEN_API_KEY api_base: https://example.com/zen input_cost_per_token: 0.00000174 output_cost_per_token: 0.00000384 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000174 router_settings: routing_strategy: cost-based-routing ``` Two deployments, same `model_name`, different providers and prices. Cost-based-routing picks the cheaper OpenRouter deployment. The spend log records `model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider=openrouter`. **Verification inside the running container:** ```python import litellm # The shared backend key has NO pricing: print(litellm.model_cost.get("openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro")) # → None (not registered at all, because shared_backend_model_info stripped the cost fields) # get_model_info fails for the backend model+provider combo: litellm.get_model_info(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter") # → raises: "This model isn't mapped yet" # So compute_savings_spend returns (0.0, 0.0): from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import compute_savings_spend result = compute_savings_spend( model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter", compression_saved_tokens=100000, cache_read_input_tokens=500000, ) print(result) # SavingsSpend(compression=0.0, prompt_caching=0.0) # Expected: SavingsSpend(compression=0.04225, prompt_caching=0.000203625) # (100k * $0.4225/M = $0.04225 compression, 500k * ($0.4225 - $0.035)/M = $0.000203625 caching) ``` **Observable effect:** - Headroom `/stats` endpoint shows compression is actively working (6.7M tokens removed across 457 requests) - But `/user/daily/activity` shows `compression_savings_spend: 0.0` for all days after switching to multi-deployment cost-based routing **Before/After comparison from our daily activity data:** ``` 2026-08-11 saved_tokens=430430 comp_savings_spend=$0.09 ← single deployment per model_name 2026-08-12 saved_tokens=2256791 comp_savings_spend=$2.34 ← last day with old config 2026-08-13 saved_tokens=0 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← switched to multi-deployment 2026-08-14 saved_tokens=3939121 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← compression works, pricing broken 2026-08-16 saved_tokens=543419 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ``` ## Suggested fix `compute_savings_spend()` receives the `model` and `custom_llm_provider` from the spend log payload but not the `router_model_id` (deployment ID). Two possible approaches: **Option A (minimal):** Thread the deployment's `model_info.id` into `compute_savings_spend()` and look up pricing via `litellm.model_cost[model_info_id]` first, falling back to `get_model_info()` only when the ID lookup misses. **Option B (more robust):** Thread the deployment's actual `input_cost_per_token` / `cache_read_input_token_cost` values directly into `compute_savings_spend()` from `litellm_params` / `metadata.model_info`, similar to how `custom_cost_per_token` is already passed in the response-cost path. This removes the dependency on the global `litellm.model_cost` dict entirely for savings calculation. ## Relevant log output No errors are logged — `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` catches the exception from `get_model_info()` and degrades silently: ```python except Exception as e: verbose_proxy_logger.debug( "savings: no model info for provider=%s model=%s (%s)", custom_llm_provider, model, e ) return 0.0, 0.0 ``` Setting `LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG` surfaces: ``` savings: no model info for provider=openrouter model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (This model isn't mapped yet...) ``` ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy, Cost Tracking ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.95.0 (Docker image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0`)

signal.title: [Bug]: generic_cost_per_token double-counts overlapping cached image tokens
signal.text: ### What happened? `generic_cost_per_token()` can overcharge multimodal requests when `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` are overlapping subsets of `prompt_tokens`. Some OpenAI-compatible providers report usage with these semantics: - `prompt_tokens`: total input tokens across all modalities - `cached_tokens`: the subset of total input read from cache - `image_tokens`: the subset of total input attributable to images `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` are therefore not guaranteed to be disjoint. ### Minimal synthetic reproduction Assume a model with no explicit `input_cost_per_image_token`, so image tokens use the ordinary input rate: ```python usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=10, total_tokens=110, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetailsWrapper( text_tokens=None, cached_tokens=90, image_tokens=80, ), ) model_info = { "input_cost_per_token": 1e-6, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 1e-7, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-6, } ``` With overlapping dimensions, the expected price is: ```text uncached input = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens = 10 prompt cost = 10 * 1e-6 + 90 * 1e-7 = 19e-6 output cost = 10 * 2e-6 = 20e-6 total = 39e-6 ``` Current `main` computes: ```text text_tokens = max(100 - 90 - 80, 0) = 0 prompt cost = 90 * 1e-7 + 80 * 1e-6 = 89e-6 output cost = 20e-6 total = 109e-6 ``` The 70 overlapping image/cache tokens are charged once at the cache rate and again at the full input rate. ### Root cause The generic calculator detects overlapping token details, then calculates text as the remainder: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py#L841-L861 It later prices both cached tokens and image tokens independently: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py#L654-L671 This assumes cache and modality details are mutually exclusive buckets. ### Related upstream work - #18750 and merged PR #18768 already handle the same semantic issue for Gemini by reading `cacheTokensDetails` and subtracting cached tokens per modality. - Merged PR #19772 fixes the case where `text_tokens` includes cached tokens, but its generic remainder calculation does not resolve cache/image intersection when only aggregate cache tokens are available. ### Expected behavior Each input token should be billed exactly once. - If a provider supplies cached-token counts per modality, normalize text/image/audio into uncached modality buckets before generic pricing. - If only aggregate `cached_tokens` and aggregate modality totals are available, the generic calculator should not assume they are disjoint. - For models where image tokens are included in `prompt_tokens` and use the same input rate, pricing should use `(prompt_tokens - cached_tokens) * input_rate + cached_tokens * cache_rate`. - Models with a distinct image rate need an explicit provider/model semantic or a per-modality cache breakdown; aggregate overlapping fields are insufficient to derive exact buckets. OpenAI documents that images count as input tokens and can participate in prompt caching: - https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision - https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching ### Impact Incorrect `response_cost` / `raw_spend` propagates to spend logs, budgets, alerts, chargeback, and billing reconciliation for affected OpenAI-compatible multimodal providers. ### Version Reproduced against upstream `main` at commit `bc6e7df05b018eefe6c7293790ca3f4de38709ac`. ### Data note All token counts and prices in this report are synthetic. No production request, customer, endpoint, credential, or billing data is included.

signal.title: [Feature]: Derive a stable session id for chatgpt/ models when the client sends none, so multi-turn conversations hit the upstream prompt cache
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (Closest found: #29978, which maps Codex session metadata into observability fields, and the Vertex Anthropic session-affinity work in #31898; neither derives a session id when the client sends none) ### The Feature When a request to a chatgpt/ model arrives with no session identifier, derive a deterministic one from the conversation's stable prefix (for example a hash of the system prompt plus the first user message) instead of generating a random one per request. The same conversation then maps to the same upstream cache shard on every turn, so the backend serves the resent history from its prompt cache. Clients that already send a session id keep full control; the derivation only fills the gap for clients that cannot be changed The upstream capability already exists and already works through LiteLLM when the caller passes `litellm_session_id` explicitly; the transcript below shows ~91% of input tokens served from cache on a repeat call with it, and 0% without it. The missing piece is only the default when nothing is passed: today that default is a fresh random id per request, which guarantees a cache miss on every turn of a multi-turn conversation ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a Claude Code user routing requests to a chatgpt/ model through the proxy burns subscription quota reprocessing the full conversation every turn, because each request lands on a fresh prompt-cache shard 1. They configure a model_name mapping to chatgpt/gpt-5.4 and point Claude Code at the proxy 2. Each agent turn sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the full conversation history; Claude Code sends no session identifier 3. Every response reports cached input tokens at or near zero, even though each turn resends an identical prefix that is tens or hundreds of thousands of tokens 4. Weekly subscription quota drains several times faster than the same conversation in the native client; the workaround they live with is an out-of-tree proxy hook that injects a deterministic session id hashed from the conversation prefix, which restores roughly 90 percent cached input but has to be re-verified on every LiteLLM upgrade After this feature (ideal user flow): the same conversation hits the upstream prompt cache with no client or hook changes 1. They configure the same model_name mapping and point Claude Code at the proxy 2. Each agent turn sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with no session identifier 3. The proxy derives the same conversation-stable session id turn after turn, and responses report most of the input as cached 4. Quota consumption tracks new tokens instead of full-history reprocessing ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: codex litellm_params: model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 ``` Proxy: `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000`, ChatGPT device-code auth cached under `~/.config/litellm/chatgpt/` Version or commit: stock `litellm_internal_staging` at 973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e Two request bodies were generated, each with a different deterministic ~6.4K-token filler document (different between runs so the second run starts from a cold cache and cannot ride anything the first warmed). Run A sends the identical body twice with no session field; Run B sends its identical body twice with `"litellm_session_id": "stable-demo-1"` added ```bash curl -sS -D a1.headers -o a1.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_a.json curl -sS -D a2.headers -o a2.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_a.json curl -sS -D b1.headers -o b1.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_b.json curl -sS -D b2.headers -o b2.body http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @run_b.json ``` All four calls returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Usage extracted from each response's `response.completed` event (the provider returns the body as SSE), verbatim: ``` a1.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 26, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6471} a2.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 24, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6469} b1.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 26, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6471} b2.body -> {"input_tokens": 6445, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 5888, "cache_write_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 24, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 6469} ``` What stopped me there: with no session field, the byte-identical repeat call (a2) reports `cached_tokens: 0`; there is nothing a client like Claude Code can set without modification, and nothing in proxy config changes the default. Passing `litellm_session_id` explicitly makes the repeat call (b2) report 5888 of 6445 input tokens cached (~91%), which shows the upstream path is already functional and only the no-id default is missing ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details https://linkedin.com/in/dkrisman

signal.title: fix(anthropic): preserve model output limit with reasoning
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Anthropic reasoning silently lowers the model output limit - Length stops lose their Responses API reason How it solves it: - Preserve Anthropic's model-aware limit when callers omit one - Map completion stop reasons into incomplete response details ## User Flow Before: a developer runs a tool-heavy Anthropic Responses turn and receives no final answer 1. They send POST https://litellm.example/v1/responses with Claude Haiku 4.5 and low reasoning 2. They omit `max_output_tokens` and allow the model to call tools 3. The response stops after an implicit 5,120-token limit with no useful incomplete reason After: the same turn retains the model limit and completes with a final answer 1. They send POST https://litellm.example/v1/responses with Claude Haiku 4.5 and low reasoning 2. They omit `max_output_tokens` and allow the model to call tools 3. Anthropic receives its 64,000-token model limit and the response completes normally 4. A genuine length stop reports `incomplete_details.reason` as `max_output_tokens` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (fac1a18c0a) 1. Sovara ran its real Claude Haiku 4.5 compatibility workflow with low reasoning and application tools 2. signal.title: fix(proxy): keep org admins' team memberships in other orgs visible
signal.text: ## Relevant issues <!-- e.g., "Fixes #000" --> Regression introduced by #25904. ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-3723 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a team-management / RBAC fix on `GET /team/list` and `GET /v2/team/list` — no inference is involved, so the end-to-end proof is at the HTTP level against the endpoints (real proxy + Postgres, no mocks). **Scenario:** `user-x` is **org admin of org-A** and a **plain member of org-B**. `team-1` ∈ org-A (user-x admin), `team-2` ∈ org-B (user-x admin), `team-3` ∈ org-A (user-x **not** a member). `user-x2` has the same memberships but is **not** an org admin (control); `user-y` is a member of team-2 and team-3 (cross-user boundary target). Each user lists teams with their own key (`user_id == caller`); check **C** has user-x query user-y. ```bash # self-query as user-x curl -s "http://localhost:4000/v2/team/list?user_id=user-x" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_X_KEY" | jq '[.teams[].team_alias] | sort' curl -s "http://localhost:4000/team/list?user_id=user-x" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_X_KEY" | jq '[.[].team_alias] | sort' ``` Teams are created with a unique per-run prefix (`<prefix>-team-1`, etc.) so repeated runs against the same DB don't collide — the prefix is cosmetic. The `A` / `B` / `C` labels below are static scenario tags printed by the harness regardless of outcome. **Before the fix** — `team-2` (org-B) is dropped from user-x's own view (the bug); control and boundary are as expected: ``` === A. user-x (org admin of A) self-query === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-1"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-1","lit3723-1782752637-team-3"] === B. CONTROL — user-x2 (same teams, NOT org admin) self-query === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-1","lit3723-1782752637-team-2"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-1","lit3723-1782752637-team-2"] === C. BOUNDARY — user-x queries user-y === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-3"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782752637-team-3"] ``` `A` drops `team-2` on both endpoints; `B` (identical memberships, no org-admin role) sees both teams — confirming the org-admin role is the trigger. **After the fix** — user-x sees every team they belong to; control unchanged; boundary still never leaks `team-2`: ``` === A. user-x (org admin of A) self-query === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-1","lit3723-1782755216-team-2"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-1","lit3723-1782755216-team-2","lit3723-1782755216-team-3"] === B. CONTROL — user-x2 (same teams, NOT org admin) self-query === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-1","lit3723-1782755216-team-2"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-1","lit3723-1782755216-team-2"] === C. BOUNDARY — user-x queries user-y === v1 /team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-3"] v2 /v2/team/list : ["lit3723-1782755216-team-3"] ``` `A` now returns `team-2` on both endpoints (bug fixed); `B` is unchanged (the change only touches the org-admin path); `C` still returns only org-A teams, never `team-2` — the cross-user org boundary from #25904 is preserved. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Changes A user who is an org admin of at least one organization stopped seeing teams they belong to in *other* organizations where they are only a member or team admin. Both `GET /team/list` and `GET /v2/team/list` scoped the caller's teams to the organizations they administer, dropping their own memberships elsewhere. The UI sidebar and Teams page always issue a self-query (`user_id == caller`), so they rendered an incomplete list. Root cause: #25904 changed the org-admin scoping in both endpoints from a **union** (the admin's org teams ∪ the caller's own member teams) into an **intersection** (org teams ∩ memberships), and applied that clamp even to a self-query. The intent of #25904 — preventing an org admin from enumerating *another* user's teams across org boundaries — is correct, but it should not clamp the caller's view of their own memberships. The fix is strictly additive — only the self/bare org-admin query changes, and no team that is currently returned is removed: - `_enforce_list_team_v2_access` returns a `union_org_admin_membership` flag for a self/bare org-admin query and keeps `user_id = caller` (instead of nulling it) so the where-builder can look up the caller's memberships. - `_build_team_list_where_conditions` emits `OR(teams in my orgs, teams I'm a member of)` for that case instead of the ANDed intersection. It is gated off when an explicit `organization_id` filter is supplied and for the deleted-teams path. An org admin with no memberships still sees their org teams. - `_authorize_and_filter_teams` (v1 `/team/list`) returns the caller's full membership list across all orgs for a self-query. - **Cross-user org-admin queries are unchanged** — they keep the org-boundary intersection from #25904, so an org admin still cannot list another user's teams outside their orgs. Tests: new `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_list_org_admin_scope.py` (12 self-contained cases) covering the where-builder union vs. intersection, an org admin with no memberships still seeing org teams, `search` co-existing with the union, the v2 access gate's flag and its 401/403 boundary gates, and the v1 self-query-union vs. cross-user-intersection vs. bare paths. Existing `test_org_admin_team_access.py` stays green.

signal.title: fix(caching): guard RedisCache.disconnect against None connection pool in cluster mode
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - In Redis cluster mode, the proxy raises an unhandled AttributeError on every shutdown, aborting cleanup before the JWT handler close, DB writer close, billing metrics flush, and langfuse flush run How it solves it: - Guards the None connection pool dereference in RedisCache.disconnect(), gives RedisClusterCache its own disconnect() that tears down the cluster client, and wraps the shutdown-path cache disconnect call in try/except so a cache teardown failure can't cascade into skipping the rest of shutdown ## User Flow Anyone running the proxy against a cluster-mode Redis (any deployment using REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES or startup_nodes, including managed offerings that are always cluster-mode) currently sees shutdown fail with an AttributeError on every restart, and with it, up to one export interval of billing data plus the final langfuse flush silently dropped. After this fix, shutdown completes cleanly. ## Relevant issues Fixes #37137 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I could not exercise this against a live Redis Cluster instance in this environment (no cluster-mode Redis available, and the bug is specifically in a shutdown code path rather than a request-serving one, so there is no useful curl against a running proxy to demonstrate it). Instead, added regression tests in tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py and tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cluster_cache.py that reproduce the exact failure: constructing a cache with async_redis_conn_pool None (the cluster-mode condition) and calling disconnect() raised AttributeError before this change and passes after it. Ran locally with pytest and confirmed all three new tests fail on the pre-fix code and pass on the post-fix code. If a maintainer can point me to a way to spin up a cluster-mode Redis in this environment, or can verify it against one in review, that would close the gap this test-only verification leaves. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Changes - litellm/caching/redis_cache.py: RedisCache.disconnect() now checks async_redis_conn_pool is not None before calling disconnect on it - litellm/caching/redis_cluster_cache.py: RedisClusterCache now overrides disconnect() to close redis_async_redis_cluster_client via aclose() before delegating to the base class - litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py: proxy_shutdown_event() now wraps the litellm.cache.disconnect() call in try/except so a cache teardown failure can't skip the jwt handler close, db writer close, billing metrics flush, and langfuse flush that follow it - tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py: added a regression test for disconnect() with no connection pool - tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cluster_cache.py: added regression tests for RedisClusterCache.disconnect() both with and without an initialized cluster client ## QA runbook 1. Point the proxy at a cluster-mode Redis (REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES set, or any deployment that is always cluster-mode) 2. Start the proxy, then send SIGTERM 3. Before this fix: shutdown log shows an unhandled AttributeError and skips the steps after cache disconnect. After this fix: shutdown completes and logs proceed through JWT handler close, DB writer close, billing flush, and langfuse flush ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): update VerificationToken.spend when SpendLogs record key spend
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #37144 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes SpendLogs can persist `api_key` from `standard_logging_object.metadata.user_api_key_hash` even when the cost-callback `token` / `metadata.user_api_key` is missing (user/team ids still trigger spend tracking). Key spend previously used only the `token` argument, so `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` stayed 0 while SpendLogs accumulated. - Resolve the hashed key for `_update_key_db` from the SpendLogs payload `api_key` when `token` is missing. - In the cost callback, fall back to `standard_logging_object.metadata.user_api_key_hash` so `update_database` and spend counters receive the same key. ## Tests - Successful logged spend increments `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` when `token` is provided. - Successful logged spend increments `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` for the SpendLogs `api_key` when `token` is None and the standard logging payload has `user_api_key_hash`. - Cost callback passes that hash as `token` when `metadata.user_api_key` is missing.

signal.title: [Bug]: LangSmith tracing 400s with "trace_id does not match first part of dotted_order"
signal.text:
## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (#7140 is the closest but covers child-run `dotted_order` with a `parent_run_id`. This is a root-run `trace_id != run_id` mismatch, no parent involved.) ## What happened? With LangSmith tracing enabled in the proxy config, requests that carry a session/trace header have every run batch rejected by LangSmith with a 400. No trace for those requests lands in LangSmith. Plain requests without such a header land fine. Langfuse (enabled side by side) works throughout. Likely cause: `_ensure_required_ids` in `litellm/integrations/langsmith.py` mints a fresh `run_id` when the request has no `id`, but only defaults `trace_id` to `run_id` when `trace_id` is *also* missing. When a request carries one of the headers LiteLLM maps to `metadata["trace_id"]`, the proxy honors it while generating a new `run_id`. For a root run LangSmith requires `trace_id == run_id`, so the payload is rejected. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/ef84494d52c6708e4e9f4a54ce551a265995ad8f/litellm/integrations/langsmith.py#L170-L181 `metadata["trace_id"]` is derived from headers in `get_chain_id_from_headers` (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`), which accepts `x-litellm-trace-id`, `x-litellm-session-id`, and any `x--session-id` header whose value looks like a session id. That last rule is what makes this hit real users without them ever setting a `trace_id` - for example, Claude Code through ngrok sends a constant `x-claude-code-session-id` for the whole session, so every run in the session carries the same `trace_id` while each gets a fresh `run_id`. ## User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer who turns on LangSmith tracing in the proxy gets no traces in LangSmith for requests that carry a session id header. 1. They set the LangSmith API key and project in the proxy environment, enable LangSmith tracing in the proxy config, and start the proxy. 2. They send `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with a model name and a message, their client (e.g. Claude Code) attaching a session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200 with the completion content. 4. They open their LangSmith project. No trace appears for that request. 5. The proxy log shows LangSmith's API rejecting the run with a 400. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request produces a trace in LangSmith. 1. Same proxy config and LangSmith keys. 2. Same `POST https:///v1/chat/completions` with the same model, message, and session id header. 3. The proxy returns a 200. 4. A trace for that request appears in the LangSmith project, and the proxy log shows no 400. ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml # litellm-config.yaml (excerpt) litellm_settings: success_callback: ["langfuse", "langsmith"] ``` Env vars set on the proxy: `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`, `LANGSMITH_PROJECT`, `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL` (values redacted; `LANGSMITH_BASE_URL=https://apac.api.smith.langchain.com`). Version or commit: `v1.97.0` (image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`). The `_ensure_required_ids` logic is byte-identical in `v1.96.2`. Commands and their full output: All three LLM endpoints are affected. Each was sent with its own `x-litellm-trace-id` so the runs can be told apart, and each returned 200 to the caller before LangSmith rejected the run on the next batch flush.
POST /v1/chat/completions - command and 400 ```bash podman compose up -d curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 does not match first part of dotted_order a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 for run_id:a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 trace_id:3097ec42-c4f6-4634-b481-15d7bf99f792 dotted_order:20260818T100130082650Za0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/messages - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id 7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a does not match first part of dotted_order 4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 for run_id:4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 trace_id:7a92dd42-656b-4665-a3e6-fb618b035a2a dotted_order:20260818T102348430265Z4c364ee4-212c-4a57-a763-ee37495b3a78 parent_run_id:"} ```
POST /v1/responses - command and 400 ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-litellm-trace-id: bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","input":"hi"}' ``` ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: langsmith.py:432 - Langsmith HTTP Error: 400 - {"error":"Bad request: invalid 'dotted_order': trace_id bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 does not match first part of dotted_order 6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a for run_id:6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a trace_id:bf259ae6-936a-497d-ac6f-f9588f7c6540 dotted_order:20260818T102443557144Z6b5e4199-e9ee-47c8-ac5c-cb24e58f2a5a parent_run_id:"} ```
The same request without the `x-litellm-trace-id` header lands cleanly on every one of those endpoints. Shown here for `/v1/chat/completions`, verified against the LangSmith API:
Headerless control - the run lands, id == trace_id ```bash # headerless request curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # resolve the project to its session id curl -s "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/sessions?name=$LANGSMITH_PROJECT&limit=1" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" | jq -r '.[0].id' # # the headerless run is present: id == trace_id, success, no error curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"]}' \ | jq -r '.runs[] | [.id, .trace_id, .status, .error, .dotted_order]' # ["7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa","success",null,"20260818T100034808837Z7d6658d2-e861-42c6-98b1-d0937e3f9cfa"] # the run_id from the /v1/chat/completions 400 above never lands - no run exists for it curl -s -X POST "$LANGSMITH_BASE_URL/api/v1/runs/query" \ -H "x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":["a0af48ee-e01a-4d99-9f06-b0685b3f5ec0"]}' | jq -r '.runs | length' # 0 ```
Only requests carrying one of the session/trace headers trip the 400. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? `v1.97.0` ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _(optional, leave blank)_

signal.title: fix(realtime): honor explicit api_key/api_base in realtime calls
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Realtime calls dropped the api_key resolved from a named credential - `/v1/realtime` failed with "api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls" How it solves it: - `_arealtime` now honors its explicit `api_key`/`api_base` arguments - Same precedence fix applied to the Azure branch ## Relevant issues Fixes #36066 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Credential resolution already worked: `load_credentials_from_list` hydrates `api_key` from `litellm_credential_name` into kwargs, which reaches `_arealtime` as its explicit `api_key` parameter. The provider branches then ignored that parameter and only looked at `dynamic_api_key`, the globals, and the env var, so with no `OPENAI_API_KEY` set the key ended up `None` and the handler raised Proxy run with a credential-only key, `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset. Note that this environment has no egress to api.openai.com, so the credential points at a local realtime websocket server that prints the Authorization header it receives; that is enough to show which key the proxy forwards upstream config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-rt litellm_params: model: gpt-4o-realtime-preview custom_llm_provider: openai litellm_credential_name: openai-secret credential_list: - credential_name: openai-secret credential_values: api_key: sk-credential-key-123 api_base: http://localhost:8799 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` before, at 24dbd2b2db: ``` $ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config rt_config.yaml --port 4002 $ python rt_client.py # websockets.connect("ws://localhost:4002/v1/realtime?model=my-rt") websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError: received 1011 (internal error) Internal server error # proxy log: raise ValueError("api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls") ValueError: api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls ``` after, at 63b2eca39b: ``` $ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config rt_config.yaml --port 4001 $ python rt_client.py CLIENT RECEIVED: {"type": "session.created", "session": {"id": "sess_stub", "model": "gpt-4o-realtime-preview"}} # upstream log: UPSTREAM SAW Authorization: Bearer sk-credential-key-123 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/realtime_api/main.py` adds the explicit `api_key` and `api_base` arguments to the precedence chain in the openai and azure branches, right after the `dynamic_*` values from `get_llm_provider`, so an explicitly passed key wins over globals and env vars instead of being discarded `tests/test_litellm/realtime_api/test_main.py` gets two regression tests driving `_arealtime` with an explicit key and no globals or env vars, asserting the provider handler receives it. Both fail on the parent commit ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(streaming): preserve usage in OpenAI SDK chunks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Usage-only and final SDK chunks follow distinct paths - Final SDK chunks overwrite provider usage during assembly How it solves it: - Retain usage-only chunk normalization - Normalize final SDK usage before stream assembly ## User Flow Before: a developer streams an OpenRouter completion and records incorrect usage 1. They send `POST https://proxy.example/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "openai/z-ai/glm-5.2"`, `"stream": true`, and `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` 2. The provider completes successfully, but the assembled stream reports estimated prompt tokens and zero completion tokens 3. Their usage tracker records `12` total tokens and no cached-token count instead of the provider totals After: the same developer records the provider-reported usage from that stream 1. They send the same `POST https://proxy.example/v1/chat/completions` request 2. The provider completes successfully and the assembled stream retains its usage fields 3. Their usage tracker records `17` prompt, `4` completion, `21` total, cached-token, and reasoning-token details ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: export `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and, if required, `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY`. At each commit, run: ```sh PYTHONPATH=litellm uv run python - <<'PY' import os import litellm messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: ok"}] response = litellm.completion( model="openai/z-ai/glm-5.2", api_base="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", api_key=os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"], messages=messages, max_tokens=4, stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}, ) assembled = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=list(response), messages=messages) print({ "prompt_tokens": assembled.usage.prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": assembled.usage.completion_tokens, "total_tokens": assembled.usage.total_tokens, "cached_tokens": getattr(assembled.usage.prompt_tokens_details, "cached_tokens", None), "reasoning_tokens": getattr(assembled.usage.completion_tokens_details, "reasoning_tokens", None), }) PY ``` ### Before (901b08f524) 1. Run the shared stream request from this commit with `stream_options={"include_usage": True}` 2. Observed output: `{'prompt_tokens': 12, 'completion_tokens': 0, 'total_tokens': 12, 'cached_tokens': None, 'reasoning_tokens': 4}` ### After (678e89fc2e) 1. Run the identical shared stream request from this commit with `stream_options={"include_usage": True}` 2.
